# ADR 0049 — Full-residual input is the codec default

- **Status:** Accepted (owner directive 2026-06-10: "Switch to full detail bands as default. L3 approx is basically impossible to do anything serious like 63-525:1 CR with 5-20 PRD and R above 0.9.")
- **Extends:** ADR 0009/0031 (L3-approx-input quality ceiling), ADR 0033 (joint pipeline), ADR 0045 (latent is the wire). Relates ADR 0035/0036 (two-tier deploy), 0046 (broker).

## Context

The neural codec compressed the **L3 approximation only** — the level-3 lifting-DWT
**lowpass** band (`[N,313]`, ~31 Hz effective, 8× downsampled) — and trained the decoder
to reconstruct the full `[N,2500]` @ 250 Hz signal. The encoder was **blind to the >15 Hz
detail** (the l1/l2/l3 detail subbands were dropped from its input), so the decoder had to
hallucinate the high-frequency content from a lowpass latent. This is the root of the
quality ceiling (the historical ~0.81 small-scale plateau, ADR 0009/0031; the current
honest fullband **R ≈ 0.42–0.52**, TRUTH_LEDGER §2). L3-only input **cannot** reach the
LQS-M/LQS-C targets (R > 0.9 @ 63–525:1 CR / PRD 5–20) — it is an information ceiling, not
a model-capacity one (decoder size does not fix it; the tier-3 30ep ≥ tier-5 30ep A/B is
consistent with input-, not capacity-, limited).

The `--detail-bands all` lever existed (E1 probe, task #238) but was **never run to a
fullband-R number**. Critically, the detail rides the **input, not the wire**: the latent
stays `[32,79]`, so the full residual is **free on compression** (CR is set by the FSQ
level schedule on the 79 frames, ADR 0045 — adding input channels does not change the
packet size).

## Decision

The codec's **default input domain is the full residual**: `train_joint.py` defaults are
now `--detail-bands all --detail-stack-mode fold` (information-preserving, no coefficient
dropped) → encoder `in_ch = 21·8 = 168` at N=21. `--detail-bands none` (L3-only,
`in_ch=21`) is demoted to an **opt-in** ablation / tightest-SRAM SKU.

## Consequences

- **From-scratch retrain.** The encoder front-end input width changes (21 → 168), so
  L3-only checkpoints are not warm-start-compatible. The foundation oracle + the
  decoder-solo cascade (ADR 0033 + `--freeze-encoder`) train under the new default.
- **MCU encoder is bigger but the data is on-device.** The detail subbands are the lifting
  DWT output the MCU already computes for the lossless codec, so feeding them costs only a
  wider encoder stem (168→W), not new on-device compute. The clinical STM32N6 tier (larger
  INT8 encoder) accommodates this; the RP2350 general tier may keep the L3-only ablation if
  the wider stem overflows SRAM (HAZ-002/firmware budget — to be measured).
- **Channel-agnostic is incompatible with detail-bands** (the CA front-end consumes
  per-electrode L3; detail-band channel stacking is a follow-on). CA mode pins `in_ch=21`
  (L3-only) until CA detail-conditioning lands. `train_joint` raises on `--channel-agnostic`
  + `in_ch≠21` — no silent misconfig.
- **Broker footprint gap (must fix before launching).** The BLUT footprint model
  (`blut/src/broker/footprint.rs`) has **no `in_ch` / detail-bands term** — it bills a
  168-ch run identically to a 21-ch run, so a fullband run is under-estimated and will be
  cgroup-killed (the same admit-then-kill class as the tier-5 OOMs, ADR 0046). The
  fullband default is NOT safe to launch until the broker bills input channels (and uses
  proportional headroom). Tracked as a broker-hardening follow-up.
- **NOT YET RUN.** The fullband-input path has never trained end-to-end to a fullband-R
  number (E1 #238). The first action under this ADR is a smoke + a converged baseline,
  graded against the LQS floors (`Eagle/lqs/src/levels.rs`). The decision is the
  architecture direction; the validated result is pending.

## Alternatives rejected

- **Keep L3-only + grow the decoder.** Rejected — capacity is not the bottleneck (ADR
  0009/0031; the decoder A/B), and a bigger decoder cannot recover information the input
  never carried.
- **interp stacking** (lossy: l1/l2 downsampled to the 313 grid, in_ch=84). Rejected as the
  default — drops high-freq coefficients, so a quality null could be blamed on the stacking
  rather than the model (ADR 0031). `fold` is the honest full residual.

# ADR 0050: Optimizer registry + config datatype for the lamquant cookbook

## Status

Proposed 2026-06-16

(Design handoff. Implementation lands in `blut-lamquant` — the cookbook
recipe tree is mid-restructure under its owner, so this ADR is the
contract, not yet-merged code. Supersedes nothing; see Related.)

## Context

Optimizer selection in the lamquant (EEG/SNN/codec) trainers is a set of
duplicated, drifting `if args.optimizer == ... elif ...` chains:

- `blut/python/lamquant/snn/train_4state_controller.py:870` — `adamw | esoap`
- `blut/python/lamquant/snn/pretrain_ssl_tueg.py:454` — `adamw | esoap`
- `blut/python/lamquant/student/train_joint.py` — its own chain (soap / adamw / muon)

The implementations are already co-located in `blut/python/lamquant/student/`:
`soap_optimizer.py`, `esoap.py`, `sinksoaph.py`, `muon_optimizer.py`,
`cautious_wd.py`. A second, **separate** factory exists for the lamu/LLM
cookbook (`blut/python/trainer.py:build_optimizer`, AdamW/Apollo via
`SFTTrainer`); that one is out of scope here — it serves a different
optimizer pool and a different (transformers) training loop.

Two forces motivate the change now:

1. **The A/B goal is blocked on plumbing, not on the optimizers.** #71
   (COSMOS A/B) and #209 (SinkSOAPH arm) both need a new `--optimizer`
   branch added to a trainer before they can even smoke-test. SinkSOAPH
   exists (`sinksoaph.py`) but is only wired into the archived mamba
   trainer; activating it means hand-editing another `if/elif`.
2. **The routing logic is non-trivial and gets copied wrong.** ESOAP is
   not "construct an optimizer" — it is "split params into a SOAP-routed
   group (2-D weights whose name ends in `in_proj.weight` / `x_proj.weight`
   / `out_proj.weight` / `spatial_mix.weight`) and an AdamW-rest group,"
   then add the distiller's `student_proj` as an AdamW group
   (`train_4state_controller.py:889`). SinkSOAPH goes further and *raises*
   on any non-2-D param. Each trainer that wants ESOAP/SinkSOAPH must
   re-derive this routing. A flat `name → class` registry would lose it.

This ADR also answers the explicit question raised when the change was
proposed: **does a registry hurt training throughput or torch.compile?**
(Answer in Rationale: no.)

## Decision

Introduce a typed **optimizer registry** in a new
`blut/python/lamquant/optimizers/` package. Move the five `student/*`
optimizer modules there. Each registry entry is an `OptimizerSpec`, not a
bare class:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptimizerSpec:
    name: str                                  # "esoap", "sinksoaph", "soap", "muon", "adamw"
    config_cls: type                           # the per-optimizer config dataclass (validated)
    build_param_groups: Callable[[Iterable[tuple[str, Tensor]], Config], list[dict]]
    construct: Callable[[list[dict], Config], torch.optim.Optimizer]
    requires: tuple[str, ...] = ()             # e.g. ("license:cosmos",) — hard gate
    supports_compiled_step: bool = False       # opt-in per optimizer AFTER validation; see Rationale

@register_optimizer
def _esoap() -> OptimizerSpec: ...
```

A single entry point replaces every `if/elif`:

```python
optimizer = build_optimizer(spec_name, named_params, cfg, *, extra_groups=...)
```

`build_optimizer` looks up the spec, validates `cfg` against
`spec.config_cls`, calls `spec.build_param_groups` (which owns the ESOAP
suffix routing / SinkSOAPH 2-D guard), appends any `extra_groups` (the
distiller `student_proj`), and calls `spec.construct`.

`extra_groups` follow standard torch param-group semantics and inherit the
optimizer's top-level defaults unless they carry their own override keys.
This must match current behavior exactly: today
`optimizer.add_param_group({"params": student_proj…})`
(`train_4state_controller.py:889`) passes *no* `lr`/`weight_decay`/`method`,
so the group inherits the optimizer `defaults` — and because ESOAP's
default `method` is `"adamw"`, `student_proj` lands as a plain AdamW group.
An `extra_group` that needs different semantics must set those keys itself;
the registry never positionally re-routes an extra group into a
preconditioned method. Each optimizer's
hyperparameters live in a validated config dataclass mirroring its real
`__init__` (e.g. ESOAP: `lr, rank_frac, mu, gram_beta, betas, ns_steps,
nesterov, eps, weight_decay, cautious_wd`; SinkSOAPH: `lr, mu, gram_beta,
sinkhorn_steps, nesterov, betas, eps, sinkhorn_eps, weight_decay`).

The recipe layer gains an **optimizer-sweep arm**: a recipe can declare
`optimizers = ["esoap", "sinksoaph", "soap"]` and BLUT fans out one run
per spec (admission-gated like any other recipe run), so the COSMOS /
SinkSOAPH / SOAP A/B is a config edit, not a code edit. License-gated
specs (`requires=("license:cosmos",)`) are refused at registry-resolve
time, preserving the COSMOS hard-gate (#71).

**Out of scope for this ADR:** decomposing the trainers into primitives
(data → forward → loss → backward → step → log → checkpoint). That is a
larger, higher-blast-radius refactor and gets its own ADR; the optimizer
registry stands alone and does not depend on it.

## Rationale

- **The registry is construction-time only — zero runtime cost.**
  `build_optimizer` runs once at trainer setup. There is no per-step
  indirection added; the returned object is a plain
  `torch.optim.Optimizer` the loop calls `.step()` on exactly as today.

- **No torch.compile interaction** (in the default `torch.compile(model)`
  path; the fused/capturable-step exception is the next bullet).
  `torch.compile` compiles the model's
  forward (and, if requested, backward). The optimizer `.step()` executes
  *after* backward, outside the compiled graph, in eager mode by default.
  The registry chooses the optimizer before the training loop and outside
  any compiled region, so it cannot trigger guard failures or
  recompilation. The only way an optimizer perturbs compile is if it
  injects forward hooks or a second forward (SAM-style) — none of
  SOAP / ESOAP / SinkSOAPH / Muon / COSMOS do; they precondition gradients
  inside `step()`. The intrinsic per-step cost (SOAP-family `eigh` /
  preconditioner matmuls — the same math that OOM'd at
  `max_precond_dim=10000` in the codec ceiling run) is unchanged by the
  abstraction.

- **If `step()` is ever compiled** (fused/capturable optimizer + CUDA
  graphs, a future optimization), different specs produce different
  compiled step graphs — each compiles once and is cached. That is
  per-spec, not per-step, and not a regression. `supports_compiled_step`
  on the spec documents which optimizers are safe to wrap; it defaults to
  `False` (none are validated under a compiled step today) and each
  optimizer opts in only after a fixed-seed equivalence check, so the loop
  never silently CUDA-graph-captures an unvalidated `step()`.

- **Param-group routing belongs to the optimizer, not the trainer.**
  Folding `build_param_groups` into the spec is the load-bearing reason to
  do this at all: it kills the copy-paste of ESOAP's suffix list and
  SinkSOAPH's 2-D guard across trainers, and makes "add a new optimizer"
  a single-file change that every trainer picks up.

- **Matches the established typed-recipe philosophy** (ADR 0044, the
  `register_recipe!` macro + defaults unification). An optimizer spec is
  the same shape of object one layer down.

- **Honours the BLUT scope charter (ADR 0034).** Optimizers are PyTorch
  research code; the registry lives in the Python cookbook, not the Rust
  control plane. BLUT still only *selects and launches* — it does not
  reimplement optimizer math.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Flat `name → optimizer_class` registry.** Rejected: loses ESOAP's
  param-group routing and SinkSOAPH's 2-D guard. Every caller would have
  to re-derive the grouping, which is exactly the duplication being
  removed. The spec must own `build_param_groups`.

- **Keep the per-trainer `if/elif` chains.** Rejected: this is the status
  quo that blocks #71/#209 behind a code edit per optimizer and lets the
  routing logic drift between trainers (4state and ssl already differ from
  joint).

- **Model optimizer selection in the Rust control plane.** Rejected:
  optimizer construction needs live `torch.nn.Parameter` objects and the
  param-name routing — it is research code by ADR 0034. Rust selects the
  *recipe*; Python selects the *optimizer* inside it. The sweep arm is the
  seam: Rust fans out N recipe runs, each pinned to one spec name.

- **Unify with the lamu `build_optimizer`.** Rejected for now: different
  optimizer pool (Apollo/AdamW8bit), different loop (`SFTTrainer` owns
  construction via `TrainingArguments(optim=...)`). A shared registry
  interface is possible later but is not required for the A/B goal and
  would widen blast radius across both cookbooks.

## Consequences

- `blut/python/lamquant/optimizers/` becomes the single home for codec/SNN
  optimizers; `student/*optimizer*.py` + `esoap.py` + `sinksoaph.py` +
  `cautious_wd.py` move there (import sites in 3 trainers update).
- The three `if/elif` chains delete down to one `build_optimizer` call
  each. New optimizers (COSMOS once licensed) are a single spec file.
- The recipe schema grows an optional `optimizers: list[str]` sweep field
  (BLUT-API, ADR 0044 surface) — coordinate with #264 (single schema
  source) so the field shows up in `recipe show` + the TUI form once.
- Load-bearing: the spec's `build_param_groups` is now the *only* place
  ESOAP routing lives. A regression there silently changes which params
  get SOAP vs AdamW. Validation (below) must pin it.
- Trainer-primitive decomposition remains open as a separate, later ADR.

## Related Decisions

- ADR 0034 — BLUT scope charter (control plane vs research code).
- ADR 0044 — BLUT-API standardization / typed recipes (`register_recipe!`).
- ADR 0030 — cautious weight decay (a flag the ESOAP/SOAP configs carry).
- ADR 0029 — SNN objective (the trainer these optimizers feed).
- Tasks #71 (COSMOS A/B), #209 (SinkSOAPH arm) — the work this unblocks.

## Validation

- **Behavioral equivalence before/after.** On a fixed seed, a 1-epoch run
  through the registry must produce the *same* param-group split and the
  *same* loss trajectory as the current `if/elif` path, for both `adamw`
  and `esoap` on `train_4state_controller`. Assert the ESOAP group
  membership (which named params land in the SOAP-routed group) is
  byte-for-byte identical to the hand-rolled suffix filter at `:875`.
- **Config validation is fail-closed.** An unknown optimizer name, a
  missing required hyperparameter, or a license-gated spec without the
  license raises at resolve time (mirrors `build_optimizer`'s existing
  `RuntimeError(f"unknown optimizer: {opt_name!r}")`).
- **Sweep arm parity.** A recipe with `optimizers=["esoap"]` produces a
  run identical to the single-optimizer recipe — the sweep machinery adds
  no behavioral delta when N=1.
- **Revisit trigger.** If a future fused/compiled-step optimization shows
  a measurable recompile cost attributable to spec selection, revisit
  `supports_compiled_step` and the construction-time guarantee.

# ADR 0051: Competitive posture vs ITU-T H.BWC, and NWB as a container

## Status

Accepted 2026-06-18

(Strategy ADR. Records verified facts about the competing standard and the
codec-feature gaps they imply.)

**Owner posture decision (2026-06-18): head-to-head rival.** The owner chose
to position LamQuant as a direct competitor aiming to win adoption against
H.BWC, over the flank/contribute options this ADR analyzed. The three
technical tracks below (benchmark, near-lossless+rate-control, NWB) are
retained as the *foundation* of that posture — a rival must at minimum match
H.BWC's working points and metrics — and the honest risk of the rival path
(opposing the HEVC/VVC team + Fraunhofer HHI + Dolby + DICOM WG32 on their
core competency, with an unvalidated neural lossy and a lossless tier the
standards body has declared insufficient) is recorded in Consequences and
stands. Track 1 (the benchmark harness) is built (`tools/hbwc_bench/`,
commit 3d5fa590).

## Context

### What H.BWC actually is (verified against the source CfP)

Primary source: **ITU-T SG16 Q6/16 Call for Proposals SG16-TD286-R1/PLEN,
"Coding of biomedical waveform data," Rennes, 26 April 2024** (provisional
Recommendation name **H.BWC**, "Biomedical and general waveform signal
coding"). Key facts, quoted/paraphrased from the CfP:

- **Who.** Q6/16 is the ITU-T video-coding question (VCEG) — the group
  behind H.264/HEVC/VVC. Rapporteur **Gary J. Sullivan** (HEVC/VVC).
  CfP coordinator **Jonathan Pfaff (Fraunhofer HHI)**. DICOM liaison
  **Jonathan Halford (DICOM WG32 co-chair, MUSC)**. Committed contributors:
  **Fraunhofer HHI and Dolby Laboratories.** This is the team that
  standardized modern video coding, not a research lab.
- **Modalities tested: EEG, ECG, EMG.** (Not PPG — PPG is out of the test
  scope. ECG and EMG are in, alongside EEG.)
- **Nine working points.** WP0 = `MAE = 0` (lossless). WP1–WP8 cap the
  bitstream at decreasing **bits-per-sample** ceilings and, for each
  ceiling, *minimize PRD*:
  WP1 `BPS≤4.0`, WP2 `≤3.5`, WP3 `≤3.0`, WP4 `≤2.5`, WP5 `≤2.0`,
  WP6 `≤1.5`, WP7 `≤1.0`, WP8 `≤0.75`. (`BPS = bits_in_bitstream / (N·M)`.)
- **Metrics, exact formulas in the CfP.** `MAE` (max abs error), `PRD`
  (mean-removed % RMS distortion), `CPRD` (channel-normalized PRD), and
  `PSNR` per-channel + averaged with `B = 16`. Proponents report
  BPS/PRD/CPRD/PSNR per working point, plus rate–distortion graphs.
- **Test data (downloadable; public creds in the CfP, `ftp.hhi.fraunhofer.de`
  login `dicom`):** EEG = **MUSC_Dataset_E** (interictal epileptiform
  discharges + seizures, **41 sequences**); ECG = **MIT-BIH Arrhythmia**
  (48); EMG = **Mendeley sEMG hand-gestures** (40). **All test data is in
  EDF.** Not CHB-MIT, not NMR, not NWB.
- **Timeline.** CfP responses Oct/Nov 2024 (Antalya). Annex A.1 lists
  `Timing: 2025-10`, approval process AAP — i.e. a consented Recommendation
  is expected late-2025 → 2026.
- **IPR.** Common Patent Policy (ITU/ISO/IEC, i.e. RAND) for the standard,
  BUT the CfP states reference *software* is "likely" to be published under
  a **permissive software licence**, as with prior Q6/16 projects.
- **The thesis, verbatim from Annex A.1 requirement 5:** *"A lossless-only
  approach will not produce better than a 2-3X compression ratio, which is
  not sufficient."* The standards body has explicitly decided lossless
  alone is a dead end and the deliverable is **lossless + near-lossless +
  lossy**.
- **Other hard requirements (Annex A.1):** 16–24 bit (possibly higher);
  500–2000 Hz clinical, up to 40 kHz research; up to hundreds of channels;
  **mixed per-channel sampling rates**; **block-level random access with an
  index storable outside the bitstream** (DICOM fragments/frames style);
  a mode with **independent per-channel decoding**; metadata storable
  outside the bitstream.

### Where LamQuant actually stands

- **Validated asset: the lossless path.** Bit-exact EDF/BDF roundtrip,
  cross-backend byte-equal golden gate, and — uniquely — **proven bit-exact
  on $5 silicon** (RP2350 Hazard3, lossless firmware fits 512 KB SRAM).
- **Unvalidated: the neural lossy.** Honest fullband R ≈ 0.42–0.52, no
  validated end-to-end number, PCCP not passed, on-MCU neural deferred.
- **Codec capability vs H.BWC requirements (read from source):** bit depth
  is *scaffolded* — container header carries a 16/24 `bit_depth` field
  (`container.rs:706`), EDF reader has a BDF/24-bit path, internal math is
  `i32`/`i64`; HDF5 is already an *optional* export feature
  (`write_hdf5`, MAT-v7.3). **Missing:** any near-lossless / bounded-error
  mode, a target-BPS rate-control knob, verified 24-bit/int32/float
  roundtrip, per-channel mixed sampling rate, an NWB reader, and an HDF5
  *compression filter*.

### The two-market split this reveals

H.BWC's test data and DICOM lineage put it squarely in the
**clinical / DICOM interchange** market, where the container is EDF→DICOM.
**NWB (HDF5 + schema, NIH BRAIN-mandated)** is the *AI/BCI/iEEG research*
market — which H.BWC is **not** targeting. "EDF vs NWB" is therefore not a
codec choice; it is a *market* choice. Pivoting LamQuant's native container
to NWB moves it toward a segment H.BWC is ignoring, and *away* from
head-to-head on H.BWC's own EDF/DICOM turf.

## Decision

Do **not** position LamQuant as a rival *standard* racing H.BWC to consent.
Racing Sullivan + Fraunhofer HHI + Dolby on transform-codec BPS-vs-PRD,
with an unvalidated neural lossy and a lossless path the standards body has
already declared insufficient, is not a winnable "become the standard"
play. Instead adopt a **three-track, no-regret posture**, all deterministic
and independent of the stalled neural model:

1. **Measure against the real target.** Build an apples-to-apples benchmark
   harness on H.BWC's *actual* datasets (MUSC EEG-41, MIT-BIH ECG-48,
   Mendeley sEMG-40, all EDF, publicly downloadable) at its *actual* nine
   working points (WP0 lossless + WP1–WP8 BPS ceilings) reporting its
   *actual* metrics (MAE, PRD, CPRD, PSNR @ B=16). Without this every claim
   is unfounded. This is the first build.

2. **Close the "lossless-insufficient" gap in the lossless crate.** Add a
   **bounded-MAE near-lossless mode** and a **target-BPS rate-control knob**
   spanning lossless → near-lossless → lossy. This is deterministic DSP
   (bounded residual quantization pre-rANS), ships without the neural path,
   and directly answers requirement 5. Plus the bounded requirements:
   verified 24-bit/int32, block random-access index (LMA already has an
   index), independent-channel-decode mode.

3. **Own the NWB flank H.BWC is not addressing.** Ship a **registered HDF5
   compression-filter plugin** (LML as an HDF5 filter ID) + an NWB
   `ElectricalSeries` reader/writer, **host-only** (never in the no_std
   firmware build). This makes LamQuant "the codec for NWB" without forking
   the container, in a market the standard is leaving open.

Keep the **embedded + permissive** wedge central across all three: LamQuant
already runs bit-exact on silicon and is MIT/Apache; H.BWC will be a spec
(RAND patents) whose permissive reference software is unlikely to ship a
512 KB-SRAM MCU implementation at consent. A fourth path — **contribute the
embedded reference implementation to H.BWC** rather than oppose it (the CfP
explicitly welcomes non-member contributions and a permissive reference) —
is recorded as a live alternative, not foreclosed.

The neural lossy remains upside-if-it-validates (it could, in principle,
win WP6–WP8 where transforms struggle), but it is **not** on this critical
path and must not gate tracks 1–3.

## Rationale

- **The competitor's own thesis names our weakness and dismisses our
  strength.** "Lossless-only ≤ 2–3× is not sufficient" is the exact
  inversion of LamQuant's posture (validated lossless, unvalidated lossy).
  Ignoring it means competing only at WP0, which the standard treats as
  table stakes. Track 2 is therefore existential, not optional.
- **You cannot out-govern a DICOM-liaised ITU-T Recommendation.** Adoption
  in clinical interchange flows through PACS/DICOM vendors who implement the
  standard. A permissive OSS codec wins on *deployment* and *segment*, not
  on standardization.
- **The benchmark is no-regret.** Whatever posture is chosen, knowing
  LamQuant's BPS/PRD/PSNR on the exact CfP datasets is required input — to
  compete, to flank, or to contribute.
- **NWB is a flank, not a frontal assault.** It is genuinely where AI/BCI
  data is going (requirement-free of H.BWC's DICOM framing) and plays to
  LamQuant's HDF5 scaffolding. It also de-risks the strategy: it does not
  depend on beating Fraunhofer/Dolby at rate-distortion.
- **Permissive-license edge is real but softer than first assumed.** The
  *spec* carries RAND patents, but the CfP signals a *permissive reference
  implementation*. The durable differentiator is therefore **proven
  embedded deployment**, not license alone.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Race H.BWC to be the standard.** Rejected: opposes the HEVC/VVC team +
  Fraunhofer + Dolby + DICOM WG32 on their core competency, with weaker
  assets. No governance path to "the standard" for a lone OSS project.
- **Publish a rival open standard.** Rejected: standards win on
  institutional adoption; a second standard fragments rather than wins, and
  duplicates the CfP's own permissive-reference plan.
- **Ignore H.BWC, ship lossless as-is.** Rejected: the standards body has
  declared exactly that posture insufficient; it cedes WP1–WP8 entirely.
- **Pivot native container fully from EDF to NWB.** Rejected *as stated* —
  NWB is a container, not the codec, and EDF is H.BWC's own test format, so
  dropping EDF would *forfeit* the ability to benchmark/interoperate on the
  standard's turf. **Add** NWB as a first-class container (track 3); do not
  *replace* EDF.
- **Contribute the embedded reference impl to H.BWC.** Not rejected — kept
  live as the fourth path; revisit once track-1 numbers exist.

## Consequences

- A new benchmark harness (host-side) targeting EDF inputs at WP0–WP8 with
  MAE/PRD/CPRD/PSNR. Reuses the existing CHB-MIT lossless bench plumbing;
  adds the lossy working-point sweep + metric set. Feeds `docs/TRUTH_LEDGER.md`.
- The lossless crate gains a near-lossless mode + rate control — a wire-format
  addition (new mode flag, bounded-error parameter). Needs a new golden
  table and the byte-equal gate extended; must stay no_std-clean for firmware
  (near-lossless encode may be host-first, decode firmware-capable).
- An optional `nwb`/`hdf5-filter` host feature; HDF5 stays out of the no_std
  build. NWB reader scoped to `ElectricalSeries` only.
- Commits the project to publishing real BPS/PRD/PSNR numbers — which may
  show LamQuant *behind* Fraunhofer/Dolby at low BPS. That is the honest
  input the posture decision needs (end-to-end-numbers-only discipline).
- The "release before DICOM / become the standard" framing is explicitly
  retired in favor of segment + deployment + (optional) contribution.

## Related Decisions

- ADR 0049 — full-residual input (the neural lossy's current ceiling work).
- ADR 0045 — latent presets / LQS teacher (neural quality ladder).
- ADR 0010 / 0017 / 0023 / 0025 — LML/LMA format + ingest (the container
  layer NWB/HDF5 plugs into).
- Lossless paper TBME pivot — hardware/deployment-validation framing is the
  same embedded wedge this ADR leans on.

## Validation

- **Track 1 done = a table in `docs/TRUTH_LEDGER.md`:** LamQuant WP0–WP8
  BPS/PRD/CPRD/PSNR on MUSC-41 / MIT-BIH-48 / Mendeley-40, alongside any
  published H.BWC anchor numbers when available. This is the factual basis
  for every subsequent claim and for the posture decision.
- **Track 2 correctness:** near-lossless mode must *guarantee* its declared
  MAE bound on every golden vector (property test: decoded error ≤ bound),
  and lossless WP0 must remain byte-exact.
- **Track 3:** an NWB file written through the HDF5 filter must round-trip
  through stock `pynwb`/`h5py` (filter registered + discoverable), with the
  `ElectricalSeries` recovered bit-exact.
- **Revisit trigger:** if track-1 numbers show LamQuant within ~5% PRD of
  the H.BWC anchor at clinically-relevant working points (≈WP3–WP5),
  reconsider the contribute-to-standard path; if far behind, lean harder on
  the NWB/embedded flank.

# ADR 0052: Two-format, three-profile lossless codec architecture (Firmware / Desktop / Optimum)

## Status

Accepted 2026-06-20

(Architecture ADR. Organizes the deterministic lossless codec into two wire
formats sharing one functional surface, exercised by three build profiles.
Owner-converged in design discussion, 2026-06-20. The campaign that uses this
architecture to beat H.BWC is tracked separately in ADR 0054.)

## Context

ADR 0051 positioned LamQuant as a **head-to-head rival to ITU-T H.BWC**. The
H.BWC benchmark (`tools/hbwc_bench/`) gave the honest verdict:

- **WP0 lossless:** EEG ≈ parity (+1.6% BPS synthetic, +21% real CHB-MIT); ECG
  +37% behind the HHI reference.
- **WP1–WP8 lossy:** HHI wins **every** working point (WP2: 5.8% PRD vs 1.3% —
  4.5×).
- **The entropy lever is spent.** Context arithmetic gave ~nothing over order-0
  because LPC already removes inter-sample correlation. The gap lives in the
  **transform + R-D allocation**.

Today the codec is **one crate** (`codec-lossless/lamquant-lossless`, lib name
`lamquant_core`). The firmware/host distinction exists only as a *compute
backend* (`ComputeBackend::Firmware` vs `Desktop`, byte-equal), and the float /
max-ratio experiments (target-BPS RD search, context arithmetic `arith_cat`,
extended LPC, `rans`) are entangled inside the firmware crate behind env-var
flags. There is no clean home for the deterministic float-allowed "win the
working points" work, and no *structural* guarantee keeping its heavy deps out of
the 512 KB MCU build.

**Verified firmware-purity finding:** the no_std *encoder* is not strictly
integer — `lpc.rs::autocorr_scalar` returns `Vec<f64>` (lpc.rs:43) and Levinson
runs in f64 (lpc.rs:360-371), quantized to Q27 i64 (lpc.rs:383-389). On
Cortex-M/Hazard3 that is f64 soft-float. The *decoder* (synthesis from Q27
coefficients) is pure integer. The `blockfloat` Levinson alternative is host-only
(`LMQ_LEVINSON=blockfloat`, lpc.rs:308-333).

## Decision

Organize the deterministic lossless codec as **two wire formats sharing one
functional surface, exercised by three build profiles.** The unifying idea: all
encoders **consume the same input abstraction and the same `Mode`, run their own
process, and stamp a format magic on the output** so each stream is a distinct,
self-describing object. The shared seam is the **I/O contract, not the
implementation** — the inner transform / entropy / rate-control machinery
diverges fully per format.

**Two wire formats, identical functional surface**
(`Mode ∈ {lossless · bounded_mae(δ) · target_bps(b)}`):

- **LML — the cheap-decode floor / interchange standard.** Integer-decodable,
  MCU-fittable. The universal format every decoder in the project must read.
- **LMO — the Optimum ceiling.** Deterministic, **no restrictions on technique**
  (float math, deeper/better transforms, RD-optimal PCRD allocation, context
  arithmetic / rANS, H.BWC-class tools re-implemented in Rust). **Includes a
  true-lossless WP0** (bit-exact, just smaller than LML). Decode is no_std-
  *capable* (soft-float) but heavy.

The two formats trade **compression ratio against decode cost**: LML decodes
anywhere cheaply; LMO compresses harder at a heavier decoder. Same functionality,
opposite ends of one axis.

**Three build profiles**

- **Firmware** — LML encode + decode, fits an MCU, *no SIMD / desktop tricks*.
  Can **optionally** include the LMO-decode module ("only if you really need it";
  usually omitted to stay small).
- **Desktop** — **identical to Firmware, just fast** (SIMD + desktop tricks the
  MCU can't run), producing **byte-identical** LML output, **plus** the Optimum
  (LMO) encoder + decoder as standard. The superset *assembly*, not a
  reimplementation.
- **Optimum** — *is* the LMO codec: the deterministic max-CR encoder + its
  decoder. The **encoder is host-only**; the **decoder is no_std-capable** (the
  module Desktop ships standard and Firmware can opt into).

**Shared abstraction.** A single `Codec` trait (`encode(&Signal, Mode) ->
Stream`, `decode(&[u8]) -> Signal`) with two implementations (LML, LMO). A
universal `decode(bytes)` dispatches on the leading **format magic**; on a build
lacking the optional LMO module it returns a typed *"LMO decoder not installed"*
rather than mis-parsing.

**Crate structure** (promotes the feature boundary to a dependency-graph
boundary):

```
codec-lossless/
  lamquant-lossless-core/   # no_std+alloc. Input abstraction + Codec trait +
                            # LML codec (encode+decode, integer) + magic-
                            # dispatch decoder. Builds for riscv32. = Firmware.
  lamquant-optimum/         # the LMO codec. Feature `decode` (no_std-capable,
                            # Firmware opt-in) + feature `encode` (std + float,
                            # NEVER reachable from the no_std build).
  lamquant-lossless-host/   # std. core+SIMD (fast LML) + optimum(decode+encode)
                            # + container/edf/lma/cli/tui. = Desktop assembly.
  crates/lamquant-common/   # (unchanged) shared CRC-32 / path / ingest.
  lamquant-py/              # (unchanged) PyO3, depends on -host.
```

The `optimum/encode` ↔ `optimum/decode` feature split is what makes all three
constraints structural at once: Optimum *encode* (heavy/float/SIMD) can never
enter the firmware graph; Optimum *decode* is opt-in on Firmware and standard on
Desktop. The `lamquant_core` lib-name re-export is preserved so the 19 Rust + 22
Python dependents do not churn.

**Firmware-purity scope (follow-up).** Tier "Firmware" is, for now,
**integer-decode + f64-soft-float-encode** (autocorr + Levinson). Porting a
fixed-point/blockfloat autocorr to no_std for a genuinely integer end-to-end
encoder is a sized follow-up, not a blocker.

## Rationale

- **The split matches the code.** `ComputeBackend::Firmware`/`Desktop` are
  byte-equal today; Firmware/Desktop are *the same codec in two execution
  profiles*, exactly the model here. Naming reuses the existing enum.
- **Seam at the I/O contract, not the guts.** Sharing the input object + `Mode` +
  guarantees + magic-stamped output buys symmetry (one test battery over both
  formats). Sharing the inner DSP would couple LML's integer deadzone path to
  LMO's float PCRD — two things that should evolve independently.
- **Why keep LML if LMO compresses better:** LML decodes *anywhere* cheaply; it
  is the interchange floor and the silicon-proven artifact. LMO is the ceiling
  you reach for when the decoder can afford it.
- **Crate isolation makes purity structural.** The env-var experimental coupling
  (arith_cat/rans/extended-LPC in the firmware crate) is the exact leak a
  dependency-graph boundary removes. `optimum/encode` is simply unreachable from
  the no_std build.
- **Magic-dispatch is self-describing.** One decode entry point, format-tagged
  streams, typed "module not installed" — no out-of-band config, clean firmware
  story.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Desktop as a heavier *encoder* (FLAC -8) emitting smaller LML.** Rejected:
  the owner specified Desktop is *identical to Firmware, just fast* (byte-
  identical output). Ratio gains come from Optimum/LMO, not from a heavier LML
  encoder. Desktop's value is **speed + carrying Optimum**, not compression.
- **Optimum host-only, never in the firmware graph.** Rejected: the LMO *decoder*
  must be a portable, optional Firmware module. Only the *encoder* is excluded
  from the firmware graph.
- **Three wire formats (one per profile).** Rejected: Firmware and Desktop share
  LML byte-for-byte; only Optimum is a genuinely different codec → two formats.
- **One crate, feature-gated tiers.** Rejected as the structural choice: purity
  would rest on feature discipline, not the dependency graph (the lib-name
  re-export still minimizes churn under the split).
- **Allow neural / learned models in Optimum.** Rejected: Optimum is
  **deterministic only**. Learned entropy/codecs stay in LMQ (ADR 0049) and keep
  Optimum out of PCCP scope (lossless = deterministic).

## Consequences

- **A three-member workspace** + the `optimum` decode/encode feature split.
  Mechanical module migration; green `cargo build` + `cargo test` + the no_std
  riscv build required at each step.
- **Gate semantics sharpen.** `byte_equal_backends.rs` is a **within-codec**
  property (Firmware-profile LML == Desktop-profile LML). A new **cross-codec**
  property asserts WP0 decode-equivalence to the original across both formats. One
  parametrized functional battery (lossless bit-exact, δ-bound, BPS ceiling) runs
  over both LML and LMO. The `core-no_std` CI job retargets at
  `lamquant-lossless-core`.
- **The format magic touches every stream surface:** the LMA container must wrap
  LMO too, and `verify` / `roundtrip` / `info` / EDF-export dispatch on it.
  Designed-in now, cheap; retrofitted later, painful.
- **Env-var experimental flags leave the firmware crate** (`arith_cat`, `rans`,
  extended-LPC → `lamquant-optimum`).
- **Firmware encoder f64 follow-up** (accept soft-float, or port blockfloat to
  no_std) sizes the core crate's purity claim.

## Related Decisions

- ADR 0058 — **amends** this ADR's crate names (the `lamquant-lml-*` tier family)
  and reverses the "Desktop as a separate crate — Rejected" alternative below
  (Desktop is now its own crate, `lamquant-lml-desktop`). ADR 0058 is the
  authority on crate naming.
- ADR 0051 — competitive posture vs H.BWC + NWB (the strategy).
- ADR 0054 — the in-progress warplan/campaign that uses this architecture to beat
  H.BWC.
- ADR 0010 / 0012 — LML format spec + production config.
- ADR 0023 / 0025 — ingest + neural/lossless boundary.
- ADR 0041 — LMA v2 streaming archive (the container that must wrap both magics).
- ADR 0049 — full-residual *neural* lossy (LMQ; distinct from this deterministic
  Optimum tier).

## Validation

- **Split done =** `cargo build -p lamquant-lossless-core --no-default-features
  --target riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf` green with no `optimum/encode` in the
  graph; `cargo test` green, goldens unchanged.
- **Profile equivalence =** Firmware-profile and Desktop-profile produce
  byte-identical LML for the same input+config (`lml roundtrip`).
- **Cross-format =** LML and LMO both reconstruct the same signal at WP0
  (bit-exact); δ-bound and BPS-ceiling honored on every golden vector for both.
- **Magic-dispatch =** a Firmware build without the LMO module returns the typed
  "not installed" error on an LMO stream, never a mis-parse.

# ADR 0053: TUI hub-and-spoke architecture (standalone binaries, hub as launcher)

## Status

Accepted 2026-06-20

## Context

LamQuant ships multiple tools: `lml` (lossless codec), `flash` (firmware), `lmq` (neural codec), `blut` (training), `eagle` (evaluation), `vision` (visualization). Each tool is a standalone Rust binary with its own TUI. A hub binary (`lamquant`) orchestrates them.

The current state has two problems:

1. **The LML binary is noncompliant.** Running `lml` with no args boots into a mini-hub (tiles for codec hub, settings, peers, install, diagnostics) instead of going directly to lossless codec operations. The user must click through to "codec hub" to reach encode/decode/verify. This is because `lml` copied the hub's entire TUI framework rather than building its own focused TUI.

2. **TUI framework code is duplicated.** Both `tui/` (hub) and `codec-lossless/lamquant-lossless/src/tui/` have identical copies of ~15 modules (app.rs, panel.rs, router.rs, state.rs, theme.rs, config.rs, history.rs, peers_config.rs, etc.) and ~15 panel files. Changes to the framework must be replicated across all copies.

The owner's design intent: each binary is a self-contained tool that opens its own TUI directly. The hub detects installed binaries, launches them, and offers to install missing ones. No embedding, no feature gates, no shared panel trait. The hub is a launcher + installer, nothing more.

## Decision

Three new crates, one behavioral contract, one config model:

### 1. `lamquant-tui` — shared TUI framework crate (`crates/lamquant-tui/`)

A library crate that provides the reusable TUI infrastructure. Every spoke binary depends on it. Contains:

- **Core:** `app.rs` (generic event loop + router + panel HashMap), `panel.rs` (Panel trait, PanelAction, Action), `router.rs` (Router + history stack), `state.rs` (AppState), `theme.rs`, `art.rs` (LOGO, ASCII art), `layout.rs`, `crash.rs`, `clipboard.rs`, `snapshot.rs`
- **Shared widgets:** `file_browser.rs`, `dialog.rs`, `splash.rs`, `syscheck.rs`, `preflight.rs`, `resume.rs`, `root_warn.rs`, `tutorial.rs`, `wizard.rs`, `settings.rs`, `settings_help.rs`, `input.rs`, `output.rs`, `menu.rs`
- **Ops framework:** `ops/op_spec.rs` (operation spec), `ops/runner.rs` (subprocess runner + event channel)

The App is constructed via a builder pattern:

```rust
let app = App::builder("lml")
    .splash(splash_config())
    .home_screen("codec_hub")
    .register_panel("codec_hub", || Box::new(CodecHubPanel::new()))
    .register_panel("settings", || Box::new(lamquant_tui::widgets::SettingsPanel::new()))
    .build();
app.run();
```

Each binary sets `home_screen` to its primary panel. The hub sets it to `"main"` (the tile grid). `lml` sets it to `"codec_hub"` (lossless operations). `flash` sets it to `"firmware"` (toolchain + targets).

### 2. `lamquant-config` — shared config crate (`crates/lamquant-config/`)

A library crate with zero TUI dependencies. Every spoke binary and the hub depend on it. Contains:

- `load.rs` — parse, validate, recover (state machine below)
- `save.rs` — atomic write + .bak rotation
- `schema.rs` — known sections, keys, types, defaults
- `merge.rs` — fill gaps, preserve unknowns, type coercion
- `cli.rs` — `config show/set/reset` subcommand (shared across spokes)
- `comment.rs` — TOML comment preservation via `toml_edit`

**Config file:** `~/.config/lamquant/lamquant.toml`

**Section names match binary names:** `[lml]`, `[flash]`, `[lmq]`, `[blut]`, `[eagle]`, `[hub]`. Human-readable comments in the TOML provide context for each key.

**Lifecycle rules:**

1. Each spoke owns its section. `lml` reads/writes `[lml]` only. `flash` reads/writes `[firmware]` only. They never touch other sections.
2. First run creates the file with `[core]` + the spoke's own section with defaults.
3. Installing additional spokes appends their section with defaults. Changed settings in existing sections are preserved.
4. Installing the hub fills in ALL known sections with defaults (not just installed spokes). Changed settings are preserved.
5. Unknown sections and unknown keys within known sections are always preserved. Never delete what you don't understand.
6. `toml_edit` is the parser (not `toml`/serde) so that comments survive programmatic saves.

**CLI interface (shared across all spokes):**

```
lml config                          # show all
lml config show lml                 # show [lml] section only
lml config show lml.backend         # show single value
lml config set lml.backend firmware # set value
lml config reset                    # reset [lml] to defaults (prompts)
lml config reset --force            # skip confirmation
lml config validate                 # check for errors, show state
lml config diff                     # show what changed from defaults
lml config path                     # print config file path
```

Each spoke's `config` subcommand is restricted to its own section. `lml config set firmware.probe jlink` → error: "firmware section belongs to the flash binary". The hub's `config` subcommand can access all sections.

### 3. Config state machine

```
State 0: No file (first run)
  → Create with [core] defaults + spoke's own section. Save. Continue.

State 1: File exists → Parse TOML
  ├─ 1a: Parse FAILS (syntax error)
  │    → Copy to lamquant.toml.corrupt.<timestamp>
  │    → Try lamquant.toml.bak (last known good)
  │    → If .bak valid: load it, show recovery message
  │    → If no .bak: load built-in defaults, show recovery message
  │    → TUI dialog / CLI print with options:
  │      [e] Edit file  [r] Reset to defaults  [v] View error  [c] Continue
  │
  ├─ 1b: Parse OK → validate schema
  │    ├─ 1b-i: Valid, complete → load, continue (silent)
  │    ├─ 1b-ii: Valid, partial (missing sections)
  │    │    → Insert defaults for missing installed-spoke sections
  │    │    → If hub installed: fill ALL known sections
  │    │    → Save, brief info message
  │    ├─ 1b-iii: Valid, unknown sections → load, preserve, continue (silent)
  │    ├─ 1b-iv: Valid, unknown keys in known sections → load, preserve (silent)
  │    └─ 1b-v: Valid TOML, wrong types
  │         → Use default for mismatched keys, log the mismatch
  │         → Save corrected file, show message with [r] Reset [c] Continue
  │
  ├─ 1c: Empty file → treat as State 0
  │
  └─ 1d: File too large (>1MB) → refuse, show error with [v] View [r] Reset [q] Quit
```

### 4. Backup chain

```
~/.config/lamquant/
├── lamquant.toml              ← current (source of truth)
├── lamquant.toml.bak          ← last known good (auto-saved on every successful write)
└── lamquant.toml.corrupt.*    ← broken files (timestamped, never overwritten)
```

On every successful `Config::save()`:
1. Rename `lamquant.toml` → `lamquant.toml.bak` (overwrite previous .bak)
2. Write new `lamquant.toml`
3. If write fails → rename `.bak` back to `lamquant.toml`

### 5. Binary behavioral contract

Every spoke binary follows the same pattern:

| Binary | `home_screen` | Own domain panels | Reuses from `lamquant-tui` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lamquant` (hub) | `"main"` (tile grid) | main_hub, codec_hub, firmware, eagle, viz, train | settings, peers, splash, dialog, file_browser, etc. |
| `lml` | `"codec_hub"` (operations) | codec_hub, mode_panel, lossless_prompt | settings, peers, splash, file_browser, etc. |
| `flash` | `"firmware"` (toolchain + targets) | toolchain, targets, build, flash, bench | settings, peers, splash, etc. |
| `lmq` | `"neural"` (neural ops) | neural panels | same shared widgets |
| `blut` | standalone TUI (own framework) | N/A — too complex to embed | N/A — subprocess only |
| `eagle` | standalone CLI | N/A | N/A — subprocess only |

The hub detects installed spokes via `which::which`. Installed tiles show ✅ and launch the binary. Missing tiles show ❌ and offer to install via `cargo install --git <url> --bin <bin> --locked` (never bare crate name — dependency confusion protection, ADR 0025).

`blut` and `eagle` remain Level 1 (subprocess dispatch) — they have their own complex TUIs that don't benefit from embedding in the hub. The hub tile launches them as child processes.

### 6. TOML format

```toml
# LamQuant Configuration
# https://github.com/Quitetall/LamQuant
#
# Section names match binary names: [lml], [flash], [lmq], etc.
# Edit manually or use: <binary> config set <section>.<key> <value>
# Unknown sections and keys are preserved — never deleted by LamQuant.

[core]
# Log level: error, warn, info, debug, trace
log_level = "info"

# ── Lossless codec (lml) ──────────────────────────────────────────
[lml]
# Compute backend: "desktop" (AVX2+rayon) or "firmware" (scalar, matches MCU)
backend = "desktop"

# Default encode mode: "lma" (archive), "lml_siblings" (files + copy), "prompt" (ask)
default_mode = "lma"

# Verify CRC after every encode
verify_on_encode = true

# Worker threads (0 = auto-detect CPU count)
workers = 0

# ── Firmware (flash) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
[firmware]
# Default target: rp2350, stm32n6, esp32s3
default_target = "rp2350"

# Debug probe: "auto" (detect), "picoprobe", "jlink", "cmsis-dap"
probe = "auto"

# Use OpenOCD instead of probe-rs
openocd = false

# ── Neural codec (lmq) ────────────────────────────────────────────
[lmq]
# Model checkpoint (path or registry name)
model = "default"

# Quantization: fp32, int8, ternary
quant_mode = "fp32"

# ── Hub (lamquant) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
[hub]
# Theme: "auto" (follow terminal), "dark", "light"
theme = "auto"

# Show splash screen on launch
splash = true

# Auto-install missing spokes when selected
auto_install = false
```

## Rationale

- **Hub as launcher, not embedder.** Feature-gated embedding (ADR alternative) couples the hub to every spoke's ratatui version, requires a shared `SpokePanel` trait, and means the hub binary grows with each spoke. Subprocess dispatch is simpler: the hub never imports spoke crates, spokes evolve independently, and the hub stays thin. The tradeoff is no shared state between hub and spoke — acceptable because each spoke owns its own file picker, settings, and workflow.

- **Shared TUI framework, not copy-paste.** The current duplication (15+ identical modules in `tui/` and `lml/src/tui/`) means every bug fix or feature must be replicated. A shared crate (`lamquant-tui`) eliminates this. Each spoke binary is ~200 lines of domain panels + builder call, not ~4000 lines of copied framework.

- **Config in its own crate, not in the TUI crate.** Pure-CLI spokes (like a future `lml encode` that never opens a TUI) shouldn't pull in ratatui just to read config. `lamquant-config` is ~500 lines, zero TUI deps.

- **Section names match binary names.** Less confusion than `[lossless]` vs `lml`. The TOML comments provide human context.

- **toml_edit, not toml/serde.** Comment preservation is essential for UX. Users who hand-edit the TOML expect their comments to survive programmatic saves. `toml_edit` is the only Rust TOML library that supports this.

- **One rollback depth (.bak).** Deeper history (git, numbered backups) adds complexity for little value. The .corrupt.* files preserve forensic evidence. Users who need more history can use git on the config directory.

- **Spoke config restricted to own section.** Prevents `lml` from accidentally modifying `[firmware]` settings. The hub is the only binary that can access all sections.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Feature-gated embedding (SpokePanel trait).** Each spoke crate exports a panel module behind `#[cfg(feature = "panel")]`. The hub imports spokes as optional dependencies. Pros: in-process rendering, shared AppState. Cons: couples hub to every spoke's ratatui version, requires trait negotiation, hub binary grows with each spoke, complex Cargo feature matrix. Rejected: the subprocess model is simpler and the hub stays thin.

- **Dynamic plugin loading (libloading).** Spokes register panels via shared libraries loaded at runtime. Pros: zero compile-time coupling. Cons: unsafe FFI, version negotiation, no type safety, hard to debug. Rejected: massive complexity for marginal benefit over subprocess dispatch.

- **Per-spoke config files (`~/.config/lamquant/lml.toml`, `flash.toml`).** Each spoke owns its own file. Pros: no cross-spoke coordination. Cons: fragmented settings, no single file to inspect, hub can't fill gaps. Rejected: the single-file model is simpler for users and enables the hub's gap-filling behavior.

- **serde-based TOML (no comment preservation).** Simpler parser, but comments are lost on save. Rejected: unacceptable UX for a config file users are expected to hand-edit.

## Consequences

- `tui/src/tui/` (hub's TUI framework) becomes a thin wrapper around `lamquant-tui`. The hub's own panels (main_hub, firmware, eagle, etc.) stay in `tui/src/tui/panels/`, but the framework modules (app, panel, router, state, theme, etc.) move to the shared crate.

- `codec-lossless/lamquant-lossless/src/tui/` is deleted entirely. The LML binary imports `lamquant-tui` for the framework and `lamquant-config` for config. Its domain panels (codec_hub, mode_panel, lossless_prompt) move to `codec-lossless/lamquant-lossless/src/panels/` (or stay in the binary crate).

- The LML binary's `home_screen` changes from `"main"` (mini-hub) to `"codec_hub"` (operations directly). This is the fix for the noncompliance.

- Every spoke binary gains a `config` subcommand for free (from `lamquant-config::cli`), restricted to its own section.

- The hub's registry (`registry.rs`) gains install-source entries for every public spoke. The install flow (C.2, currently deferred) becomes the primary way to add spokes.

- `lamquant-tui` and `lamquant-config` are publishable to crates.io (no path deps to submodules). Spoke binaries can `cargo install` from git without the meta-repo.

## Related Decisions

- ADR 0025 (LML wire format + tool registry — the `registry.rs` + `InstallSource` dependency-confusion protection this builds on)
- ADR 0034 (BLUT scope charter — BLUT remains a subprocess spoke, not embedded)
- ADR 0019 (firmware targets — the `flash` spoke's target definitions)

## Validation

- `lml` (no args) opens directly to codec operations, not a mini-hub.
- `lml` standalone creates `~/.config/lamquant/lamquant.toml` with `[core]` + `[lml]` sections.
- Installing `flash` appends `[firmware]` section, preserves `[lml]` settings.
- Installing `lamquant` fills all missing sections with defaults, preserves changed settings.
- Corrupt TOML triggers recovery dialog, not crash.
- Unknown TOML sections/keys survive round-trip (load → save → load).
- Comments in TOML survive programmatic saves.
- `lml config set firmware.probe jlink` is rejected with a clear error.
- Hub tile grid shows all known spokes with ✅/❌ status.
- No spoke crate imports ratatui (except through `lamquant-tui`).

# ADR 0054: Warplan — beat ITU-T H.BWC on its own datasets and metrics

## Status

**In Progress** (Proposed 2026-06-20)

(Living campaign ADR. Tracks the sequenced plan to win head-to-head against
H.BWC, the battlefronts, and live progress. Strategy = ADR 0051; codec
architecture = ADR 0052. This ADR is the *campaign* that wields them. Update the
Progress section as work lands; flip to Accepted only when the win condition is
measured.)

## Context

ADR 0051 chose the **head-to-head rival** posture against ITU-T H.BWC
(Sullivan / Fraunhofer-HHI / Dolby; EEG/ECG/EMG; nine working points WP0 lossless
+ WP1–WP8 BPS-capped, minimizing PRD; metrics MAE/PRD/CPRD/PSNR; all test data in
EDF, public). ADR 0052 organized the deterministic codec into two formats (LML
floor / LMO ceiling) over three profiles (Firmware / Desktop / Optimum).

The benchmark harness (`tools/hbwc_bench/`) is built and has run against the
**real Fraunhofer BWC reference EncoderApp v5.0** on real signals. The honest
scoreboard today:

- **WP0 lossless (BPS, lower better):** EEG +1.6% (synthetic) / **+21%** (real
  CHB-MIT); ECG **+37%** behind HHI.
- **WP1–WP8 lossy (PRD %, lower better):** HHI wins **every** working point.
  WP2: ours 5.8% vs HHI 1.3% (**4.5×**); WP5: 20.8% vs 4.0%; WP8: 39.0% vs 13.6%.
- **Diagnosis (P3.5):** the **entropy lever is spent** — order-1 context
  arithmetic gained ~nothing over order-0 because the LPC stage already removes
  the inter-sample correlation context would exploit. The 4.5× gap lives in the
  **transform + rate–distortion allocation**:
  - 3-level Le Gall 5/3 lifting vs HHI's deeper/better transform;
  - coarse global-scale binary search vs true Lagrangian per-subband PCRD-opt;
  - uniform deadzone quant vs RD-optimized quantization.

We are at WP0-parity-ish on EEG, behind on ECG, and behind across all lossy
working points. The gap is **deterministic DSP work**, not entropy coding and not
the (unvalidated, off-critical-path) neural lossy.

## Decision

Run a focused campaign to **match-or-beat H.BWC at WP0–WP8 on its own datasets
(MUSC EEG-41, MIT-BIH ECG-48, Mendeley sEMG-40), measured by its own metrics**,
by building the **Optimum/LMO codec** (ADR 0052) and pouring effort into the
**transform + R-D allocation** where the bench says the gap is. The campaign is
all-deterministic and independent of the neural lossy.

**The win is fought on four battlefronts:**

1. **WP0 lossless ratio.** Close EEG +21% and ECG +37%. Levers: LMO's deeper
   transform; an ECG **periodicity-aware long-lag / pitch predictor** on top of
   LPC (ECG's QRS quasi-periodicity is exactly what HHI exploits and our EEG-tuned
   pipeline misses); better residual entropy coding in the LMO format (free to use
   rANS/arithmetic directly since LMO has no MCU-decode constraint).
2. **WP1–WP8 lossy PRD.** Close the 4.5× gap. Levers: true **Lagrangian
   per-subband PCRD** allocation replacing the coarse global-scale search; **RD-
   optimized quantization** replacing uniform deadzone; a deeper / better
   transform. This is LMO's core mandate.
3. **The embedded + permissive wedge** (ADR 0051's durable differentiator). Keep
   LamQuant uniquely **bit-exact on $5 silicon** (RP2350, LML floor) and
   MIT/Apache, where H.BWC will be a RAND spec whose reference software is
   unlikely to ship a 512 KB-SRAM MCU implementation. The LML floor is the moat;
   LMO is the ratio attack.
4. **The NWB flank H.BWC ignores** (ADR 0051 track 3). Registered HDF5
   compression-filter plugin + NWB `ElectricalSeries` reader/writer, host-only —
   own the AI/BCI research segment the DICOM-framed standard is not targeting.

**Win condition (ADR 0051 revisit trigger, made the campaign goal):** LamQuant
within **~5% PRD of the H.BWC anchor at clinically-relevant working points
(≈WP3–WP5)**, **WP0 matched-or-beaten** on EEG and ECG, with all numbers
published in `docs/TRUTH_LEDGER.md`. Hitting it reopens the *contribute-the-
embedded-reference-to-the-standard* path (ADR 0051's fourth option); falling far
short means leaning harder on the embedded + NWB flank.

## Campaign phases

- **Attack where the bench says the gap is.** The P3.5 finding is decisive:
  entropy coding is exhausted, so effort goes to transform + R-D allocation

- **The reorg is a prerequisite, not a tax.** LMO needs a home where float / heavy
  DSP can't threaten the silicon-proven LML floor (ADR 0052). Phases 1–2 buy that
  cleanly and are no-regret.
- **Measure on their turf or the claim is empty** (ADR 0051). Every phase feeds
  `docs/TRUTH_LEDGER.md`; the campaign is end-to-end-numbers-only.
- **The moat and the attack are different artifacts.** LML (silicon + permissive)
  is defensible regardless of the ratio race; LMO is the offensive ratio play.
  Decoupling them means a stalled Phase 3/4 never endangers the shipped floor.
