# ADR 0079: Symmetric P2P mesh — every host is server, worker, and (optionally) scheduler

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite earlier text. When the deliverable passes its gate, fill
> **Completion** and set Status to `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Status

Proposed 2026-07-07. Part 2 (the distributed spine) of the "BLUT real-tool"
roadmap (`~/.claude/plans/dazzling-mixing-haven.md`), tracked as ADR 0067
**Tier 4** slices A1–A6. Supersedes the **hub-and-spoke topology** of ADR 0061;
everything else in 0061 (the trust matrix, Ed25519 identity, QUIC/TLS
transport, X25519 blob sealing, zero-trust content verification, and the
clinical hard-block) **survives unchanged**.

## Context

ADR 0061 shipped a working, secure P2P compute plane, but it is structurally
**hub-and-spoke**: a single `Coordinator` is "the single point of control";
roles are chosen at the CLI (`blut p2p serve` = coordinator, `blut p2p connect`
= worker); the QUIC transport uses **uni-directional streams in a fixed
direction per role** (workers only send `Handshake`/`Result`/`Error`, only the
coordinator sends `Task`/`Cancel`); TLS pins **only the client's view of the
server** (`with_no_client_auth` on the server side, so a peer's identity is
self-asserted in the handshake and auto-added to the registry as `Anonymous`);
and peer discovery is a hand-edited static `peers.json`.

The roadmap's vision — "every host able to run as a server or a single node" —
needs a **symmetric mesh**: any node can dispatch to, and accept work from, any
other. The hub-and-spoke shape blocks that in four concrete ways (mutual auth,
bidirectional streams, dual-role process, discovery), and it widens the attack
surface if lifted naively (an unauthenticated inbound peer writing into every
node's registry; `Restricted`/clinical data routing depending on each node's
local hand-edited trust file).

## Decision

Make the node the unit, not the role. A single process — `blut p2p node` — is a
QUIC **server + worker + optional scheduler**, all at once. "Coordinator"
becomes a **capability** (`scheduler`) any node may enable; the existing
`Coordinator` struct survives as that scheduler component *inside* a node. Six
independently-shippable slices, each loopback-testable behind the existing
`p2p` feature:

- **A1 — Mutual TLS pinning.** The server side gains a client-cert verifier
  that extracts the Ed25519 SPKI from the presented self-signed cert (reusing
  the already-tested webpki extraction) and **binds PeerId to the TLS
  identity** — killing the self-asserted-identity hole. The client presents its
  identity cert. A Hello whose claimed identity ≠ its cert identity is refused.
  Compat: a `--allow-legacy-peers` flag accepts no-client-cert connections for
  one release.
- **A2 — Symmetric wire protocol.** A `MeshFrame` envelope (versioned) carried
  on `open_bi()` request/response streams replaces the role-locked uni-stream
  pairs. Hello carries a `protocol_version`; v1 peers keep the uni-stream path.
- **A3 — `blut p2p node`.** `MeshNode` binds the server, dials seeds, and runs a
  select-loop over {inbound connections, outbound peer maintenance, local
  dispatch}. Capabilities `{worker, scheduler}` default both true. The
  scheduler capability wraps the existing dispatch-matrix / reputation /
  `DispatchSubmitter` logic verbatim — only connection ownership moves into the
  node. `serve`/`connect` become deprecated thin wrappers.
- **A4 — Signed registry + introductions.** `peers.json` entries gain a
  self-signature (tamper-evident; invalid entries dropped fail-closed). A
  signed `Introduction { introducer, subject, max_trust, expires_at, sig }` lets
  a Trusted node vouch for a peer — but **only up to `Registered`**; promotion
  to `Trusted` stays an operator-CLI decision. Expiry is mandatory.
- **A5 — Discovery.** Static `--seed` list first (persisted), then a periodic
  signed `PeerExchange` gossip (A4 makes it safe: receivers verify
  self-signatures and admit peers as `Anonymous`, subject to the fail-closed
  dispatch matrix). mDNS is explicitly deferred — gossip over the authenticated
  mesh covers the WAN case; mDNS only helps LANs.
- **A6 — Mutual reputation.** Workers also score schedulers (verified
  result-ack, abusive cancel) via the existing local EMA, so "whom to accept
  work from" uses the same signal as "whom to dispatch to".

### What stays (from ADR 0061)

The **trust matrix** (`DataClass × TrustLevel`, fail-closed to `Restricted`),
Ed25519 identity, QUIC/TLS 1.3 transport, per-blob X25519 sealing, zero-trust
`blake3(output) == expected` verification, and the **clinical hard-block**
(weights + gradients never leave a node for `Restricted`/PHI data; training
stays local) are unchanged. A symmetric mesh does not relax any of them — it
extends them to be enforced *in both directions*.

### Reputation stays local-only (rejected alternative)

Each node keeps its **own** EMA of every peer it has dispatched to or served —
there is no gossiped, global reputation. A shared reputation number is a Sybil-
laundering vector (a ring of colluding nodes upvotes a bad actor), and it makes
`Restricted` routing depend on a value the local operator didn't set. Trust
decisions stay local; introductions (A4) propagate *identity + a capped vouch*,
not a reputation score.

## Non-goals / stays forbidden

- **No in-engine HTTP server** (ADR 0034). The mesh is QUIC; the cloud-worker's
  REST API stays in `crates/blut-worker`, outside `blut/src`.
- **No transitive `Trusted`.** An introduction can only reach `Registered`;
  clinical-data routing requires an operator-set `Trusted`.
- **No global reputation** (see above).
- **No relaxation of the clinical hard-block.** Symmetry is about *who can talk
  to whom*, never about *what data may leave a box*.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep hub-and-spoke, add HA to the coordinator (Raft).** Rejected for the
  mesh goal — it hardens the single point of control rather than removing it;
  HA coordinator is a separate, later concern (ADR 0067 T3.4).
- **Gossiped global reputation.** Rejected — Sybil laundering (above).
- **mDNS as the primary discovery.** Rejected as primary — LAN-only; the
  authenticated gossip generalizes. Kept as a possible later LAN convenience.

## Consequences

- Server-side client-cert verification is new attack surface reviewed under A1;
  the `--allow-legacy-peers` escape hatch is time-boxed to one release.
- The mesh is validatable on localhost (three `MeshNode`s, any-to-any dispatch)
  for every slice except the final two-machine confirmation, which is
  network-gated like ADR 0067 T2.3.

## Anti-re-litigation clause

This ADR does not reopen ADR 0061's clinical hard-block or its trust-matrix /
crypto choices, nor ADR 0034's HTTP-server ban. A future proposal to gossip
reputation, to allow transitive `Trusted`, or to move gradients for
`Restricted` data must supersede this ADR (and, for the last, ADR 0080)
explicitly with new evidence.

## Progress Log

- 2026-07-07 — ADR written. Implementation sequenced as Part 2 Phase D2 slices
  A1–A6; the shared data plane (chunk dedup/resume + object store) it and the
  operator both build on is Phase D1. Each slice lands with a loopback test and
  appends here.

## Completion

_Loopback/CI cores are LANDED (2026-07-07): A1–A6 + registry apply + `blut p2p
node` + the deduped/resumable transfer, all in `cargo test --features p2p` (823
tests). Hardware sign-off pending — see **`docs/tier4-hardware-validation.md`
Gate M** (two real hosts running `blut p2p node`, any-to-any dispatch, resume/
dedup byte counts). Fill this section + freeze when Gate M passes._

# ADR 0080: Async distributed training with differential privacy (FedAvg + DP-SGD)

> **This file is append-only and living.** Append dated Progress-Log entries as
> implementation proceeds; fill **Completion** and set Status to
> `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD` when the deliverable passes its gate.

## Status

Proposed 2026-07-07. Part 2 (the distributed spine) of the "BLUT real-tool"
roadmap, tracked as ADR 0067 **Tier 4** slices C1–C5. Supersedes ADR 0061's
"gradients never cross the wire" fence **for `Public`/`Internal` data only** —
`Restricted`/PHI stays local-only, differential privacy or not.

## Context

ADR 0061 forbade model weights and gradient state from leaving a node, enforced
by the dispatch matrix ("training → always local"), and explicitly deferred
"Hivemind-style async gradient averaging over the internet" as "a future
extension (**requires differential privacy**), not part of this ADR." The
roadmap wants that async-training capability: a network of nodes training a
shared model without pooling raw data.

The codebase already carries an **unwired** FedAvg reference module
(`codec-neural/.../decoder/federated.py` — `FederatedServer`/`FederatedClient`
with an ad-hoc DP-noise knob, marked "post-launch", imported by nothing). This
ADR productionizes it *behind a fail-closed privacy gate*, over the existing
P2P data plane.

The load-bearing constraint remains ADR 0061's clinical hard-block: EEG is PHI
under HIPAA. So this ADR does **not** unlock async training universally — it
unlocks it for **non-clinical** corpora, with mandatory DP, and keeps clinical
data local.

## Decision

Add **asynchronous federated training** (FedAvg with client-side DP-SGD) over
the symmetric mesh (ADR 0079), gated fail-closed by data class and a privacy
budget. Five slices (ADR 0067 C1–C5):

- **C1 — Privacy ledger + dispatch gate (the brake, built first).** A
  `PrivacyLedger` (per-corpus ε budget/spent, append-only and Ed25519-signed so
  it is tamper-evident) with an `admit(cost)` that refuses over-budget. The
  dispatch policy gains a `carries_gradients` flag; the verdict is **Deny**
  unless `data_class ∈ {Public, Internal} ∧ a DP config is present ∧ the ledger
  admits`. `Restricted ∧ carries_gradients` is a **hard Deny** citing this ADR.
  Fail-closed default: unknown gradient-bearing status ⇒ treated as carrying
  gradients.
- **C2 — Fed round protocol.** An initiator-side round driver: seal the global
  weights per participant (the existing X25519 blob path), dispatch N
  local-train tasks via the existing `DispatchSubmitter` seam, collect signed
  delta results, hash-verify them, and hand deltas to the Python aggregator.
  **Aggregation always runs on the initiator.** Straggler policy:
  `min_clients` + a round deadline; late updates dropped and reputation-scored.
- **C3 — Opacus DP-SGD + fed stages.** Replace `federated.py`'s ad-hoc post-hoc
  noise with a real Opacus `PrivacyEngine` local fine-tune (per-sample gradient
  clipping + calibrated noise) that emits an RDP-accounted `(ε, δ)` in its
  result JSON for the Rust ledger. Two content-addressed cookbook stages —
  `fed-local-train` (worker) and `fed-aggregate` (initiator).
- **C4 — Rounds as dynamic DAG nodes.** A `fed_round(...)` helper (built on the
  ADR 0078 `map_output` fan-out) expands to fan-out(`fed-local-train` × N) →
  `fed-aggregate`; the round loop is dynamic-DAG generation terminated by a
  convergence metric or ledger budget. Resume replays to the last completed
  aggregate via the existing resume path (each aggregate's output is a round
  artifact).
- **C5 — Hardware-gated validation.** A real multi-node DP round + a
  utility-vs-ε curve on a real decoder corpus. C1–C4 are CPU/loopback pure
  software.

### Hard invariants (fail-closed)

1. `DataClass::Restricted` gradient / delta / weight-derived artifacts **never
   dispatch** — no DP override. (HIPAA; ADR 0061 clinical block.)
2. **Ledger exhaustion is a hard stop**, not a warning — a round that would
   exceed the corpus ε budget is refused.
3. Global weights are **X25519-sealed per recipient**; updates are
   Ed25519-signed and content-verified like every other task result.
4. Aggregation runs **only on the initiating node**.
5. DP is **mandatory** for any gradient-bearing dispatch: `noise_multiplier == 0`
   is rejected in both the Python trainer and the Rust ledger.

### ε accounting lives in Python, enforcement in Rust

Opacus's RDP accountant is the source of truth for the per-round ε cost; the
Rust ledger **stores and enforces** the accounted numbers (charter: delegate
the verb — DP math — to the domain layer; the engine owns the gate). Rust never
reimplements DP math.

## Non-goals / stays forbidden

- **No async training for `Restricted` data**, ever, DP or not (invariant 1).
- **No server-side DP or secure-aggregation** in v1 — deltas carry an
  honor-plus-signature DP attestation (a malicious worker could under-noise); a
  cryptographic secure-aggregation protocol is a documented later extension.
- **No gradient exchange without a ledger admission** (invariant 2).

## Alternatives considered

- **Hivemind-style DHT gradient averaging.** Rejected for v1 — no per-corpus ε
  accounting, no data-class gate; it is the exact "internet async averaging"
  0061 fenced.
- **Server-side DP (noise added at the aggregator).** Rejected — it trusts the
  aggregator with raw gradients; client-side DP-SGD bounds each participant's
  contribution before it leaves the box.
- **Trust-based (no DP) async for `Internal`.** Rejected — DP is the roadmap's
  stated precondition for gradients on the wire; making it optional invites a
  slow slide to un-noised gradient sharing.

## Consequences

- The unwired `federated.py` becomes a real, gated code path; `opacus` joins the
  cookbook's Python deps.
- DP attestation being honor+signature is a known limitation, documented; it is
  acceptable for a Trusted-peer mesh and is the seam a future secure-aggregation
  protocol closes.
- C4 depends on the ADR 0078 `map_output` primitive (now shipped).

## Anti-re-litigation clause

This ADR does not reopen ADR 0061's clinical hard-block. A future proposal to
move gradients for `Restricted` data, to make DP optional, or to aggregate off
the initiator must supersede this ADR explicitly with new evidence (e.g. a
validated secure-aggregation protocol + a regulatory analysis).

## Progress Log

- 2026-07-07 — ADR written. Implementation sequenced as Part 2 Phase D4 slices
  C1–C5; C4 builds on the ADR 0078 `map_output` fan-out (shipped 2026-07-07).
  Each slice lands with tests and appends here.

## Completion

_C1–C4 are LANDED (2026-07-07): the `PrivacyLedger` + fail-closed gate,
`finalize_round`, real Opacus DP-SGD (`federated.py`/`fed_stages.py`), and the
`fed_round` Starlark builtin — in `cargo test --features p2p --lib p2p::privacy
p2p::fedround` + the cookbook `test_federated.py`/`test_fed_stages.py`. C5
(hardware) pending — see **`docs/tier4-hardware-validation.md` Gate D**
(multi-node round + ε-vs-utility curve, exhaustion + Restricted-denial spot
checks, kill/resume). Fill this section + freeze when Gate D passes._

# ADR 0081: Vertically-integrated training memory footprint (deterministic estimation over calibrate-and-retry)

> **This file is append-only and living.** Append dated Progress-Log entries as
> implementation proceeds; fill **Completion** and set Status to
> `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD` when the deliverable passes its gate.

## Status

Proposed 2026-07-08, prompted directly by a live incident (see Context). Builds
on the broker footprint/containment work (ADR 0046/0047: `FootprintSource`
calibration ladder `Default < Measured < OomCorrected`, cgroup `memory.max` as
the never-OOM-the-box backstop). Not yet implemented.

## Context

Launching the `codec_sweep_eeg_limits` campaign (`lamquant_joint_codec`, tier-4,
e1 preset, full-residual `detail_bands=all`) on 2026-07-07/08 cost three
consecutive OOM-kills across ~20 minutes before the run trained cleanly:

1. Admission auto-tuned decode workers to 5 ("fit 45G available"), the run
   OOM-killed at 42.4G peak. The broker recorded an `OomCorrected` lower bound
   and retried.
2. Same worker count, OOM-killed again at 41.8G peak — a *smaller* number than
   the first kill, which looked like the self-reinforcing-tightness bug this
   project hit once before (an OOM'd run's clamped peak becoming the next
   cap, biasing tighter every cycle). It wasn't that bug: the persisted
   calibration store correctly took the max across samples; the apparent
   shrinkage was admission's own cap computation reacting to slightly less
   available RAM at each attempt, not the calibration degrading.
3. Third kill, then admission correctly computed that the true peak needed
   ~49.2G, that the box only had ~43.8G free, and **refused to escalate
   further rather than OOM a fourth time** — the hard safety net worked
   exactly as designed. But it took three real, multi-minute training-process
   launches to discover empirically what was knowable in advance: the config
   (workers=5, tier=4, `detail_bands=all`, batch=8) does not fit this box.

Root-caused to four compounding gaps, none of them fundamental limits:

- **Three independent worker-count decisions.** Admission auto-tunes a decode
  worker count ("2 → 5", later "2 → 6"); `lamquant_warm_fb_cache` separately
  decides its own fork-pool size via `warm_workers`/`--workers`; and
  `lamquant_train_joint` reads `LMA_NUM_WORKERS` from `extra_env`, which
  admission also writes to *if the recipe hasn't already pinned it*. Sizing a
  footprint around a number that's decided three different, uncoordinated ways
  cannot be estimated accurately regardless of how good the per-worker
  constant is.
- **Fork+COW dataloader workers.** Each decode worker is a copy-on-write fork
  of the parent process; its real RSS growth is however many pages it happens
  to dirty, which depends on which windows it decodes and in what order — not
  a number knowable from the worker count alone.
- **A closed-form term folded into a generic heuristic.** SOAP's
  `eigh(max_precond_dim)` preconditioner memory is `O(d²)`–`O(d³)` in a config
  knob that's already known at launch time — it doesn't need estimating, it
  needs calculating, but today it's absorbed into the same per-worker
  `PREFETCH_PER_WORKER`/`PER_BATCH` constants that cover everything else.
- **No pre-flight measurement.** The system waits for a *real* training
  process to report a *real* peak (via clean exit or OOM-kill) rather than
  measuring the largely-deterministic chunk of the footprint — model
  parameters, optimizer state, activations — ahead of time. This chunk is
  more deterministic here than in most training pipelines: EEG windows are
  fixed-shape (2500 samples × 21/168 channels, always), so there is no
  variable-batch-shape variance to estimate around.

## Decision

Add a **pre-admission measurement pass** that vertically integrates the pieces
currently guessed at, so admission can *know* rather than *estimate* the
dominant terms of the footprint. The existing calibrate-and-retry system
(`FootprintSource`, cgroup `memory.max`) stays as the fallback safety net for
whatever residual slop remains — this ADR tightens the number that feeds
admission, it does not remove the guarantee that a wrong number can't take the
box down.

- **D1 — Unify the worker-count knob.** Admission decides the worker count
  exactly once per launch; `lamquant_warm_fb_cache` and `lamquant_train_joint`
  both read that single decision instead of each running their own
  auto-tune/default logic. Prerequisite for the rest of this ADR — there is no
  point precisely measuring a config whose actual worker count is still
  decided three different, potentially-disagreeing ways.
- **D2 — Dry-run / meta-tensor measurement for model + optimizer + activations.**
  Before admitting a real run, construct the same graph (encoder + decoder +
  optimizer state) at the target tier/latent_dim/batch_size — on meta tensors
  or via one throwaway forward+backward+`optimizer.step()` on synthetic data —
  and read the allocator's actual footprint. Deterministic given the fixed
  window shape; this is the single biggest lever.
- **D3 — Closed-form calculation for SOAP's `eigh(max_precond_dim)` term.**
  Compute its memory contribution directly from `max_precond_dim` instead of
  folding it into the generic per-worker constants.
- **D4 — Shared-memory-arena dataloader workers.** Replace fork+COW workers
  with workers spawned against a pre-sized shared-memory ring buffer (fixed to
  `batch_size × window_shape × dtype × prefetch_depth`), converting "however
  many pages get dirtied" into an enforced, exact bound.
- **D5 — Warm-up-then-measure for the CUDA/host allocator steady state.** Run
  one full-size throwaway batch through the real fwd/bwd/step path before
  admitting production data, and read `torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()` +
  host RSS at that point — tighter than a static estimate because it captures
  real allocator fragmentation/caching behavior instead of assuming it away.

Pilot on `lamquant_joint_codec` (the recipe that prompted this ADR) before
considering rollout to other recipes.

## Non-goals / stays forbidden

- **Not claiming byte-exact.** OS/cgroup page-cache accounting, allocator
  fragmentation drift over a long run, and leaked handles (this exact incident's
  log carried a real "21 leaked semaphore objects" warning) remain a residual.
  The target is collapsing multi-gigabyte surprises into low-hundreds-of-MB
  slop, not eliminating slop entirely.
- **Not removing the calibrate-and-retry safety net.** `FootprintSource`
  (`Default`/`Measured`/`OomCorrected`) and the cgroup `memory.max` hard cap
  stay as the backstop for residual slop and for any recipe not yet migrated
  to D1–D5.
- **Not a blanket rollout.** Scoped to `lamquant_joint_codec` first; other
  recipes keep today's calibrate-and-retry behavior until this pilot proves
  out.

## Alternatives considered

- **Status quo (calibrate + hard cap + retry only).** Cheap, already built,
  and the safety net genuinely held (the box never went down across three
  kills). Rejected as the *sole* mechanism because it wastes real box-time
  discovering empirically what D2/D3 could know in a fast dry-run — this
  incident cost ~20 minutes and three real process launches to learn "this
  config needs ~49G, the box has ~44G."
- **Bigger conservative safety margins on the existing heuristic.** Avoids
  OOM-cycling by over-estimating, but wastes admittable headroom (jobs that
  would actually fit get refused) and doesn't fix the root confusion — three
  independent worker-count decisions stay uncoordinated regardless of how
  padded the constant is.
- **Full offline profiling database** (measure every tier × latent_dim ×
  batch × detail_bands combination once, cache the results). More accurate
  than a static heuristic, but combinatorially expensive to build and
  maintain, and goes stale the moment training code changes. A per-launch
  dry-run (D2) measures fresh every time instead of trusting a cache that can
  silently drift from the code it's supposed to describe.

## Consequences

- Admission can catch a won't-fit config (like this incident's 49G-need vs.
  44G-available) in one fast dry-run instead of three real OOM-kill cycles.
- Real engineering investment required: a dry-run/meta-tensor harness, a
  shared-memory dataloader arena, a closed-form SOAP memory calculator, and
  worker-count-knob unification across three call sites — none of this exists
  today.
- D1 (unifying the worker knob) is a prerequisite for D2–D5 to mean anything;
  it should land first even if the measurement work is staged after.
- Recipes not migrated to D1–D5 are unaffected — they keep relying on
  `FootprintSource` calibration exactly as today.

## Anti-re-litigation clause

This ADR does not propose removing the cgroup `memory.max` backstop or the
`OomCorrected` calibration path — a future proposal to do so must supersede
this ADR explicitly with evidence that the residual slop after D1–D5 is
provably zero, not merely "usually small."

## Progress Log

- 2026-07-08 — ADR written, prompted by the `codec_sweep_eeg_limits` campaign
  incident (three OOM-kills, ~20 minutes, before admission correctly refused
  to escalate further). Not yet implemented.

## Completion

_Pending. D1 (worker-knob unification) should land first; D2–D5 build on it._

# ADR 0082 — BLUT cloud compute queue (object-store dispatch, billed on compute)

> **Renumbered 2026-07-09.** Drafted as ADR 0070 on the (now-deleted) branch
> `docs/cloud-adr-0070`; renumbered to 0082 because 0070 on `main` is the LMQ
> experiment ledger. Content otherwise verbatim from commit `a778b1ca`.

- **Status:** Proposed 2026-06-30 (v1 built + proven on `feat/cloud-queue`)
- **Extends:** ADR 0061 (P2P distributed compute — the data plane this reuses), ADR 0067
  (remaining-work catalogue · Tier-3)
- **Promotes:** `docs/proposals/blut-cloud-compute-queue.md` (the design, previously doc-only)

## Context

The vision's economic endgame: turn cloud GPU from "rent a server, set up an env, run,
tear down" into **"submit a job, get the result back," billed on compute** — because
every BLUT stage is already content-addressed + resource-typed (ADR 0061's cache is the
trust anchor; the P2P module extended it to the network).

Three ground-truth audits established that **a cloud queue is a transport swap on the
P2P data plane, not a redesign.** The artifact bundle (`p2p::bundle` — pack/unpack +
four fail-closed gates), the worker choreography (`p2p::peer_exec::execute_one`), the
dispatch trust matrix (`p2p::trust`), the content-addressed cache, and the file-backed
artifact handle contract are all **transport-agnostic and reused verbatim**. The only
P2P-specific piece is QUIC blob streaming (`p2p::transport`), whose object-store analog
is *simpler* (a plain put/get; no chunking). A full proposal existed but was doc-only —
zero cloud/S3 code in the tree.

## Decision

Build the cloud queue as **the P2P dispatch path with an object store in place of QUIC**,
behind a default-OFF `cloud` cargo feature (which implies `p2p`, reusing its data plane).
v1 (T3.1) ships:

- **Object-store transport** (`cloud::store::BlobStore` / `ObjStore`) over the
  `object_store` crate — one trait across the local filesystem + any S3-compatible store
  (AWS S3 / Cloudflare R2 / MinIO). Blobs are bundle packs keyed by `ContentHash`
  (idempotent puts; skippable downloads; `MAX_BLOB_SIZE` ceiling). **Dev-testable on the
  local filesystem with no cloud account**; a real provider is a config swap.
- **Leased priority queue** (`cloud::queue::CloudQueue` / `MemQueue`) — `CloudJob`/
  `CloudResult` records + a visibility-timeout lease with `reclaim_expired` (the
  durability `blut-worker`'s file queue lacked), priority-descending claim, and
  **lease-fenced `complete`** (only the current lease holder may finish a job).
- **Submitter + worker** (`cloud::submitter`, `cloud::worker`) — `dispatch_to_peer` /
  `execute_one` with `put_blob`/`get_blob` swapped for the QUIC blob streams. The four
  fail-closed bundle gates (incl. the bind to `expected_output_hash`) run unchanged; a
  wrong result is rejected exactly as in P2P. A claimed job is always completed (success
  OR failure), so a lease is never stranded.
- **Clinical hard-block** — cloud workers run at `Registered` trust, so the reused
  `DispatchMatrix` refuses `DataClass::Restricted` (PHI EEG). Only Public/Internal stages
  (preprocess/encode/eval/export — already the dispatch allowlist) leave the box; training
  never does.
- **Cost ledger** (`cloud::cost`) — `cost = f(ResourceRequest, wall_time_ms)` in abstract
  compute units, recorded per **successful** job after `complete` durably commits (the
  "billed on compute" property, end-to-end).
- **CLI** — `blut cloud smoke [--store <dir>] [--input <text>]` runs the whole data plane
  as one command (the turnkey demonstration + the MinIO/S3 smoke entry). `LaunchTarget::Cloud`
  is added as the user-facing selector; like P2P it side-steps `Launcher` (dispatch is the
  cloud submit path, not `srun`-style placement).

## Rationale

- **Mechanism B, not the blocking launcher.** Slurm/Ray (`Launcher::wrap`) assume a shared
  filesystem the cloud lacks. The async submit→poll→result seam (`DispatchSubmitter`/
  `DispatchHandle`) is the right shape; the P2P `Coordinator` is the worked example. v1's
  submitter mirrors `dispatch_to_peer` (driven by the CLI), exactly as P2P's own data plane
  runs through the CLI rather than the still-incomplete executor offload seam.
- **Reuse over reinvent.** The bundle's content-addressed verification is the integrity
  guarantee regardless of who delivered the bytes (a QUIC peer or an S3 GET), so the cloud
  worker is `execute_one` minus the transport. This keeps one audited data plane, not two.
- **Provider-agnostic + no-account dev loop.** Building on `object_store` + testing on the
  local filesystem means the entire queue is proven before any cloud spend — the same
  pattern that made FSDP/P2P turnkey before hardware.
- **Clinical-safe by construction.** Reusing the trust matrix means PHI EEG cannot reach a
  cloud worker without an explicit, later decision to vet + mark a provider `Trusted`.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Extend `blut-worker` into the queue.** Rejected as the base: its file-extension state
  machine is single-host with no lease/requeue, its API/worker state is desynced, and it
  ships no result-byte transport. We kept its `Job`/`JobResult` schema shape + recipe→DAG
  entrypoint and built the durable queue + data plane fresh.
- **Encrypt bundles at rest in v1.** Deferred to T3.2: v1's object store is
  operator-controlled and clinical data is hard-blocked, so content-addressed integrity +
  the trust gate suffice. Reusing `p2p::crypto` for at-rest sealing lands with untrusted
  multi-tenant providers.
- **The executor offload seam (`DispatchSubmitter`) for v1.** Deferred: `DispatchRequest`
  carries no artifact bytes (the same gap P2P has), so wiring it needs the producing
  stage_dir threaded through. v1 uses the explicit submit path; the seam is T3.2.

## Consequences

- One data plane, two transports (QUIC + object store), sharing `bundle`/`trust`/`cache`.
  A change to the bundle wire format or the gates must keep both in lock-step.
- `cloud` depends on `p2p` (the shared data plane); building cloud pulls the p2p deps.
- The fail-closed `expected_output_hash` model means v1 dispatches deterministic stages (or
  cache-verified re-execution); a "trust the worker's claimed hash for novel work" mode is
  a deliberate T3.2 addition.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract)*

- **Deliverable:** the `cloud` module + `blut cloud` CLI on `feat/cloud-queue` (engine).
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `cargo test -p blut --features cloud` + `cargo clippy -p blut --features cloud -- -D warnings` + default (no-cloud) build green.
  - `pass when:` `cloud_dispatch_round_trips_over_local_object_store` verifies `HELLO CLOUD`
    end-to-end; `restricted_job_is_refused_by_a_registered_cloud_worker` proves the
    clinical hard-block; the `blut cloud smoke` handler round-trips.
- **Rollback:** the `cloud` feature is default-OFF and additive; drop the feature.

## Progress Log  *(append-only)*

- _2026-06-30 — v1 built + proven (engine `feat/cloud-queue`)._ T3.1a object-store
  transport · T3.1b leased queue (lease-fenced complete) · T3.1c/d submitter+worker + the
  end-to-end loopback PROOF · T3.1e cost ledger · T3.1f `blut cloud smoke` CLI. 14 cloud
  unit + 2 integration + 3 CLI tests green; default build unaffected; every commit
  MiMo-reviewed. **Deferred to T3.2:** at-rest encryption, novel-work verification,
  multi-provider routing + cost-aware selection, preemption→resume (reuse `durable_resume`),
  the S3 cache tier, real $ pricing, vetting a provider `Trusted` to lift the clinical block.
- _2026-07-09 — **v1 LANDED on engine `main`** (`01a3ed7`; ADR renumbered 0070→0082 same
  day)._ Rebased across the Tier-4 spine (85 commits): `blut cloud` CLI ported to the
  `src/cli/` module split (`cli/cloud.rs`); `cloud` feature coexists with `s3`;
  `LaunchTarget::Cloud` joins `K8s`; `JobStatus::Done` boxed (clippy). 850 lib + 2
  integration tests green with `--features cloud`; `feat/cloud-queue` branch deleted.
  Trunk half of the Completion verdict is satisfied — remaining: a provider runs it live.
- _2026-08-17 — corrected the clippy leg of `gate_cmd`, which could never run._ It was
  written `cargo clippy --features cloud -D warnings`; cargo reads `-D warnings` as its
  own argument, not rustc's, and exits on the unknown flag before linting anything. The
  lint level has to cross the `--` boundary: `-- -D warnings`. `-p blut` is added for the
  same reason the sibling `cargo test` leg carries it — the engine is a submodule
  workspace, and without a package the gate resolves to the meta root, where `--features`
  is rejected outright. A wording fix, not a scope change: the leg asserted nothing
  before and asserts what it always claimed to now.

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill at freeze)*

- **verdict:** _pending_ (frozen when v1 lands on the engine trunk + a provider runs it live)
- **gate_cmd:** _see Implementation Plan_

## Related Decisions

ADR 0061 (P2P data plane — extended here), ADR 0067 (Tier-3 catalogue), ADR 0044 (BLUT API).

## Validation  *(ongoing)*

Wrong if: the cloud bundle path diverges from the P2P bundle gates (two data planes drift),
a `Restricted` job ever runs on a non-`Trusted` worker, or the cost ledger double-bills /
bills failed work. Any triggers a corrective Progress Log entry or a superseding ADR.

# ADR 0083 — BLUT interface stack: CLI engine, sidecar TUI/web crates, and the charter boundary

> **This file is append-only and living.** Append dated Progress-Log entries as
> implementation proceeds; fill **Completion** and set Status to
> `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD` when the deliverable passes its gate.

- **Status:** `Complete — frozen 2026-07-19` (M1 2026-07-12 → M2/M3 2026-07-19)
- **Extends:** ADR 0034 (scope charter — this ADR documents its sidecar boundary
  properly, replacing the one-liner in ADR 0079's Non-goals), ADR 0037 (cookbook
  architecture), ADR 0078 (out-of-process front-end precedent: `blut-dsl`)
- **Context:** the premier-heavyweight roadmap (plan
  `alright-i-want-you-abundant-island`, M1–M6). Locked user decisions: TUI-first;
  web = Leptos + WASM, Rust end-to-end; **UI and TUI in separate crates; the
  engine ships as the CLI tool**.

## Context

ADR 0034 forbids HTTP servers, GPU monitoring, plotting, log aggregation, and
process supervision inside the engine (`blut/src`) — but until today the ban was
enforced by convention (the guard script existed in the meta-repo and ran in no
CI), and the one legal exception (`crates/blut-worker`'s axum server) was
documented only as a one-line Non-goal in ADR 0079. Meanwhile the roadmap adds
two interface surfaces (a web dashboard, a notifier daemon) and splits the TUI
out of the engine — all of which need the boundary stated precisely, once.

## Decision

### 1. The charter boundary, stated precisely

**The unit of the charter is the engine source tree (`blut/src`), not the git
repository.** A *sidecar crate* — any crate under `crates/*` — may host servers,
HTTP clients, SMTP, or other delegated concerns, because it is a separate
process the operator opts into, supervised by systemd, that the engine never
links. The engine may `exec` a sidecar (dispatch, below); it must never embed
one.

Enforcement is now mechanical: `scripts/scope_guard.sh` (canonical copy beside
the source it guards; the meta-repo `tools/blut_scope_guard.sh` is a delegating
wrapper) runs as the first step of the engine CI's build-test-lint job. The
allowlist beside it distinguishes **permanent by-design exemptions** (the broker
admission probe, the containment ladder's `pre_exec` — each citing its ADR) from
**staged migrations** (citing the step that removes them).

### 2. Crate topology (end state, built across M1–M3)

```
blut-types      NEW   pure-serde wire types; wasm32-safe (serde + serde_json only)
   ↑        ↑
   |        |
 blut     blut-web/ui  NEW  Leptos+WASM CSR front-end
   ↑   ↑      ↑
   |   |      | (static bundle embedded via include_dir!)
   |  blut-tui  NEW  crates/blut-tui — console + cookbook-cockpit binary
   |
 blut-web    NEW  crates/blut-web — axum API host + webhook ingress, serves the UI
 blut-notify NEW  crates/blut-notify — status.jsonl tail → sinks + SLA rules
 blut-dsl, blut-operator   existing sidecars, unchanged
 blut-worker DEPRECATED    → deleted in M3 (superseded by src/cloud + blut-web)
```

- **`blut-types` is the keystone**: `StageEvent`/`HostedEvent`, the PlanSpec IR,
  `SensorOutcome`, lineage rows — data types only, `serde`+`serde_json` as the
  only mandatory deps. The engine re-exports them at their old paths (no
  downstream churn). CI carries a required
  `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p blut-types` job from day one —
  the Rust-end-to-end premise of the web UI depends on this staying green.
- **`blut-tui`** takes `src/tui/` (~6.5k LOC) as the `blut-tui` binary. The
  `CookbookTui` trait STAYS in the engine (cookbooks compile against `blut`),
  behind a `tui-api` feature carrying only the trait definitions + ratatui
  types. Ratatui is pinned `=x.y` in lockstep between the two crates; the trait
  surface is frozen by this ADR (changes require a Progress-Log entry).
- **`blut-web`** hosts the axum API (read paths serve exactly the artifacts the
  TUI reads: status.jsonl, lineage SQLite, PeerRegistry, PrivacyLedger) and the
  embedded Leptos bundle. One binary, zero deploy steps.
- **`blut-notify`** tails status.jsonl and routes rule matches to sinks
  (webhook / SMTP / exec); SLA rules live in its engine-readable rule file so
  `blut sla check` (a pure lineage-db read in the engine — charter-fine) gives
  the TUI and CI the same answers.

### 3. CLI dispatch: cargo-style external subcommands

`blut <cmd>` falls through to `exec`ing `blut-<cmd>` from `PATH` when `<cmd>` is
not built in: `blut tui` → `blut-tui`, `blut web` → `blut-web`,
`blut notify` → `blut-notify`. This is `exec`, not process supervision
(charter-safe); it keeps "the main engine ships as the CLI tool" literally true;
and it makes every future sidecar free to add. (~80 LOC in `src/cli/mod.rs`.)

### 4. Live control: the exec bridge

Mutating web endpoints never reach into engine internals — they shell out to the
CLI (`blut run …` spawned detached via `systemd-run --user`; the existing
`blut cancel <id> --grace`). One enforcement path for human and API; the
user-action audit log (`~/.blut/audit.jsonl`, M4) wraps the bridge in one place.
Retry = re-launch — the content-addressed cache makes completed nodes free, which
is the honest semantics.

- _2026-07-19 — M2 INCREMENT 1 LANDED (engine `3b81dbe`): `crates/blut-web`,
  the read-only web sidecar._ Standalone-workspace axum binary (engine
  path-dep; the engine never links it; reached as `blut web` via the M1
  dispatch). Serves the TUI's stores as JSON: jobs, bounded status.jsonl
  tails, lineage graphs (JSON/DOT), model cards, run diffs, model-registry
  pointers+history. Custody fail-closed: `EXPORT_EXCLUDES_RESTRICTED` is a
  constant `true` with a tripwire test (ADR 0061); shared-tenant-only registry;
  ADR-0095 bearer-token auth; a non-loopback bind WITHOUT a token store is
  refused. CI gate added. Live-smoked on the box (real jobs served, 404s,
  0.0.0.0 refusal). 5/5 tests, clippy 0. REMAINING M2/M3: the exec bridge
  (mutations via rbac::enforce → the CLI), the embedded Leptos+WASM bundle
  (shares the blut-types wire types these endpoints serve), the blut-tui
  extraction, blut-worker deletion._

- _2026-07-19 — M2 COMPLETE + M3 DELETION (engine `0bc653d` → `2724ec9`;
  backends `bd4facf`; cookbook `ae7faf4`). Four landings:_
  1. **The exec bridge (incr 2, `0bc653d`)** — `POST /api/jobs` (run) +
     `POST /api/jobs/{id}/cancel`: `rbac::enforce` (Operator floor, shared
     tenant only, allow AND deny audited to `audit.jsonl` BEFORE dispatch,
     audit-write failure = deny) → shell out to the CLI (`--cli` names the
     cookbook binary; args travel as ONE argv element, spawn detached with a
     launch log). No token store ⇒ mutations denied even on loopback. One
     enforcement path for human and API — §4 exactly as written.
  2. **The blut-tui extraction (`5f43ce8`)** — `src/tui/` (~7.5k LOC) →
     `crates/blut-tui` (standalone workspace; lib + `blut-tui` binary). The
     engine ships ZERO terminal-UI deps (ratatui/crossterm/fuzzy-matcher gone,
     `tui` feature deleted, default = []). Seam: `cli::TuiHook` (two plain fn
     pointers) + `run_with_tui` — a cookbook binary passes `blut_tui::hook()`
     and bare invocation opens the console over its live registry; a hookless
     binary's `tui` subcommand execs `blut-tui` from PATH via the M1 dispatch.
     Per the 2026-07-12 correction, NO ratatui type crosses the engine
     boundary (`CookbookTui` unchanged), so the ratatui `=x.y` lockstep pin is
     moot — the engine has no ratatui to lock against. Cookbook flipped
     (`ae7faf4`): `lqt tui --check` renders 14 views + 8 tabs + 4 overlays
     through the hook; live dry-run resolves the identical 40.0G (ADR 0133
     store continuity intact across the move).
  3. **The embedded Leptos+WASM dashboard (incr 3, `198d7ef`)** — the gate
     line is TRUE: `blut web` serves the dashboard from one binary. Leptos 0.8
     CSR app (`crates/blut-web/ui`): jobs table → status tail + cancel, a
     recipe launcher through the exec bridge, lineage graph/card panels —
     deserializing the wasm-safe `blut-types` wire types the endpoints emit
     (the keystone premise, closed). Bundled by `scripts/build_ui.sh` (cargo
     wasm32 + wasm-bindgen pinned `=0.2.126`; trunk rejected — its
     libdeflate-sys build breaks here), staged by build.rs into the binary via
     `include_dir!` (428K; a self-describing stub page when unbuilt, so
     API-only builds still serve "/"). Static shell unauthenticated; ALL data
     via the token-gated `/api`. CI: wasm32 fmt+clippy gate for the ui crate.
  4. **blut-worker DELETED (M3, `2724ec9`)** — superseded by `src/cloud`
     (ADR 0082) + this stack; CI gate, deny line, release steps removed. Its
     sidecar precedent survives as this ADR.

## Consequences

- The engine's dependency tree gets *smaller* (ratatui/crossterm leave the
  default build in M1); the lean-CLI story becomes real.
- Two lockstep constraints appear: the ratatui `=x.y` pin (blut ↔ blut-tui) and
  the wasm32-cleanliness of `blut-types` (blut ↔ blut-web/ui). Both are CI-gated.
- `blut-worker` is deprecated now, deleted in M3 — its sidecar precedent is the
  only part that survives, as this ADR.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last)*

- _2026-07-09 — opened._ Same day: the scope guard moved to its canonical home
  (`training/engine/scripts/scope_guard.sh` + allowlist) and became the first
  step of the engine CI build-test-lint job — the charter is now enforced, not
  conventional. Four accumulated violations triaged into the allowlist with
  justifications (containment `pre_exec` ×2 → permanent by design, ADR 0046;
  nvidia-smi one-shot probes ×2 → consolidating into the ADR 0087 GPU-inventory
  seam). `crates/blut-worker` marked deprecated (README), deletion scheduled M3.
- _2026-07-12 — M1 LANDED (engine main `d66e87f`): the wasm32 keystone crate +
  the external-subcommand dispatch seam._ Two of this ADR's load-bearing pieces:
  1. **`crates/blut-types`** — the wasm32-SAFE keystone. The read-side lineage
     wire types (`ProvenanceGraph`/`ModelCard`/`RunDiff`/`CardContent`/`GraphNode`,
     ADR 0099) move here from `src/lineage_report.rs`; serde + serde_json are the
     only structural deps (sha2/faster-hex are pure-Rust hash helpers) — NO tokio,
     rusqlite, filesystem, or engine dep, so the Leptos+WASM `blut-web` sidecar can
     depend on it. **Zero downstream churn:** `src/lineage_report.rs` is now an
     EXPLICIT re-export (`pub use blut_types::report::{…}` — named, not a glob, so
     the keystone can't silently widen the engine's public API), so
     `crate::lineage_report::{…}` still resolves for `lineage_db` + the CLI.
  2. **External-subcommand dispatch** — `#[command(external_subcommand)]
     External(Vec<String>)`: `blut <cmd> <args…>` with no built-in match execs
     `blut-<cmd>` from PATH, forwarding args + propagating exit status/signal. This
     is the seam by which the sidecar binaries the engine deliberately never links
     (`blut-web`, `blut-notify`, eventually `blut-tui`) become first-class `blut`
     subcommands — no in-process server, no dylib loader (ADR 0034). Fail-closed:
     the name is ALLOWLISTED (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, cargo's `cargo-<cmd>` convention) so
     no path/escape/separator can reach outside the `blut-*` family; a missing
     sidecar is a hard error naming the binary, never a silent no-op.
  3. **CI gate `wasm32-keystone`** — `cargo check -p blut-types --target
     wasm32-unknown-unknown` + host tests. Fail-closed guard: a PR that adds a
     non-wasm dep to `blut-types` breaks here before it can reach main.
  Gate part: `cargo test -p blut-types` = 4 passed (incl DOT node-ID/edge escape),
  `cargo test -p blut external_subcommand` = 3 passed (traversal-reject, empty-argv,
  missing-sidecar), `--test lineage_graph_card_diff` = 5 passed (re-export intact);
  full suite green (`-j 2`); clippy 0; fmt clean; scope_guard PASS; blut-types
  wasm32 check green. MiMo: DOT-injection fix (escape node IDs + edge endpoints, not
  just labels) + allowlist-over-blocklist applied; `CardContent`-missing finding was
  a verified FALSE POSITIVE (it is the first item in the re-export list; suite
  compiled green). **REMAINING (M2/M3):** the `blut-tui` / `blut-web` (Leptos+WASM
  dashboard reading the lineage/partition tables) / `blut-notify` sidecar crates;
  deleting `crates/blut-worker`. ADR stays In progress until `blut web` serves the
  dashboard from one binary.
- _2026-07-12 — INTERFACE CONTRACT CORRECTION (owner-locked)._ A cookbook's
  bespoke TUI is **not** a BLUT widget framework and is not required to use
  BLUT-owned Ratatui components. The current `CookbookTui` surface is deliberately
  small, object-safe discovery/lifecycle glue (`label`, `about`, and `run` with
  the live `Arc<Registry>`); it exposes no Ratatui widget or event-loop types.
  A cookbook may implement a normal Ratatui application with its own component
  model, or launch an arbitrary sidecar binary, own the terminal while active,
  and return control when it exits. The generic BLUT console is an optional
  fallback for cookbooks without a bespoke TUI. Therefore the earlier proposed
  `tui-api` feature carrying Ratatui types and a lockstep Ratatui API surface is
  not the controlling contract; keep launch/status/control messages stable, not
  cookbook UI implementation internals. Execution order is also corrected:
  finish engine software before starting the web tier. ADR remains In progress._

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill at freeze)*

- **verdict:** passed
- **gate_cmd:** engine CI green with the scope-guard step + the wasm32
  `blut-types` check; `blut tui` opens via external-subcommand dispatch;
  `blut web` serves the dashboard from one binary.
- **result:** all three hold — scope_guard PASS + wasm32 gates in CI (now
  incl. the blut-web-ui wasm32 lint + the blut-tui sidecar gate); the `tui`
  subcommand routes to the sidecar (in-process via `TuiHook` for cookbook
  binaries — `lqt tui --check` 14 views/8 tabs/4 overlays; PATH exec for
  hookless binaries via the M1 dispatch, dispatch tests green); the embedded
  dashboard live-smoked from one binary (shell 200, 392K wasm
  `application/wasm`, `/api` coexisting, 404s). Engine 762 + web 10 + tui 76
  + backends 93 + cookbook suites all green; clippy 0 everywhere.
- **shas:** engine `2724ec9` (bridge `0bc653d`, extraction `5f43ce8`,
  dashboard `198d7ef`, worker deletion `2724ec9`) · backends `bd4facf` ·
  cookbook `ae7faf4`.

## Related Decisions

ADR 0034 (charter), 0037 (cookbooks), 0078 (out-of-process front-ends), 0079
(the superseded one-liner), 0082 (cloud queue — retires blut-worker's queue),
0084–0091 (the roadmap ADRs that build on this stack).

## Validation  *(ongoing)*

Wrong if: any `crates/*` code gets linked into the engine binary (the boundary
is process, not repo), the scope guard is removed/skipped in CI, `blut-types`
grows a non-serde mandatory dep, or a mutating web endpoint bypasses the exec
bridge (two enforcement paths would drift).

- **result:** all three hold — scope_guard PASS + wasm32 gates in CI (now
  incl. the blut-web-ui wasm32 lint + the blut-tui sidecar gate); the `tui`

# ADR 0084 — Cross-channel joint coding: the measured frontier, and the learned-joint-entropy commitment

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-07-09
- **Extends:** ADR 0064 (beat-H.BWC warplan + spatial-decorrelation frontier), ADR 0054 (three-tier lossless / Optimum keep-best), ADR 0063 (physics-honest high-freq), ADR 0062 (H.BWC patent posture — oracle, never a dep)
- **Records (so it cannot drift):** the *measured* localization of the residual H.BWC gap to cross-channel joint structure; the retirement of the entire fixed-transform family (cosine/wavelet/KLT/best-basis) and of block-matching; the head-to-head cross-channel second-stage A/B (ALS-MCC vs rate-gated-difference vs spatial-LS) with its per-recording win/loss map; and the decision to route the remaining headroom to a **learned joint entropy model** (LMQ thread), not another linear stage.
- **Numbering note:** `0082–0091` were provisionally reserved for the BLUT premier roadmap; this codec ADR takes `0084` as the next free integer. Renumber on commit if it collides — the digest keys on filename (ADR 0064 precedent).

## Context

ADR 0064 left the campaign at a clean frontier: every *single-channel* deterministic lever
(prediction, transform, entropy coding) was at or near its floor, and the two patent-clean
**spatial** shots (cross-channel LS predict-then-wavelet, KLT rotation) had both LOST to the
**cascade penalty** — spatial decorrelation cuts residual energy but flattens the intra-channel
spectrum the coder feeds on, so per-bit it loses. The open question: *where does the remaining gap to
H.BWC actually live, and is it concentrated or diffuse?*

This ADR records the campaign that answered it — a measurement-first arc, every step a committed probe
in `codec-lossless/lamquant-lml-optimum/examples/`:

1. **Fixed-transform family retired (measured).**
   - `best_basis_probe.rs` — per-block competition among predictor / DCT-II / 5/3 wavelet, rate-selected.
     On the referential lose-set the ceiling is ~0 (eegmmidb exactly 0.000% at every block size; siena
     ≤ −0.38% with the DCT proxy *inflated*). Wavelet never wins a block anywhere; DCT wins only on
     long-block (≥8 s) non-stationary cognitive data (`ma`) — recordings we don't need help on. The
     AR(1)↔1/f duality pins the whole fixed-basis family inside the −1.2…−1.9 % oracle headroom, which
     is **smaller than the referential gap** — so no fixed transform closes it. (Companion first-
     principles note: DCT ≈ KLT of AR(1) stationary rhythm; wavelet ≈ KLT of 1/f self-similar; EEG is a
     mixture, so neither dominates — and mv_rls already whitens both components.)
   - Block-matching / long-term prediction retired earlier in all three forms (cross-channel backward-
     adaptive LS +23 %; forward temporal LTP side-info-eaten; backward-adaptive temporal LTP −0.57 %
     best on the most rhythmic recording, fails the −1.0 % gate). EEG is quasi-oscillatory but **not
     periodic** at the codec's scale.

2. **The gap localized (measured).** `gap_attribution_probe.rs` decomposes our rate on the mv_rls
   residual into three reducible buckets, bits/sample so they add:
   - **Coder loss** — our shipped container already sits *below* the plain residual's order-2 magnitude-
     context entropy on the lose-set (siena 5.687 < 5.805; eegmmidb 4.640 < 4.800). The entropy coder is
     tight; the gap is **not** in coding.
   - **Within-channel context** — the ~0.22–0.39 b/s of order-2 context structure is already banked by
     the shipped `scale_cond` + bias-cancel path.
   - **Cross-channel** — the Gaussian residual multi-information is large (5.7–48 b/s), but that is a
     *continuous-model ceiling*, not integer-realizable (it exceeds our total rate); the *realizable
     linear* cross-channel gain was already measured ~0 (ricct/crosschan cascade). **The entire H.BWC
     referential gap (siena +4.16 %, eegmmidb +2.3 %) is cross-channel joint structure** — one
     concentrated source, not death-by-1000-cuts.

3. **Deep-research shortlist** (fan-out web search + adversarial verify; verification pass was infra-
   rate-limited, so most claims are unverified-not-refuted — treat as plausible, spot-checked). The
   convergent lesson: **don't rotate — cross-predict the *residual*, selected by *rate*.** Ranked
   buildable mechanisms: (1) MPEG-4 ALS Multi-Channel Coding — residual-domain adaptively-weighted
   inter-channel prediction (3-0 verified, patent-clean, mature standard); (2) rate-gated inter-channel
   coupling (couple only when residual cross-correlation clears a threshold, select by coded bits);
   (3) reference-channel MVAR using the co-temporal present sample. All patent-clean; the VVC/H.BWC
   integrated `J=D+λR` loop (RDOQ + trellis quant + CABAC) is the "gold" version but VVC-essential-
   patent-encumbered — capture the *principle*, not the toolset.

## Decision

**D1 — mv_rls IS already the integrated joint spatio-temporal predictor.** `mv_rls` predicts each
channel from `[own K past] + [M prior channels at the SAME instant]` — present co-temporal spatial +
temporal, one RLS, channel-major. The research's #1 (ALS-MCC-class residual-domain joint prediction) is
therefore *already banked in spirit*, and the container (`lmo_lossless`, transform_id=2) additionally
runs **multi-reference integer spatial prediction on the raw signal** (gate 0c −10.5 %…−22 %) keep-best
against mv_rls variants + LSB-split. The container already fights cross-channel two ways.

**D2 — the head-to-head, measured on all data.** `crosschan_residual_ab.rs` competes the shortlist as a
**second** cross-channel stage on the best-config mv_rls residual (never the raw signal), rate-gated
keep-best, side-info counted, reversibility structural. Two baselines: `B0` = best-of-7-config per-
channel mv_rls residual (isolates the cross-stage); `CONT` = shipped `LmoCodec` Lossless (the real
"beat production" bar). Correcting a strawman caught mid-probe: config-0 residual alone is 4–7 % weaker
than the container, so *only* the vs-CONT column is load-bearing.

| recording | ch | CONT bps | B0 bps | M1/B0 (scalar) | M2/B0 (unit-diff) | M3/B0 (spatial-LS) | ORA/B0 | **ORA/CONT** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| siena | 35 | 5.687 | 5.953 | −1.72 % | −0.40 % | −2.21 % | −2.25 % | **+2.32 %** |
| eegmmidb | 64 | 4.640 | 4.947 | −0.74 % | −0.19 % | −0.62 % | −0.87 % | **+5.70 %** |
| ma | 21 | 4.916 | 4.806 | −0.23 % | −0.01 % | −0.19 % | −0.34 % | **−2.56 %** |
| tuar | 33 | 5.832 | 6.079 | −0.68 % | −0.09 % | −0.96 % | −0.98 % | **+3.20 %** |
| helsinki | 21 | 3.539 | 3.558 | −0.63 % | 0.00 % | −1.09 % | −1.19 % | **−0.67 %** |
| chbmit | 23 | 5.282 | 5.293 | −1.01 % | −0.15 % | −1.55 % | −1.56 % | **−1.35 %** |

**Mechanism ranking (durable):** **M3 (multi-reference spatial LS) > M1 (scalar single-ref ALS-MCC) ≫
M2 (unit difference, near-useless).** The multi-reference joint LS is the winning form — validating the
research's #1 as the *multi-ref* variant and **killing the naive "just difference the channels" idea**
(M2 buys 0–0.4 %). The pure cross-stage gain over best-config mv_rls (M3/B0) is real and consistent,
−0.19 %…−2.21 %, largest on bipolar/telescoping montages.

**D3 — the mv_rls→spatial stack is a MONTAGE-SPECIFIC keep-best candidate, not a universal win.** It
beats the shipped container on bipolar/neonatal montages (ma −2.56 %, chbmit −1.35 %, helsinki −0.67 %)
and loses on referential (siena +2.32 %, eegmmidb +5.70 %, tuar +3.20 %) where the container's *raw*
multi-ref spatial prediction is already stronger — because running mv_rls first temporally-whitens each
channel and partly destroys the clean raw common-mode that raw-spatial exploits (a mini cascade). The
two approaches are **complementary; neither dominates.** As a keep-best container candidate it is
never-worse and gains on the three bipolar/neonatal sets.

**Decision on D3:** wiring "best-config mv_rls residual + M3 multi-ref spatial-LS residual stage" as a
new `lmo_lossless` keep-best candidate is a **clean, never-worse, patent-clean** montage-specific win
(≈−1 to −2.5 % on bipolar/neonatal). It is **approved but LOW priority** — gate it behind the existing
keep-best so it cannot regress referential, ship it only when a bipolar/neonatal deployment is
prioritized. It does **not** close the referential H.BWC gap (that is what the container's raw-spatial
already partly does, and the rest is nonlinear — see D4).

**D4 — the remaining headroom is nonlinear: learned joint entropy is the committed future direction.**
The container already extracts most of the *linearly-realizable* cross-channel redundancy (it beats
config-0 mv_rls by 4–7 % on referential). The large residual cross-channel multi-information the gap
ledger surfaced is therefore dominantly the part **no linear stage can reach** — it needs a model that
conditions *jointly and nonlinearly* across the channel axis. This is committed to the **LMQ thread**
(runs in parallel; not deterministic-codec work):

- **Prior-art anchor:** Integer Discrete Flows (IDF, Hoogeboom et al. 2019) / L3C — invertible-integer
  learned lossless via a bijective map to a factorized discrete prior. The buildable target is a learned
  autoregressive/flow **entropy model conditioned on the co-temporal already-decoded samples of
  correlated channels** — the coding-domain analog that never rotates the signal.
- **Why it can win where linear can't:** the cross-channel structure H.BWC's integrated CABAC captures,
  and the residual MI our linear stages leave, are exactly the nonlinear joint dependencies a learned
  conditional model is built for. This is the same joint-structure target as the deterministic
  cross-channel work — approached with the one tool that has headroom beyond the linear class.
- **Patent-cleanliness:** academic, non-standard-essential; check per-architecture. Distinct from the
  VVC-essential-patent RDOQ/TCQ/CABAC path, which stays an *oracle only* (ADR 0062).
- **Gate (measure-before-adopt, per house rule):** a learned joint entropy model earns adoption only on
  a held-out end-to-end lossless bits win over the shipped container across the corpus — not on a
  proxy. Unbuilt; scoped as the next LMQ-side probe.

## Patent landscape (recorded)

- **Clean:** MPEG-4 ALS Multi-Channel Coding (mature ISO standard); classical CALIC/JPEG-LS context
  conditioning; our `mv_rls` + `lmo_lossless` multi-ref spatial (independently derived, integer, ours).
- **Encumbered (oracle only, never a dep):** VVC-essential RDOQ (`J=D+λR` against real CABAC bits),
  dependent/trellis quantization, CABAC neighbor-context — the H.BWC "integrated loop". Capture the
  *principle* (rate-driven selection, neighbor conditioning) in the clean ALS/context lineage, never the
  toolset. Re-check with counsel before any RDOQ/TCQ/CABAC-derived mechanism.

## Methodology lessons (so they cannot drift)

- **The baseline is the SHIPPED container, not a single mv_rls config.** A cross-stage that beats
  config-0 by −3.6 % but is still +2.3 % vs the container is a *strawman win* — caught and corrected
  mid-probe by adding the `CONT` and best-config columns. Always compare to production bytes.
- **Rate, not energy.** Every cross-channel selection is gated on actual coded bits (or the coded-size
  the keep-best measures), never LS residual energy — LS-energy selection is precisely what caused the
  cascade penalty in ricct/crosschan.
- **Residual-domain, not raw-rotation.** Cross-predicting residuals preserves each channel's spectrum;
  rotating the raw signal destroys it. Confirmed by M3 (spatial LS on the residual, rate-gated, never-
  worse) winning where orthogonal KLT rotation lost.

## Progress Log

- **2026-07-09** — ADR created. Probes committed + MiMo-reviewed + pushed to `codec-lossless` main:
  `best_basis_probe.rs` (7ceb76d), `gap_attribution_probe.rs` (d2b9637), `crosschan_residual_ab.rs`
  (d01babb). Deep-research report archived at the session transcript. D1–D4 recorded. D3 (M3 keep-best
  wire) approved low-priority, unbuilt. D4 (learned joint entropy) committed to the LMQ thread, gate
  defined, unbuilt.

## References

- Probes: `codec-lossless/lamquant-lml-optimum/examples/{best_basis_probe,gap_attribution_probe,crosschan_residual_ab,ricct_probe,block_backadapt_ls_probe,ltp_backadapt_probe}.rs`
- ADR 0064 (parent), ADR 0054 (warplan), ADR 0062 (patent posture), ADR 0063 (physics-honest high-freq)
- MPEG-4 ALS MCC: Liebchen 2009 (elvera.nue.tu-berlin.de/files/1216Liebchen2009.pdf); IEICE Trans. Fund. E91.A/3/756 (14.6 % max, audio)
- Reference-channel MVAR lossless EEG/ECG: arXiv 1605.04418 (4.70 vs 5.37 bps DB1a)
- Rate-gated inter-channel coding: PMC4208236 (~11.92 % vs single-channel)
- Learned joint lossless: IDF — Hoogeboom et al., arXiv 1905.07376
- Context-based EEG lossless ceiling: Memon, Kong & Cinkler, IEEE TITB 2000 (PubMed 10719487)

# ADR 0085: Give BLUT a versioned plan registry so a fingerprinted DAG can be published, promoted to a named pointer, and rolled back atomically

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it, so the original stays as historical record. When the
> deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and set Status to
> `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`. A frozen ADR is permanent. To reverse a frozen
> decision later, write a *new* ADR that supersedes it (updating this one's
> Status pointer is the only edit allowed after freeze).

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` → `Complete — frozen 2026-07-10`

## Context

Flyte registers every workflow as an immutable, versioned entity and lets an
operator activate/deactivate a launch plan by version; Dagster code-locations
serve versioned pipeline definitions the daemon reloads. Both give a team the
operation "ship *this* pipeline to *that* environment, and undo it" without
re-running or editing source.

BLUT today has the raw material but no registry. ADR 0078 landed the PlanSpec IR
and its content-addressed fingerprint (`plan_fingerprint`, blake3 over the
canonicalised typed graph), and the Starlark front-end compiles a DAG to that IR
out-of-process. But there is nothing that *names* a fingerprint, records who
published it, or lets `registry://plan@prod` resolve to a specific frozen graph.
A run today is launched from a source path; "roll back prod to yesterday's graph"
means "find the old source, hope it still compiles the same, re-run" — which is
neither atomic nor verifiable, and silently drifts if a transitive stage
registration changed. There is also no place that a publish is type-checked
*before* it can be promoted, so a broken graph is only discovered at dispatch.

## Decision

BLUT will add a local **plan registry** backed by two SQLite tables in
`~/.blut/registry.db`: `deployments` (immutable rows — `plan_fingerprint` PK,
canonical PlanSpec bytes, publisher, timestamp, source-provenance, tenant) and
`deployment_pointers` (mutable named pointers — `(tenant, name) → plan_fingerprint`,
with a `history` of prior fingerprints per pointer). Four engine subcommands
operate it, all pure-local file/DB work (charter-safe, no server): `blut plan
publish <spec>` canonicalises + typechecks the PlanSpec and inserts an immutable
`deployments` row keyed by its ADR-0078 fingerprint (idempotent — republishing
identical bytes is a no-op returning the same id); `blut plan promote
<fingerprint> registry://plan@<name>` moves a pointer and appends the previous
target to that pointer's history; `blut plan rollback registry://plan@<name>`
pops the pointer back to its previous history entry atomically (single DB
transaction); `blut plan history registry://plan@<name>` prints the pointer's
audit trail. The fingerprint IS the deploy identity — `blut run
registry://plan@prod` resolves the pointer to a frozen `deployments` row and
dispatches that exact graph. Typecheck-on-publish is fail-closed: a PlanSpec that
does not type-resolve against the compiled stage registry cannot enter
`deployments`. Every publish/promote/rollback carries the acting tenant (ADR
0096) and refuses to cross the clinical boundary (ADR 0061) — a Restricted-tenant
fingerprint can never be promoted onto a shared-tenant pointer.

## Rationale

- The fingerprint already exists and is content-addressed (ADR 0078); reusing it
  as deploy identity means "prod == fingerprint X" is verifiable by recompiling
  the source and comparing hashes — no separate version counter to drift.
- Immutable `deployments` + mutable pointers is the minimal shape that gives
  atomic promote/rollback: rollback is a single-row pointer update inside one
  transaction, never a re-run.
- Typecheck-on-publish moves the failure from dispatch time (after broker
  admission, after side effects) to publish time, which is free and reversible.
- Pointer history is the audit substrate RBAC (ADR 0095) and multi-tenancy (ADR
  0096) hang off — "who put what on prod when" is one table.
- SQLite + files keeps the registry inside the engine process (no HTTP server,
  ADR 0034); the web dashboard (ADR 0093) reads it, never owns it.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Git tags / branches as the registry.** Rejected: a git ref names a source
  commit, not a *typed compiled graph* — the same commit can compile to a
  different PlanSpec if a transitively-registered stage changed between
  compiles, so a git ref is not a stable deploy identity the way the ADR-0078
  fingerprint is. It also cannot express per-tenant pointers or a fail-closed
  typecheck gate.
- **A monotonic integer version per plan name (Flyte-style `v1, v2`).** Rejected:
  a counter is an extra source of truth that must be allocated, synchronised
  across the mesh (ADR 0079), and can collide; the content hash is already
  globally unique and mesh-safe with zero coordination. We keep a human name only
  at the *pointer* layer, never as the artifact identity.
- **Serve the registry from the `blut-worker`/axum sidecar as the source of
  truth.** Rejected: that would make the control plane depend on a running server
  for a `blut run` to resolve a pointer, violating the "engine ships as the CLI
  tool, offline-capable" premise (ADR 0083). The sidecar may *read* the DB; it is
  not the registry.

## Consequences

- Upside: `blut run registry://plan@prod` and one-command rollback become real;
  the plan graph shown in the console/web (ADR 0093) can be pinned to a
  fingerprint, so the UI stops guessing which source is live.
- Upside: the registry is the natural home for the RBAC audit log and tenant
  quota accounting — later ADRs extend it rather than inventing new storage.
- Downside: a second stateful store (`registry.db`) to back up and migrate
  alongside the lineage DB; a schema-migration discipline is now load-bearing.
- Downside: typecheck-on-publish couples publish to the *current* compiled stage
  registry — publishing a plan that references a stage removed from the binary
  fails, by design, which some workflows will experience as friction.
- Constraint inherited: pointers are per-tenant; a shared control plane cannot
  have one global `prod` — every pointer name is tenant-qualified (ADR 0096).

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — write once; amend only by a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** `~/.blut/registry.db` with `deployments` (immutable,
  fingerprint-keyed) + `deployment_pointers` (named, with history) tables, and
  `blut plan {publish,promote,rollback,history}` subcommands; a `registry://` URI
  resolver in the run dispatcher.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `cargo test -p blut --test registry_roundtrip` — publishes a
    known PlanSpec, promotes it to `registry://plan@test`, publishes a second,
    promotes, rolls back, and asserts the resolved fingerprint + that a
    type-broken PlanSpec is rejected at publish and a Restricted-tenant
    fingerprint is refused at promote.
  - `pass when:` `exit == 0` (rollback resolves to the exact prior fingerprint;
    broken-publish and clinical-cross-promote both return non-zero and write no
    row).
- **Rollback:** feature-gate the subcommands behind `--features registry`; if
  abandoned, drop the two tables and the URI resolver — `blut run <path>` (source
  dispatch) is unaffected.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-07-10 — LANDED + FROZEN (engine main `f8082c7`). `src/registry_db.rs`:
  `~/.blut/registry.db` (SQLite, `$BLUT_REGISTRY_DB` override) with `deployments`
  (immutable, ADR-0078 fingerprint PK, canonical spec bytes + publisher + tenant
  + source), `deployment_pointers` (`(tenant,name)→fingerprint`) and an
  append-only `pointer_history` trail. API: `publish` (fail-closed typecheck via
  `spec.compile(reg)` then insert; idempotent same-tenant, refuses cross-tenant
  re-publish of identical bytes), `promote` (cross-tenant refusal + upsert +
  history in one txn), `rollback` (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, read+write one snapshot, pops
  to the previous target with a tenant re-check), `resolve_pointer`/`resolve_spec`,
  `history`, `parse_pointer_uri` (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` allowlist). CLI: `blut plan
  {publish,promote,rollback,history}` (`--tenant`); the run dispatcher resolves
  `blut recipe declare registry://plan@<name> [--run] [--tenant]` to the frozen
  spec. **Gate met:** `cargo test -p blut --test registry_roundtrip` = 1 passed —
  publish A → promote → publish B → promote → rollback resolves to A's exact
  fingerprint + `resolve_spec` loads that graph; idempotent republish; distinct
  specs get distinct fingerprints; history trail `[A,B,A]`; a broken-stage spec
  refused at publish; a Restricted-tenant fingerprint refused at promote onto a
  shared pointer (pointer stays unset); cross-tenant re-publish refused; URI-name
  allowlist enforced. 857 lib green; clippy+fmt+scope_guard clean. MiMo (3
  rounds) → fixed a rollback TOCTOU (immediate txn), publish INSERT-OR-IGNORE
  tenant-masking + its narrow race-arm re-verify, added the tenant boundary to
  rollback + `--tenant` threading + URI validation. NOTE `RESTRICTED_TENANT` is a
  minimal clinical-boundary stand-in until ADR 0096 multi-tenancy lands. Status →
  Complete — frozen 2026-07-10._

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once; this + the frozen Status line is the single freeze mark)*

- **verdict:** `passed`
- **gate_cmd:** `cargo test -p blut --test registry_roundtrip`
- **result:** exit 0 (1 passed). Rollback resolves to the exact prior
  fingerprint; the broken-publish and clinical-cross-promote both return errors
  and write no pointer row; plus idempotent republish, distinct-fingerprint,
  full history trail, cross-tenant re-publish refusal, and URI-name validation
  all asserted.
- **git_sha:** engine `f8082c7`  ·  **artifact sha256:** n/a (source-only)

## Related Decisions

ADR 0078 (PlanSpec IR + content-addressed fingerprint — this extends it, does not
supersede), ADR 0083 (interface stack — the web sidecar reads this DB), ADR 0090
(roadmap — deployment/rollout), ADR 0095 (RBAC gates publish/promote), ADR 0096
(per-tenant pointer namespaces), ADR 0061 (clinical hard-block at promote).

## Validation  *(ongoing — distinct from the completion gate above)*

Wrong if: a promoted pointer ever resolves to a fingerprint whose stored PlanSpec
no longer typechecks (publish gate leaked); if two operators promoting
concurrently on the mesh (ADR 0079) can leave a pointer with a lost update (the
transaction isn't atomic across nodes); or if teams route around the registry
because pointer resolution is slower than re-running from source. Watch the
publish→promote→run latency and the rate of `registry://` vs raw-path runs.
