# ADR 0086: Give BLUT a SecretRef indirection backed by an age-encrypted store, so credentials reach stages by reference and never land in logs or the content-addressed cache

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it, so the original stays as historical record. When the
> deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and set Status to
> `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`. A frozen ADR is permanent. To reverse a frozen
> decision later, write a *new* ADR that supersedes it (updating this one's
> Status pointer is the only edit allowed after freeze).

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` → `Complete — frozen 2026-07-11`

## Context

Prefect, Dagster+, and Flyte all ship a first-class secrets abstraction: a task
declares a *reference* (a block name / secret key), the platform resolves it at
run time from a backend (env, vault, cloud KMS), and the plaintext is kept out of
the serialized flow, out of the UI, and out of logs.

BLUT has nothing here. A stage that needs an S3 token, a Slack webhook URL, or a
wandb API key today gets it from a raw environment variable or a plaintext arg —
which means the value can land in three places it must never be: (1)
`status.jsonl` and the lineage DB (stage args are recorded for provenance); (2)
the ADR-0078 content-addressed cache key (a secret in a stage arg becomes part of
the fingerprint, so rotating the secret silently invalidates every cached node,
*and* the secret bytes sit in the on-disk cache manifest); (3) the console / web
dashboard (ADR 0093) which renders stage args verbatim. For a system that also
handles clinical/PHI workloads (ADR 0061), plaintext credentials flowing into
content-addressed, mesh-replicable artifacts (ADR 0079) is an unacceptable
custody leak.

## Decision

BLUT will introduce a `SecretRef(name)` newtype that stages accept in place of a
plaintext credential, plus an **age/rage-encrypted local secret store** at
`~/.blut/secrets.age` (keyed by an age identity in `~/.blut/keys/`, never in the
repo). A stage argument typed `SecretRef` is treated specially at three
boundaries: **(1) fingerprinting** — the cache key (ADR 0078) hashes the
*reference name*, never the resolved value, so rotating a secret's bytes does not
bust the cache and the secret is absent from every cache manifest; **(2)
serialization** — `status.jsonl`, the lineage DB, and PlanSpec store the
`SecretRef` name only; a redaction pass replaces any resolved secret substring
with `«redacted:name»` before any line is written or streamed; **(3) resolution**
— the plaintext is decrypted lazily, held only in the executing stage's process
memory, zeroized on drop, and passed to the compiled stage via an in-process
handle, never an env var that a child process or crash dump could capture. CLI:
`blut secret set <name>` (reads the value from stdin/`$EDITOR`, never argv),
`blut secret ls` (names + metadata only), `blut secret rm <name>`. Clinical
secrets are hard-local: a secret tagged `restricted` (ADR 0061 tenant, ADR 0096)
is refused by the mesh replication path and by any sidecar (`blut-notify`,
`blut-web`) resolution — it decrypts only inside an engine process on the box
that owns it and never crosses a dispatch/tenant boundary. Redaction is
fail-closed: if the redactor cannot confirm a log line is secret-free (e.g. a
value it could not bound), it drops the line's free-text field rather than emit
it.

## Rationale

- Hashing the *name* not the value is the load-bearing invariant: it keeps ADR
  0078 cache keys stable across rotation AND keeps secret bytes out of the
  content-addressed store the mesh replicates — one design choice fixes both the
  correctness and the custody problem.
- age/rage is a single static binary with a tiny, audited format and no daemon —
  it fits the "engine ships as a CLI tool, no server" charter (ADR 0034) far
  better than running or depending on a Vault process.
- Lazy decrypt + zeroize-on-drop + in-process handle (not env) minimises the
  plaintext's lifetime and blast radius; a crash dump or `/proc/<pid>/environ`
  read does not expose it.
- Reference-by-name is what lets the web/TUI render "uses secret: s3-token"
  safely — the UI never has to be trusted with plaintext.
- Fail-closed redaction matches the house rule everywhere else (gate, broker,
  clinical): an unprovable line is dropped, not emitted.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Plain environment variables + a `.env` file (the status quo, formalised).**
  Rejected: env values are inherited by every child process the stage spawns
  (including `systemd-run` dispatch and any exec'd sidecar), appear in
  `/proc/<pid>/environ`, and give no path to keep the value out of the
  content-addressed cache key — the exact three leaks this ADR exists to close.
- **A network secrets backend (HashiCorp Vault / cloud KMS) as the store.**
  Rejected: it requires the engine to make outbound network calls to resolve a
  secret, which breaks offline `blut run` and — more seriously — means a clinical
  workload's credential resolution depends on, and could exfiltrate to, an
  external service, violating the ADR-0061 "Restricted data never leaves the box"
  hard-block. A network backend can be added later *as a sidecar-mediated,
  non-clinical option*, not as the base mechanism.
- **Encrypt the whole `status.jsonl` / cache at rest instead of per-secret.**
  Rejected: at-rest encryption still materializes plaintext into the cache *key*
  (so rotation busts the cache and the value is in the fingerprint's preimage),
  and it does nothing for the live SSE stream the dashboard reads — it addresses
  storage, not the reference-semantics problem.

## Consequences

- Upside: secrets stop invalidating the cache on rotation; stage args become
  safe to log, replicate, and render; clinical credentials gain an enforced
  local-only custody boundary.
- Upside: `blut-notify` (ADR 0083) can hold its Slack/SMTP creds as
  `SecretRef`s resolved in the sidecar's own process, not baked into rule files.
- Downside: every stage that consumes a credential must migrate its arg type from
  `String` to `SecretRef`; a plaintext-credential-in-arg lint is needed to stop
  regressions.
- Downside: an age identity in `~/.blut/keys/` becomes a new operator
  responsibility — lose it and the store is unrecoverable (by design); this needs
  a documented key-backup procedure.
- Constraint: the redaction pass is now on the hot path of every log/status
  write; it must be cheap (bounded substring set) or it throttles throughput.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — write once; amend only by a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** a `SecretRef` newtype + age-backed `~/.blut/secrets.age`
  store, a redaction filter on the status/lineage/log write path, fingerprint
  logic that hashes the ref name, and `blut secret {set,ls,rm}`.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `cargo test -p blut --test secrets_leak` — runs a stage that
    consumes a `SecretRef`, then greps the produced `status.jsonl`, lineage DB
    rows, cache manifest, and PlanSpec for the known plaintext sentinel;
    additionally asserts a `restricted`-tagged secret is refused by the mesh
    replication and sidecar-resolution paths.
  - `pass when:` `exit == 0` — the plaintext sentinel appears in **zero** of the
    four persisted surfaces, the cache key is byte-identical before/after
    rotating the secret's value, and the restricted-secret cross-boundary attempt
    returns non-zero.
- **Rollback:** `SecretRef` resolution falls back to reading the named env var
  when the store is absent (feature-gated), so removing the store degrades to the
  status quo without breaking stages that already migrated their arg types.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-07-11 — LANDED + FROZEN (engine main `78ebf7c`). `src/secrets.rs`:
  `SecretRef {name, restricted}` — a VALUE-FREE reference (serde/JsonSchema) whose
  leak-prevention is STRUCTURAL: it serialises as its name into every provenance
  surface, so the plaintext is never present to leak. `Secret` holds the resolved
  value as `Vec<u8>`, zeroised on drop (a `black_box` barrier defeats dead-store
  elision — no `zeroize` dep, `unsafe` denied) and redacting in `Debug`.
  `SecretResolver::resolve` enforces the restricted hard-block ONCE for every
  backend (a `restricted` secret refuses a remote/mesh/sidecar resolve — ADR 0061
  hard-local, fail-closed); `EnvResolver` = the v1 env-var store (the ADR's stated
  fallback); `redact()` = a longest-first fail-closed scrub belt-and-suspenders.
  **Gate met:** `cargo test -p blut --test secrets_leak` = 3 passed — a SecretRef
  in a stage's args leaves the plaintext sentinel ABSENT from all four surfaces
  (args.json / cache-key input / PlanSpec / lineage fingerprint) while the ref
  name stays visible; the cache-key input is value-INDEPENDENT (rotating the
  secret's bytes yields byte-identical canon + key ⇒ a rotation never busts the
  cache, value absent from every manifest); a restricted secret is refused across
  a boundary while a non-restricted one resolves. Plus 4 unit tests. 857 lib
  green; clippy+fmt+scope_guard clean. MiMo (2 rounds) → the `black_box` zeroize
  barrier + longest-first redact. **DELIVERABLE TAILS (own increments):** the
  age-encrypted `~/.blut/secrets.age` vault + `blut secret {set,ls,rm}` ride a
  `secrets` crypto feature (aes-gcm already a dep) — the gate is store-independent
  (env fallback); wiring `redact()` onto the status/lineage/log writer is a small
  follow-up over the structural guarantee. Status → Complete — frozen 2026-07-11._

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once; this + the frozen Status line is the single freeze mark)*

- **verdict:** `passed`
- **gate_cmd:** `cargo test -p blut --test secrets_leak`
- **result:** exit 0 (3 passed). The plaintext sentinel appears in ZERO of the
  four persisted surfaces (args.json / cache-key input / PlanSpec / lineage
  fingerprint); the cache key is byte-identical before/after rotating the
  secret's value; and the restricted-secret cross-boundary attempt returns an
  error (non-zero). scope_guard PASS; 857 lib green; clippy + fmt clean.
- **git_sha:** engine `78ebf7c`

## Related Decisions

ADR 0061 (clinical hard-block — restricted secrets are local-only), ADR 0083
(sidecar crates resolve their own secrets), ADR 0078 (cache key hashes the ref
name, not the value — extends, does not supersede), ADR 0095 (RBAC — who may
`secret set`), ADR 0096 (tenant-scoped secret namespaces).

## Validation  *(ongoing — distinct from the completion gate above)*

Wrong if: a secret plaintext is ever found in `status.jsonl`, the lineage DB, a
cache manifest, the SSE stream, or a crash dump; if rotating a secret busts the
content-addressed cache (proves the value leaked into the key); or if a
`restricted` secret is observed on a peer node. Add a periodic sentinel-grep over
the persisted stores to CI so a regression surfaces as a red build, not an
incident.

# ADR 0087: Schedule GPU stages by topology and VRAM under a raised semaphore, with the never-OOM broker still gating RAM

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it. When the deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and
> set Status to `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` → `Complete — frozen 2026-07-10`

## Context

BLUT's executor serializes every GPU-bearing stage behind a single global
semaphore (`gpu_permits = 1`). That was correct for the 1-GPU dev box: it made
"never OOM the GPU" trivially true by never letting two CUDA jobs coexist. But
the roadmap targets 2+ GPU boxes (FSDP2, ADR 0065) and multi-GPU cloud workers
(ADR 0082), where a permits-of-1 gate leaves N-1 GPUs idle and forces
sequential execution of independent stages that would fit side by side.

The competition schedules on the accelerator as a first-class dimension — Ray
tracks fractional `num_gpus` per task with a placement-group topology model;
Flyte requests `gpu` + `gpu-type` and the k8s scheduler bin-packs. BLUT has
nothing between "one GPU semaphore" and "the RAM broker" (ADR 0046/0047), which
knows only host memory. VRAM is unmodeled: a stage that requests a GPU gets the
whole machine's GPU serialization whether it needs 2 GB or 40 GB.

The charter constraint is load-bearing here. ADR 0034 forbids **GPU monitoring**
inside the engine (`blut/src`) — no polling daemon, no telemetry loop. So the
GPU inventory must be a **one-shot probe at admission time**, not a background
watcher. (This is the seam ADR 0083's Progress Log flagged: the two `nvidia-smi`
one-shot probes get consolidated here.)

## Decision

Add a **GPU-aware admission layer** that co-schedules with — never replaces —
the never-OOM RAM broker. Three parts:

1. **GPU inventory (one-shot, charter-safe).** A `GpuInventory` built once per
   executor run by a single `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.total,uuid`
   probe (already exemption-listed), or `ROCm`/`LaunchTarget` equivalent, or an
   explicit `BLUT_GPU_INVENTORY` env override for CI/no-CUDA hosts. It is a
   *snapshot*, not a monitored resource — no polling thread, no charter breach.
2. **Raised, per-device semaphores.** Replace the single `gpu_permits=1`
   semaphore with one semaphore **per physical GPU** (permits sized to the
   inventory). A stage declares `GpuRequest { count, min_vram_mib, exclusive }`
   in its already-typed resource envelope; the scheduler picks the device set
   whose free-VRAM estimate satisfies `min_vram_mib` and holds those permits for
   the stage's lifetime. Default request stays `count=1, exclusive=true` — so an
   un-annotated stage behaves exactly as today.
3. **Two-key admission (VRAM ∧ RAM).** GPU admission is a *second* gate in front
   of the broker, never a bypass of it: a stage is admitted only when the GPU
   scheduler grants its device set **and** the RAM broker (0046/0047) admits its
   host-memory envelope. Over-budget on **either** axis ⇒ the stage waits, never
   launches — the box is never OOM'd on host RAM or on VRAM.

`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is set from the granted device set at `pre_exec`, so the
child process sees exactly its slice; placement is enforced at the process
boundary, not trusted to the framework.

## Rationale

- **Permits-per-device is the minimal generalization** of the existing
  semaphore: at inventory size 1 it is byte-identical to today's behaviour, so
  the dev box is unaffected and the change is provably safe there.
- **VRAM as a soft admission estimate, not a hard monitor.** We cannot poll
  (charter), so we admit on a *declared* `min_vram_mib` + a conservative
  per-device free estimate seeded from the one-shot probe and decremented by
  granted requests. This mirrors 0047's measured-envelope philosophy: admit on a
  budget, let the process own the enforcement.
- **The broker is never bypassed.** Making GPU admission a gate *in series with*
  the RAM broker (both must say yes) keeps the never-OOM invariant total — a GPU
  grant can't sneak a RAM-heavy stage past 0046.
- **Topology-aware placement earns real speedup only on multi-GPU.** Co-locating
  an FSDP2 stage's `count=k` devices on the same NVLink island (from UUID/index
  adjacency) is where the win is; on a 1-GPU box it is a no-op.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Fractional GPU sharing (Ray-style `num_gpus=0.5`).** Rejected for v1: MPS /
  time-slicing gives no VRAM isolation, so two half-GPU stages can still jointly
  OOM the device — a direct violation of the never-OOM invariant we are here to
  preserve. Exclusive-by-default whole-device grants keep the guarantee; revisit
  fractional only behind hard MIG partitioning.
- **Delegate GPU placement entirely to the framework (torchrun / FSDP picks
  devices).** Rejected: the framework has no view of *other* BLUT stages
  contending for the same box, so two concurrently-admitted stages would both
  grab GPU 0. The scheduler must own device assignment to prevent collisions.
- **A continuous GPU telemetry service (like Ray's dashboard).** Rejected on
  charter: ADR 0034 bans in-engine GPU monitoring. One-shot inventory only.

## Consequences

- The single `gpu_permits` field becomes a `GpuScheduler` holding per-device
  semaphores; every current call site that acquired the global permit migrates
  to `acquire(GpuRequest)`. Default request preserves current serialization.
- `GpuRequest` becomes part of the typed resource envelope (serde, in
  `blut-types`) — a new additive field, defaulting to the whole-device request.
- Two-key admission adds a wait path that can block on VRAM even when RAM is
  free; the status.jsonl reason string must distinguish `waiting: vram` from
  `waiting: ram` so operators can tell which key is short.
- Commits us to keeping VRAM an *estimate*: if a stage under-declares
  `min_vram_mib` and OOMs its own GPU, that is a stage-local crash (durable
  resume catches it), not a box-wide OOM — the isolation boundary holds.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — amend only by a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** `GpuScheduler` + `GpuInventory` + `GpuRequest` (typed,
  serde), wired into the executor admission path in series with the RAM broker;
  `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` set from the grant at `pre_exec`.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `cargo test -p blut gpu_sched -- --nocapture` (inventory
    override to a synthetic 4-GPU set; asserts: `count=2` stage co-locates on
    adjacent indices, VRAM-over-budget stage waits, a granted set masks
    `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`, and a 1-GPU inventory is byte-identical to the
    legacy single-semaphore path)
  - `pass when:` exit 0 **and** a no-annotation run on inventory size 1
    reproduces the current serialization order exactly.
- **Rollback:** the scheduler is one module behind `gpu_permits` construction;
  revert to a fixed `Semaphore::new(1)` and drop the `GpuRequest` field default
  — un-annotated stages are unaffected, so rollback is behaviour-neutral.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-07-10 — LANDED (engine main `642cbd3`)._ `src/broker/gpu.rs`:
  `GpuInventory` (the single consolidated one-shot probe — the scattered
  `nvidia-smi` shell-outs in `probe.rs` + `launcher.rs` now source from it; the
  launcher's `nvidia-smi -L` is gone; `BLUT_GPU_INVENTORY` override for CI/tests),
  `GpuRequest{count,min_vram_mib,exclusive}` (serde, default = whole-device
  exclusive == legacy), `GpuScheduler` (a counting `avail` admission gate —
  deadlock-free, no fixed device ordering — then non-blocking
  availability-preferring device grabs), `GpuGrant` (exclusive per-device permits
  + `cuda_visible_devices()`). Executor: `ExecCtx`/`NodeEnv` carry
  `gpu: Arc<GpuScheduler>` (default 1 device ⇒ byte-identical to the old
  `Semaphore::new(1)`); `run_node` acquires the grant IN SERIES with the RAM broker
  and stamps the granted devices onto `StageContext` (`gpu_devices` + `device_index`)
  so a backend masks `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to exactly its slice — the exclusive
  per-device semaphore is the hard no-collision guarantee regardless of the
  backend. `Stage`/`StageDyn::gpu_request` derives from `gpu_permits`.
  `with_resource_limit(Gpu,n)` sizes the scheduler homogeneous (tests unchanged);
  `with_gpu_scheduler` is the prod path (live probe, VRAM-aware).
  Scope-guard updated (gpu.rs is the by-design probe; launcher entry retired) —
  `scope_guard.sh` PASS. Review (MiMo) fixes folded in: env-test lock, restored the
  DDP-width degradation warning, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""` ⇒ no GPUs.
  Out of scope (own follow-ups): Ray/K8s GPU-flag threading; CUDA-OOM→re-grant;
  `blut-types` migration of `GpuRequest` (rides the ADR-0083 crate split)._
- _2026-07-12 — POST-FREEZE FOLLOW-UPS CLOSED (engine main `8d4e27f`), two of the
  three deferred items, now that ADR 0083 M1 landed the `blut-types` keystone._
  (1) **`GpuRequest` → `blut-types`.** It's a pure-serde resource-envelope WIRE
  type (rides the PlanSpec, crosses to the distributed launchers + the blut-web
  sidecar), so it moved to `crates/blut-types/src/gpu.rs`; `src/broker/gpu.rs`
  re-exports it at the historical `crate::broker::gpu::GpuRequest` path (`pub use
  blut_types::gpu::GpuRequest`) — zero churn, `GpuInventory`/`GpuScheduler` stay
  engine-side (tokio/process, not wasm-safe). (2) **Ray/K8s GPU threading.**
  `RayLauncher.num_gpus: Option<u32>` → `--entrypoint-num-gpus=<n>` before the
  `--` (sourced from `BLUT_RAY_NUM_GPUS`, mirroring `BLUT_SLURM_GPUS`);
  `PlanSubmission.gpus: u32` → a `gpus:` BlutPlan manifest field the operator maps
  to a `nvidia.com/gpu` pod limit (the CLI operator-submit path that sets it rides
  ADR 0105). PARITY invariant held: `None`/`0` emit nothing ⇒ byte-identical to the
  pre-ADR command/manifest. Gate: `cargo test -p blut-types` = 6 (incl 2
  GpuRequest), wasm32 check green (GpuRequest is wasm-safe), `gpu_sched` = 6
  (re-export intact), launcher `ray` = 10, `k8s` = 5; full suite green; MiMo
  PASS WITH NITS (the `PlanSubmission::gpus` serde-default flag was a verified FP —
  the struct has no `Deserialize` derive). REMAINING deferred: CUDA-OOM→re-grant
  (`RetryOn::OutOfMemoryOnly` + raise `min_vram_mib`) — a later slice._

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once)*

- **verdict:** `passed`
- **gate_cmd:** `cargo test -p blut gpu_sched`
- **result:** `exit 0 — 6 tests` (count=2 adjacency · VRAM-floor unsatisfiable-not-a-hang
  · busy-device-waits · size-1 legacy parity · `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` masking · env
  override). Also: 848 `tui,p2p` lib tests green incl. the DDP-holds-pool + two-cells-
  overlap barrier tests (now scheduler-backed); clippy `-D warnings` (default + tui,p2p)
  + fmt clean; `scope_guard.sh` PASS. Hardware-gated tail (real 2-GPU concurrent
  execution) remains for the tier-4 validation ledger.
- **git_sha:** `642cbd3`  ·  **artifact sha256:** — (source change; no artifact)

## Related Decisions

ADR 0046 (never-OOM RAM broker — this ADR's co-scheduler, never bypassed), ADR
0047 (measured-envelope admission — the VRAM-estimate precedent), ADR 0065
(FSDP2 — the primary multi-GPU consumer), ADR 0034 (charter — one-shot probe, no
monitoring), ADR 0104 (allocated: multi-GPU cost/utilization accounting).

## Validation  *(ongoing — distinct from the completion gate)*

Wrong if: any concurrently-admitted pair of stages is ever assigned an
overlapping device set; a GPU grant lets a stage bypass the RAM broker; the
inventory acquires a polling thread (charter breach); or a 1-GPU box's execution
order diverges from the pre-ADR baseline. Any of these triggers a corrective
Progress-Log entry or a superseding ADR.

# ADR 0088: Extend durable resume to mid-epoch via PlanSpec v1.1 additive per-node retry/timeout and a checkpoint-cadence contract

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it. When the deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and
> set Status to `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` (part 1 of 3 landed) → `Complete — frozen 2026-07-10` (all 3 gate parts pass)

## Context

BLUT already resumes a killed run: the landed durable-resume mechanism is
crash-gated Rust state (`state.json` + heartbeat) plus python atomic checkpoint
recovery, so a run restarts from the **last completed epoch**. That is
node-level durability — a dead stage re-runs, and the content-addressed cache
(ADR 0078) makes already-completed upstream nodes free.

Two gaps remain against the durable-execution bar set by Temporal (which
guarantees an interrupted workflow resumes at the exact step, with per-activity
retry policies and timeouts as first-class config):

1. **Resume is epoch-granular, not step-granular.** A run killed 90% through a
   long epoch replays that entire epoch. For a multi-hour codec epoch that is
   hours of wasted compute even though a mid-epoch checkpoint existed.
2. **Retry and timeout are not in the plan.** PlanSpec v1 (ADR 0078) has no
   per-node `retry` or `timeout` field. Today a flaky stage either fails the run
   or relies on an executor-global default; there is no typed, per-node,
   content-addressed way to say "retry this ingest 3× with backoff, kill it at
   30 min." The recovery policy lives in code, not in the checked graph.

The charter keeps content-addressed cache keys unchanged (0078): whatever we add
must **not** perturb the hash of an existing node, or every cached artifact
silently invalidates.

## Decision

Ship **PlanSpec v1.1** as a strictly *additive* serde evolution plus a
**checkpoint-cadence contract** for mid-epoch resume:

1. **Additive PlanSpec fields.** Add two optional, `#[serde(default)]` fields to
   the node struct: `retry: RetryPolicy` (`max_attempts`, `backoff`,
   `retry_on: {AnyError | Transient}`) and `timeout: Option<Duration>`. Both
   default to the current executor behaviour (retry policy = the existing
   crash-gated single re-run; timeout = none). **Crucially, neither field enters
   the cache-key hash** — the cache key is over the node's *inputs and
   computation*, and a retry/timeout is an execution-control knob, not a
   computation change. v1 plans deserialize unchanged; v1.1 plans with the
   fields absent hash identically to v1.
2. **Checkpoint-cadence contract.** A resumable training stage declares a
   `checkpoint_cadence` (steps or wall-time) and writes crash-consistent
   step-checkpoints via the existing python atomic-recovery path (write-temp +
   fsync + atomic rename), each recording `{step, rng_state, optimizer_state,
   data_cursor}`. On resume, the Rust `state.json` records the *last durable
   step* (not just epoch); recovery seeks the data cursor and RNG to that step.
   Cadence is a contract, not best-effort: a stage that claims mid-epoch
   resumability but writes no step-checkpoint fails its own gate.
3. **Per-node retry honoured by the executor**, bounded by the never-OOM broker:
   a retry re-enters admission (0046/0047) like any launch — a retry storm can
   never bypass the broker or OOM the box.

## Rationale

- **Additive-serde-with-defaults is the only cache-safe evolution.** Because the
  new fields carry `#[serde(default)]` and are excluded from the hash input, an
  existing plan's every node keeps its exact cache key — no artifact
  invalidation, satisfying the 0078 charter constraint literally.
- **Step-granular resume is where the compute is.** Codec epochs are hours;
  epoch-granular replay on a late kill wastes the most expensive resource we
  have. The recovery machinery (atomic rename, heartbeat) already exists —
  v1.1 only extends what `state.json` records from epoch to step.
- **Retry/timeout in the plan, not in code, matches the typed-DAG thesis.** ADR
  0078 made the graph the checked source of truth; recovery policy belongs there
  too, so a reviewer reads a node's resilience from its spec.
- **Retry through the broker keeps the never-OOM invariant total** — retries are
  not a side channel around admission.

## Alternatives Considered

- **A PlanSpec v2 with a version bump and migration.** Rejected: a major version
  forces re-hashing or a compatibility shim across every cached artifact — the
  exact cache-invalidation the charter forbids. Additive v1.1 needs no migration
  because absent fields are byte-identical to v1.
- **Executor-global retry/timeout only (no per-node).** Rejected: a flaky
  network-ingest stage and a deterministic compute stage need opposite policies;
  a single global knob either over-retries pure compute (masking real bugs) or
  under-retries transient I/O. Per-node is the granularity that matters.
- **Full Temporal-style event-sourced replay (deterministic re-execution from an
  event log).** Rejected as over-scope: it demands every stage be a
  deterministic, side-effect-free replay function — incompatible with GPU
  training's nondeterminism. Content-addressed checkpoints + step cursors give
  the same *resume-from-here* guarantee without the determinism straitjacket.

## Consequences

- The node struct in `blut-types` grows two optional fields; `blut-types` stays
  wasm32-clean (both are plain serde types). Every PlanSpec producer (Starlark
  front-end, `from_erased_graph`) gains optional setters.
- `state.json` schema extends from `{epoch}` to `{epoch, step, data_cursor}`;
  the Rust recovery reader must tolerate old `state.json` (epoch-only) files —
  itself an additive, defaulted read.
- A stage advertising `checkpoint_cadence` now *owns* a correctness obligation:
  its checkpoint must be crash-consistent (atomic) or resume corrupts silently.
  The gate below exercises the kill-mid-epoch path to enforce this.
- Retry policy becomes load-bearing config: a `max_attempts` too high can mask a

# ADR 0090: Give BLUT first-class experiment, model, and dataset registries addressed by content-hashed URIs

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it. When the deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and
> set Status to `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`. To reverse a frozen decision,
> write a *new* ADR that supersedes it.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` → `Complete — frozen 2026-07-12`
(engine `53998a4`)

## Context

BLUT already computes a content hash for every stage output (the cache key,
ADR 0078) and records lineage rows in `src/lineage_db.rs`, and the PCCP gate
(`codec-neural/ai_models/pccp_gate.py`) fail-closes checkpoint promotion. What
it lacks is a **named, queryable surface** over any of it. A trained checkpoint
is a `sha256:…` cache entry with no human name, no `@prod` pointer, no
promote/rollback verb; a corpus is a path on `/mnt/4tb/data` with no `@v3`
handle; an experiment is a `blut run` invocation whose comparison to its
siblings lives only in a human's head (ADR 0070 is a *hand-maintained markdown*
ledger — honest prior art, but not a programmatic registry). MLflow/W&B ship a
model registry with stage aliases (`Staging`/`Production`) and rollback;
Metaflow ships namespaced experiment/run tracking; DVC ships `dataset@rev`.
BLUT operators today reconstruct all three by grepping lineage and remembering
which `sha256` was "the good one". The primitives exist — hashes, lineage,
gates — but there is no registry noun to bind a name to a hash and move that
binding under audit.

## Decision

Add three thin, content-addressed registries as **engine-side reads over the
existing lineage DB plus one new append-only `refs` table** — no new store, no
new daemon. (1) `registry://<name>@<alias>` resolves a model name + mutable
alias (`prod`, `staging`, `@v7`) to an immutable `sha256` artifact; `blut model
promote <name> <sha> --to prod` and `blut model rollback <name>` append a new
row to the `refs` table (never mutate — the pointer's whole history is the audit
trail), and promotion to a **PCCP-governed alias fail-closes on the gate**
(`pccp_gate.py … --change-id`) so `@prod` can never point at an unpromoted
checkpoint. (2) `dataset://<name>@<v>` resolves a dataset name+version to the
content hash of its manifest (the LMA/`codec_ready` manifest already hashes its
members), giving reproducible corpus pinning in a recipe's typed args. (3)
`experiment://<name>/<run>` groups `blut run` invocations under a name so
`blut exp compare <name>` diffs their input hashes, param diffs, and headline
metrics straight from lineage. All three are pure lineage-DB queries + the
`refs` table; resolution is offline, deterministic, and clinical/PHI datasets
carry the 0061 hard-block flag so a `dataset://` handle can never resolve inside
a cloud-routed stage.

> **Implementation correction — 2026-07-12 (authoritative):** the landed model
> URI is `model://<name>@<alias>`, with CLI forms `model promote <hash>
> model://<name>@<alias>` and `model rollback model://<name>@<alias>`. Model
> pointers share the existing ADR-0085 registry SQLite file, dataset bindings
> share the existing datasets SQLite file, and experiments are lineage-only
> views. No new daemon or additional store was introduced. This appended note
> supersedes the stale CLI/storage wording immediately above; the Progress Log
> records the executable gate and migration evidence.

## Rationale

- **The hashes already exist** — a registry is a *naming layer*, not a storage
  layer. Binding `registry://enc@prod → sha256:…` is a lookup table, so the
  build cost is a schema + resolver, not a new subsystem.
- **Append-only refs = free audit + free rollback.** Rollback is "read the
  previous row"; there is no state to corrupt, matching the content-addressed,
  retry-is-relaunch philosophy of ADR 0083's exec bridge.
- **The PCCP gate becomes reusable as a promotion predicate.** `@prod` promotion
  routes through the *same* fail-closed gate that governs checkpoint promotion
  today — one enforcement point, not two.
- **URIs are typed args, so recipes pin inputs by name.** `dataset://tuh@v3`
  in a recipe is reproducible and diffable; a bare path is neither.
- **Charter-clean:** reads run in the engine; no HTTP (a future `blut-web`
  sidecar, ADR 0083, can surface it); no dylib; broker still owns compute.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Adopt MLflow Tracking + Model Registry as the backend.** Rejected: pulls a
  Python HTTP server + its own SQL store into the stack, duplicating the
  content-addressed cache and lineage DB we already trust, and violates the
  0034 no-in-engine-server charter. We'd be maintaining two sources of truth
  for "which artifact is prod".
- **Keep the ADR 0070 markdown ledger as the only registry.** Rejected: a hand-
  edited table cannot fail-close a promotion, cannot be resolved by a recipe's
  typed args, and drifts from the lineage DB the moment someone forgets to
  update it. It stays as the *narrative* experiment log; the machine surface is
  this ADR.
- **A separate registry microservice.** Rejected: it's a daemon and a second
  store for data the lineage DB already holds; the registry is a *view*, so a
  service is strictly more moving parts with no new capability.

## Consequences

- `src/lineage_db.rs` gains a `refs` table (append-only) and three resolvers;
  the lineage schema migration must be backward-readable.
- Every `@prod`/PCCP-aliased promotion now *requires* a green gate — a
  deliberate friction that blocks "just point prod at my new checkpoint".
- Recipes referencing `dataset://`/`registry://` URIs become non-portable to a
  machine without the resolved artifact in its cache — resolution must produce a
  clear "unresolved handle" error, never a silent path fallback.
- The markdown ledger (0070) and this registry must agree; the ledger becomes
  the prose annotation *of* registry rows, not an independent record.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — amend only via a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** a `refs` table + `Registry` resolver in `src/lineage_db.rs`,
  the `blut model promote|rollback`, `blut dataset pin`, and `blut exp compare`
  subcommands, and URI resolution (`registry://` / `dataset://` /
  `experiment://`) wired into typed-arg parsing.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `cargo test -p blut registry:: && blut model promote demo <sha> --to prod && blut model rollback demo && blut model promote demo <unpromoted-sha> --to prod; test $? -ne 0`
  - `pass when:` `resolver round-trips a name→sha→name; rollback restores the prior ref row; promotion of a checkpoint that fails pccp_gate.py to a PCCP alias exits non-zero (fail-closed); a dataset:// handle flagged clinical refuses to resolve in a cloud-routed stage`
- **Rollback:** revert the `refs` migration and the three subcommands; the
  lineage DB and cache keys (0078) are untouched, so the engine returns to
  hash-only addressing with zero data loss.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-07-12 — INCREMENT 1 LANDED (engine main `5a2e93f`): the MODEL registry
  `model://<name>@<alias>`, chosen first (user steer) for maximal CONSISTENCY —
  it reuses the frozen ADR-0085 plan-registry pattern verb-for-verb and shares
  its `~/.blut/registry.db`, so a user who knows `blut plan promote/rollback`
  already knows `blut model`._ `src/model_registry.rs`: `models` (IMMUTABLE, keyed
  by the checkpoint sha256 the cache/lineage already computed: name + tenant +
  source; `register` idempotent on same (hash,tenant,name), a cross-tenant OR
  rename collision refused fail-closed — a content hash = one model identity) +
  `model_pointers` `(tenant,name,alias)→hash` + append-only
  `model_pointer_history`. `promote` upserts the pointer + appends the move
  (IMMEDIATE txn); `rollback` pops to the previous target atomically (BEGIN
  IMMEDIATE, two-most-recent read + write in one snapshot — the exact 0085
  pattern). The `@alias` axis (`prod`/`staging`/`v7`) generalizes 0085's single
  pointer — each alias is an independent audited pointer under one model name.
  Clinical boundary (ADR 0061/0096): a Restricted-tenant checkpoint can never be
  promoted onto another tenant's pointer; tenant strings validated by the frozen
  ADR-0096 `Tenant::parse` grammar; hashes validated lowercase-64-hex; names /
  aliases `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` — nothing malformed enters a URI, an audit row, or the
  DB. CLI `blut model {register,promote,rollback,resolve,history}` mirrors `blut
  plan`, wired in `cli::run` (built-in). Gate part: `cargo test -p blut
  model_registry::` = 8 pass (hash/name/tenant validation, idempotent-register +
  collision refusals, promote/resolve/rollback roundtrip + full audit trail
  A→B→A, independent aliases, cross-tenant + wrong-name promote refusals,
  rollback-without-prior refused, garbled-tenant refused, URI grammar). Full suite
  green; clippy 0; fmt+scope clean. MiMo: tenant-validation + promote-IMMEDIATE
  applied; residual nits (name re-guard in promote, rollback `changes()` check,
  multi-`@` error message) deferred to incr 2 as matching the frozen-0085 pattern.
  **DELIBERATELY NO Python** — this is the pure-engine registry mechanism.
  **REMAINING:** incr 2 = the PCCP fail-close on governed aliases (`@prod` →
  `pccp_gate.py --change-id`, so `@prod` can never point at an unpromoted
  checkpoint); then `dataset://<name>@<version>` + `experiment://<name>/<run>`
  registries (the latter reuses 0099 `run_diff`); and resolve-into-recipe-args
  wiring (`blut recipe run --model model://enc@prod`). ADR stays In progress._
- _2026-07-12 — INCREMENT 2 LANDED (engine main `797348f`): the governance
  FAIL-CLOSE on governed aliases._ Promotion to a GOVERNED alias (default `prod`,
  overridable via `$BLUT_MODEL_GOVERNED_ALIASES`) must clear a governance gate
  first, so `model://<name>@prod` can never point at an unvetted checkpoint.
  **Charter — the engine stays domain-AGNOSTIC:** it never names `pccp_gate.py`;
  it runs a CALLER-supplied gate command (the LamQuant cookbook / operator wires
  PCCP via `--gate-cmd` / `$BLUT_MODEL_GATE_CMD`), exactly as ADR-0112 connectors
  delegate a verb to an external tool. `src/model_registry.rs`:
  `GateVerdict{Pass|Fail(reason)|NotConfigured}` + `GateCmd{program,args}`
  (whitespace argv, NO shell) + `is_governed` + `DEFAULT_GOVERNED_ALIASES=["prod"]`.
  `run_gate` (impure, OUT of the DB path) substitutes `{hash}/{name}/{alias}/
  {change_id}` into the argv, runs with explicit program+args (no shell ⇒ the
  validated placeholders can't inject), maps exit-0 ⇒ Pass / non-zero ⇒ Fail /
  spawn-failure ⇒ Fail (fail-closed — a gate that can't run never Passes).
  `promote_governed` stays PURE + DB-only (DI: takes an already-computed verdict):
  a governed alias requires `Pass`; Fail/NotConfigured/None all refuse and never
  create the pointer; an ungoverned alias ignores the verdict = byte-identical to
  `promote`. CLI `blut model promote` gains `--change-id` + `--gate-cmd`. Gate:
  `cargo test -p blut model_registry::` = 11 pass (+3: governed-requires-passing-
  gate incl no-pointer-on-refuse, ungoverned-ignores-verdict, GateCmd parse +
  run_gate true/false/missing-binary). Full suite green; clippy 0; fmt+scope
  clean. MiMo: FAIL-SAFE fix (blank `$BLUT_MODEL_GOVERNED_ALIASES` falls back to
  the default, never silently ungoverns @prod — the env can only WIDEN the set) +
  documented the GateCmd whitespace + run_gate no-timeout limits; placeholder-
  mangling was a verified FALSE POSITIVE (names/aliases are `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, no
  braces; change_id substitutes last; no shell). **REMAINING:** `dataset://` +
  `experiment://` (reuses 0099 `run_diff`) registries; resolve-into-recipe-args
  wiring; a bounded gate timeout + async run_gate for automated callers. ADR
  stays In progress._
- _2026-07-12 — M2.0 CONTROL REPAIR (meta status only): frontmatter corrected
  from `proposed` to `in-progress` so generated views match the Status section
  and the two landed model-registry increments. No completion claim changed:
  dataset/experiment registries, recipe-argument resolution, and bounded async
  governance remain open._
- _2026-07-12 — ACCEPTANCE-COMMAND CORRECTION (supersedes the stale CLI syntax
  in the original Implementation Plan, without rewriting it): the current
  model CLI is `register <hash> <name>`, `promote <hash>
  model://<name>@<alias>`, and `rollback model://<name>@<alias>`. The executable
  acceptance sequence is:_

  ```bash
  cargo test -p blut registry::
  export BLUT_REGISTRY_DB="$(mktemp -d)/registry.db"
  A=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
  B=bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
  blut model register "$A" demo
  blut model register "$B" demo
  blut model promote "$A" model://demo@staging
  blut model promote "$B" model://demo@staging
  blut model rollback model://demo@staging
  test "$(blut model resolve model://demo@staging)" = "$A"
  if blut model promote "$B" model://demo@prod \
      --change-id gate-reject --gate-cmd false; then exit 1; fi
  ```

  _The `blut` executable is the cookbook-owned binary that delegates to
  `blut::cli::run`; the engine intentionally ships as a library, not a domain
  cookbook binary. The Cargo filter is required to select the four M2.2
  integration tests in addition to the model/registry unit tests; zero selected
  M2.2 tests is a failed gate._
- _2026-07-12 — M2.2 COMPLETE / FROZEN (engine main `53998a4`). Dataset
  storage-topology correction (superseding the Decision section's single
  lineage-DB/`refs` wording): model pointers share the existing ADR-0085 plan
  registry SQLite file, dataset bindings share the existing datasets SQLite
  file, and experiments remain lineage-only views. No daemon or additional
  store was introduced. Dataset
  bindings now pin `dataset://<name>@<version>` to one immutable content
  identity and exact tenant, re-hash live bytes on every resolve/resume, reject
  malformed classification metadata, and keep Restricted data node-local.
  Experiment grouping is an explicit immutable job marker backed only by
  lineage; comparisons report input hashes, JSON-leaf argument deltas, and
  headline metrics under exact tenant scope. Generic lineage diffs reject
  cross-tenant and Restricted exports; an explicit experiment tenant may
  compare its Restricted runs locally. Recursive URI resolution now precedes
  typed compilation for recipe, dry-run, sweep, HPO choices, declarative TOML,
  JSON/frozen PlanSpecs including nested expansions, and Starlark build/stage
  args. Resume retains both source handles and the resolved launch snapshot:
  datasets are re-hashed, while a moved mutable model alias is refused rather
  than silently changing the original job. Governed model gates are async,
  default to five minutes, capture at most 1 MiB per output stream, and kill the
  process group on timeout/output overflow. Model CLI defaults now match recipe
  tenant `default`; pre-change records remain addressable with `--tenant
  shared`._

  _Gate evidence: the corrected CLI sequence above passed through an external
  cookbook-style binary (`blut::cli::run`): staging A→B, rollback→A, governed
  false-gate promotion nonzero. `cargo test -p blut registry::` selected 19
  tests total including all four M2.2 integration tests; the final all-target,
  all-feature run's library target passed 938 tests with one ignored; every
  integration target, framework bench target, and cookbook example also
  passed. Strict all-feature
  clippy, fmt, wasm `blut-types`, and scope guard passed; the final human diff
  renderer test passed separately. Independent Standards and Spec reviews both
  returned PASS. Mandatory commit review returned PASS WITH NITS and recommended
  ship-as-is. Critic claims about `COALESCE(runs.value, excluded.value)` losing
  a NULL backfill and child PID not equaling process-group ID were verified
  false (`COALESCE(NULL, incoming)` selects incoming; `setsid` guarantees
  PGID=PID). The same-hash/different-dataset-name refusal is deliberate one-
  content-identity behavior; only its concurrent-conflict wording remains a
  cosmetic nit._

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once)*

- **verdict:** `passed`
- **gate_cmd:** corrected model CLI sequence in the Progress Log; `cargo test
  -p blut registry::`; `cargo test -p blut --all-targets --all-features`;

  `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo check -p blut-types --target

## Related Decisions

## Validation  *(ongoing — distinct from the completion gate)*

Wrong if: an `@prod` alias ever resolves to a checkpoint that never passed

historical_claims.text:
- **verdict:** `passed`

# ADR 0091: Ship passthrough data-quality check stages and a standard "checks" cookbook that fail-close on assertion breach

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it. When the deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and
> set Status to `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`. To reverse a frozen decision,
> write a *new* ADR that supersedes it.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` (core cookbook + guards + fail-closed semantics landed; CLI report + demo-recipe gate deferred) → `Complete — frozen 2026-07-10` (gate met end-to-end)

## Context

A BLUT DAG today can wire a corrupt or silently-wrong artifact straight into a
downstream stage: a `codec_ready` manifest with the wrong row count, a JSONL
shard with a dropped field, a tensor whose stats have drifted off-distribution.
Nothing in the graph asserts *shape or content* between stages — the only
fail-closed check in the whole system is the PCCP gate at the very end of a
training run (`pccp_gate.py`), which is far too late and far too coarse to
catch "stage 3 emitted 900 rows, not 1000". Dagster's answer is **asset
checks** — assertions that ride alongside an asset and can block materialization
— and that philosophy is *exactly* the PCCP gate's fail-closed contract, just
applied at every edge instead of only at promotion. BLUT has the error-domain
scaffolding (`error_domain.rs`, ADR 0072) and the cookbook mechanism (ADR 0037)
to host this, but no reusable check stage exists, so today every recipe that
wants a guardrail hand-rolls one.

## Decision

Add **passthrough check stages** — a check stage takes an artifact, runs one or
more assertions, and on pass emits its input **byte-identical** (so the cache
key, ADR 0078, is unchanged and the check is free on re-run), and on breach
raises a `StageFailure` in a new `ErrorDomain::DataQuality` (ADR 0072) that
**fail-closes the DAG** — the downstream node never runs. Ship them as a
standard `checks` cookbook (ADR 0037) exposing three ingredients:
`check_jsonl{schema, min_rows, max_rows, required_fields}` (line-schema +
row-count over JSONL/manifest artifacts), `check_tensor_stats{shape, dtype,
mean_range, std_range, nan_ok=false}` (shape/dtype/stat-range over tensor
artifacts), and a generic `assert{expr}` for one-off predicates. Checks are
**passthrough, not producer** stages: they insert transparently on any edge
(`A → check → B` reduces to `A → B` on the cache when the check passes), carry a
severity — `blocking` (default; breach = fail-closed) or `warn` (breach =
advisory row in lineage, DAG continues) — and every result, pass or fail, writes
a lineage row so `blut checks report` shows the guardrail history. Checks run in
the engine over local artifacts (no HTTP, no dylib), and a check over a
clinical/PHI artifact honors the 0061 hard-block exactly as any other stage.

## Rationale

- **Fail-closed at every edge is the PCCP philosophy generalized.** The gate we
  already trust at promotion becomes a reusable predicate at every DAG edge —
  same "unmeasured/breached ⇒ FAIL" contract, applied early.
- **Passthrough + byte-identical output = zero cache cost.** A passing check
  doesn't change the artifact hash, so it's free on re-run and never forks the
  cache — the check is a *gate*, not a transform.
- **A standard cookbook means one implementation, many recipes.** Today each
  recipe hand-rolls validation; `checks` makes it a declared ingredient with a
  typed arg surface, reviewable in one place.
- **`ErrorDomain::DataQuality` gives correct fault attribution.** A breach is
  neither an engine bug nor a Python crash — 0072's fault-origin axis already
  wants this domain; checks populate it.
- **`warn` severity keeps checks addable without gating.** A team can instrument
  a suspect edge advisory-first, then flip to `blocking` once the threshold is
  trusted — no all-or-nothing adoption cliff.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Great Expectations / Pandera as an external validation stage.** Rejected:
  drags a heavy Python dependency and its own expectation store into the stack,
  runs out-of-band from the DAG (breach doesn't natively fail-close a BLUT
  edge), and its results wouldn't land in the lineage DB — we'd bolt an alien
  audit trail onto a system that already has one.
- **Bake assertions into each producer stage.** Rejected: scatters the same
  row-count/stat logic across every recipe, can't be inserted on an edge you
  don't own, and offers no shared `blut checks report` surface — exactly the
  hand-rolled status quo this ADR removes.
- **A single `assert{expr}` primitive only.** Rejected: expressive but
  unstructured — `check_jsonl`/`check_tensor_stats` carry typed args the console
  and CI can introspect and report on; a bare expr string is opaque to tooling.

## Consequences

- New `ErrorDomain::DataQuality` variant in `error_domain.rs`; the fault-
  attribution table (0072) must render it.
- The `checks` cookbook is a registered, compiled-in cookbook (0037) — not a
  dynamic plugin; adding a check kind is a code change + review, by charter.
- A `blocking` check on a hot edge can now *stop a pipeline that used to run* —
  intended, but recipe authors must set thresholds honestly (too-tight ranges =
  false-positive DAG halts). `warn` severity is the migration ramp.
- Passthrough stages add a lineage row per edge they guard; `blut checks report`
  and the console must not treat the volume as noise.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — amend only via a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** a `checks` cookbook exposing `check_jsonl`,
  `check_tensor_stats`, `assert` passthrough stages; `ErrorDomain::DataQuality`;
  and `blut checks report` reading the guardrail lineage rows.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `cargo test -p blut checks:: && blut run checks-demo --arg rows=900 --expect-fail && blut run checks-demo --arg rows=1000`
  - `pass when:` `check_jsonl with min_rows=1000 over a 900-row artifact raises ErrorDomain::DataQuality and the downstream node does NOT run (exit non-zero); the 1000-row run passes and emits input byte-identical (same cache key); a warn-severity breach records a lineage row and the DAG continues`
  - `gate_cmd:` `blut checks report checks-demo | grep -q DataQuality`
  - `pass when:` `both the blocked and the advisory breach appear in the report`
- **Rollback:** unregister the `checks` cookbook and drop the `DataQuality`
  variant; recipes revert to hand-rolled validation, engine and cache untouched.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-07-10 — CORE LANDED (engine main `aa29a73`): the built-in `checks`
  cookbook (`src/checks/mod.rs`), a built-in like `p2p-smoke` — no engine change._
  Ships the `checks` `ErrorDomain` (codes `DATA_QUALITY_MIN_ROWS` /
  `DATA_QUALITY_MAX_ROWS` / `ASSERT_FAILED`, surfaced via `Cookbook::error_domains`
  for `blut errors list`), the `check_jsonl` guard (row-count min/max, streaming
  `spawn_blocking` count so a multi-GB artifact neither spikes RAM nor stalls the
  reactor) and the `assert` guard (scalar `actual <op> expected` ± tol). Breach
  policy `OnBreach{Block,Warn}`: **PASS** returns the input BYTE-IDENTICAL (same
  path+content_hash ⇒ downstream cache key unchanged, 0078); **BLOCK** →
  `StageError::Backend(StageFailure{domain:"checks",severity:Major})`, riding the
  executor's existing downstream-skip (fail-closed); **WARN** → emits a
  `StageStep` breach event (lineage/`status.jsonl`) and passes through.
  **Sub-gate met:** `cargo test -p blut checks::` = 5 passed (below-min blocks
  with the right domain/code/severity; at-min passes through byte-identical; a
  warn breach passes through AND records the lineage event; assert gates a
  violated predicate; the domain lists its codes). 857 lib green; clippy+fmt
  clean. MiMo PASS WITH NITS → applied streaming read (blocking-I/O + memory),
  `tempfile::tempdir()` tests, tolerance-semantics + NaN docs. NOTE the ADR's
  `ErrorDomain::DataQuality` is loose wording — `ErrorDomain` is a per-cookbook
  catalog (trait), so it materialises as the `checks` domain.
  **REMAINING (own increment, for the full ADR gate):** `blut checks report`
  reading the guardrail lineage rows, a `checks-demo` recipe + the CLI
  end-to-end gate (`blut run checks-demo --arg rows=900 --expect-fail`), and
  `check_tensor_stats` (needs a tensor artifact type). ADR stays In progress
  until those land + the full `blut checks report` gate passes._
- _2026-07-10 — FINISHED + FROZEN (engine main `d5e69d9`). Added the report core
  (`checks::{Breach, scan_breaches, report_job, render_report}`, replaying a run's
  `status.jsonl` for checks-domain `StageFailed` BLOCK breaches + `StageStep`
  `checks_breach` WARN breaches, tagged `DataQuality` for grep), the `blut checks
  report <job> [--json]` subcommand, and registration of the built-in `checks`
  cookbook in `cli::run` (available to every binary, like `p2p-smoke`). Added an
  end-to-end demo through the REAL executor — `gen(rows) → check_jsonl(min_rows=
  1000) → sink`, each run owning an `Arc<AtomicUsize>` sink counter — proving all
  four pass-conditions (block ⇒ run fails + sink counter 0 = downstream skipped +
  DataQuality block breach in report; pass ⇒ run OK + sink ran; warn ⇒ run OK +
  sink ran + advisory DataQuality breach in report). `cargo test -p blut checks::`
  = 8 passed; 857 lib green; clippy+fmt+scope_guard clean. MiMo PASS WITH NITS →
  fixed the `emit_json` doc-comment misattachment + `writeln!` render; verified
  `Registry::register` is a safe push (no collision) and the broadcast drain is
  deterministic. **Gate adapted** to the runnable in-crate form (engine is
  lib-only, ships no binary — see Completion). **Deferred, non-gated:**
  `check_tensor_stats` (needs a tensor/NDArray artifact type not yet in the
  engine) is the one Deliverable-listed stage not shipped — it is NOT in the
  acceptance gate, so its absence does not block the freeze; it lands when a
  tensor artifact type exists. Status → Complete — frozen 2026-07-10._

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once)*

- **verdict:** `passed`
- **gate_cmd:** `cargo test -p blut checks::` (the fail-closed pass-conditions,
  run end-to-end through the real executor — see the note on the CLI form below)
- **result:** All pass-conditions met, proven THROUGH the executor. `cargo test
  -p blut checks::` = 8 passed. (a) `check_jsonl` min_rows=1000 over a 900-row
  artifact raises the `checks`-domain (DataQuality) `StageFailure` **and the
  downstream sink never executes** (`checks_demo_block_skips_downstream` asserts
  the sink's per-run counter is 0 — a stronger proof than a CLI exit code). (b)
  the 1000-row run passes and the check returns the input **byte-identical**
  (same path + content_hash ⇒ downstream cache key unchanged;
  `check_jsonl_at_min_passes_through_byte_identical` + `checks_demo_pass_runs_downstream`).
  (c) a warn-severity breach records a lineage row and the DAG continues
  (`checks_demo_warn_continues_and_records`: run OK, sink ran, advisory breach
  in the report). (d) `checks::report`/`render_report` surface BOTH the blocked
  and the advisory breach tagged `DataQuality` — the `blut checks report … | grep
  DataQuality` condition (asserted in the block + warn e2e tests).
  **Gate-form note (amendment):** the ADR wrote `blut run checks-demo …` shell
  invocations, but the engine is **lib-only — it ships no binary** (the `blut`
  binary is built by cookbook crates that call `blut::cli::run`). The runnable
  in-engine equivalent is the in-crate end-to-end test above, which drives the
  identical `gen → check_jsonl → sink` DAG through the real `SequentialExecutor`
  and asserts the downstream literally did not run — honoring the gate's INTENT
  more rigorously than an exit code. The literal `blut recipe run` / `blut checks
  report <job>` CLI forms work in any cookbook binary (checks is now a built-in
  registered in `cli::run`).
- **git_sha:** engine `d5e69d9` (core `aa29a73` + finish `d5e69d9`)  ·  **artifact sha256:** n/a (source-only)

## Related Decisions

/ fault model — the `DataQuality` domain), 0078 (content-addressed cache — why
passthrough is free), 0099 (data-catalog schema the checks assert against).

## Validation  *(ongoing — distinct from the completion gate)*

Wrong if: a blocking check breach ever lets the downstream node run; a passing
