# ADR 0097: Export Prometheus/OpenMetrics and OpenTelemetry telemetry from a sidecar crate so the engine stays HTTP-free

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it, so the original stays as historical record. When the
> deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and set Status to
> `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`. A frozen ADR is permanent. To reverse a frozen
> decision later, write a *new* ADR that supersedes it.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` → `Complete — frozen 2026-08-03`

## Context

Every competing orchestrator ships first-class metrics and distributed tracing:
Dagster, Flyte, Prefect, and Temporal all expose a Prometheus `/metrics`
endpoint and emit OpenTelemetry spans that stitch a run into Grafana/Tempo/Jaeger
dashboards out of the box. BLUT exposes **none** of this. Today an operator
reconstructs run health by tailing `status.jsonl` (ADR 0067) and reading the
lineage SQLite (src/lineage_db.rs) by hand — there is no time-series of broker
admission latency, mesh-dispatch RTT, cache hit-rate, per-stage duration, or the
ε privacy-budget gauge, and no way to trace a single stage across the hosts it
hopped through on the P2P mesh (ADR 0061). This is genuine white-space, not a
re-skin of an existing surface. The hard constraint is ADR 0034: the engine
source tree (`blut/src`) must not host an HTTP server or a scrape endpoint, and
per ADR 0083 all server/network concerns live in opt-in sidecar crates.

## Decision

Ship telemetry from a new sidecar crate `crates/blut-metrics` (dispatched as
`blut metrics` per the ADR 0083 external-subcommand convention), never from the
engine. The engine's only new responsibility is to **write** structured
telemetry records — counters, gauge samples, and span start/end events with a
`trace_id`/`span_id`/`parent_span_id` triple — into the existing
`status.jsonl` stream and lineage tables it already writes; these are typed in
`blut-types` (wasm-safe, serde-only) so both engine and sidecar share one wire
schema. `blut-metrics` tails those records and (a) serves a
Prometheus/OpenMetrics `/metrics` scrape endpoint exposing run/stage/broker/
mesh/cache/ε gauges and duration histograms, and (b) forwards reconstructed
spans to an OTLP collector, propagating trace context across mesh dispatch by
threading the `trace_id`/`parent_span_id` through the `HostedEvent` envelope so a
stage that hops hosts stays one connected trace. The engine never opens a socket;
the sidecar owns every byte of network I/O.

## Rationale

- **White-space parity at zero charter cost.** The engine already writes
  `status.jsonl` and lineage rows on the hot path; adding a monotonic
  `trace_id`/`span_id` triple and periodic gauge samples to records it already
  emits is a data change, not a server. All socket-facing work is quarantined in
  the sidecar, exactly where ADR 0034/0083 says it belongs.
- **Trace-context propagation is the differentiator.** A mesh run today is
  observable only per-host; threading the parent span id through `HostedEvent`
  turns N per-host fragments into one Jaeger waterfall — the thing operators
  actually reach for when a remote stage stalls.
- **One source of truth.** The sidecar derives metrics from the same
  `status.jsonl`/lineage artifacts the TUI and `blut sla check` read, so
  Grafana, the TUI, and CI cannot disagree about what happened.
- **Broker/ε visibility closes a governance gap.** Surfacing broker admission
  latency and the ε privacy-budget gauge as time-series makes the fail-closed
  guarantees (ADR 0046/0047/0061) auditable over time, not just at the instant of
  refusal.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Embed a `metrics`/`axum` exporter directly in the engine (the Dagster/Flyte
  shape).** Rejected outright: it puts a listening socket inside `blut/src`,
  which the scope guard (ADR 0083) fails CI on. The whole point of the sidecar
  boundary is that this is not negotiable.
- **Push metrics from the engine straight to an OTLP collector over gRPC.** Still
  an outbound network client compiled into the engine, still a charter
  violation, and it couples the engine to the collector's availability on the hot
  path — a slow collector would backpressure stage execution. Writing to
  `status.jsonl` and letting the sidecar forward decouples the two.
- **StatsD/UDP fire-and-forget from the engine.** Lossy by design (drops under
  load exactly when you need the data), no histograms, and still an in-engine
  network dependency. Rejected.

## Consequences

- Upside: BLUT reaches Prometheus + OTel parity with the incumbents; mesh runs
  become traceable end-to-end; broker/cache/ε metrics become dashboardable and
  alertable via `blut-notify` (ADR 0083) SLA rules.
- Upside: `blut-types` becomes the single telemetry schema; the web dashboard
  (ADR 0093) can read the same gauges without a second data path.
- Downside: the engine gains a small always-on cost — emitting gauge samples and
  span ids on the hot path (bounded to O(1) per stage-event; sampling rate is a
  config knob so it can be turned down).
- Downside: a new lockstep constraint — the telemetry record schema in
  `blut-types` is now shared by engine + sidecar and changes require a
  Progress-Log entry here.
- Load-bearing: `HostedEvent` gains `trace_id`/`parent_span_id` fields; anything
  that constructs a `HostedEvent` must carry them forward or the trace breaks.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — write once; amend only by a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** `crates/blut-metrics` sidecar binary serving an
  OpenMetrics-conformant `/metrics` endpoint and an OTLP span forwarder, driven
  entirely by engine-written telemetry records in `status.jsonl` + lineage_db;
  telemetry record types added to `blut-types`; `trace_id`/`parent_span_id`
  threaded through `HostedEvent` across mesh dispatch.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `scripts/scope_guard.sh && cargo test -p blut-metrics --test scrape_and_trace`
  - `pass when:` `exit==0` — scope guard confirms zero listening sockets in
    `blut/src`; the test runs a 2-host mesh fixture, scrapes `/metrics` and
    asserts the broker/stage/mesh/cache/ε gauges + stage-duration histogram are
    present with non-default values, and asserts the exported spans for a
    host-hopping stage share one `trace_id` with a correct parent chain
    (promtool/OpenMetrics-format check on the scrape body).
- **Rollback:** delete `crates/blut-metrics` and revert the `blut-types`
  telemetry records + `HostedEvent` field additions; the engine falls back to
  raw `status.jsonl` tailing with no behavioral change (the fields are additive).

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-08-03 — BUILT + FROZEN in three increments (engine `9f840b6` →
  `3de67b9` → `60d149c`)._
  1. **Wire schema (`9f840b6`)** — `blut_types::telemetry`: W3C-shaped
     `TraceId`/`SpanId` (all-zero rejected, since accepting it would fuse
     unrelated runs into one trace), `SpanContext::child()` as the only way to
     descend, `MetricName`/`Label` validated at CONSTRUCTION against the
     Prometheus grammar, and `TelemetryRecord`. In the keystone so producer and
     consumer cannot drift; the wasm32 gate still passes.
  2. **Engine emission (`3de67b9`)** — `StageEvent::Telemetry` carries the
     record FLATTENED, so ONE status.jsonl line is readable both as a stage
     event and as a `TelemetryRecord`: one line, two readers, no second stream
     that could disagree. Telemetry rides the LOSSLESS lane (a dropped sample
     is a silent hole in a time series). `HostedEvent` gained
     `trace_id`/`parent_span_id`, omitted when absent so an untraced line is
     byte-identical for pre-0097 readers.
  3. **Sidecar (`60d149c`)** — `crates/blut-metrics` links `blut-types` ONLY,
     never the engine, so the charter holds by construction. Counters
     max-merge (no false counter resets), label sets sort into the series key
     (no silently forked metrics), foreign lines are skipped as expected
     traffic. OpenMetrics rendering handles the whole-body-rejection cases:
     `_total` family naming, the mandatory `+Inf` bucket, label escaping,
     Inf/NaN forms.
  Deviation recorded: promtool is not installed in this environment, so the
  ADR's format check was implemented as an in-test OpenMetrics grammar check
  rather than skipped — and proven non-vacuous (it rejects five distinct
  malformed bodies). A gate that degrades silently is worse than one that
  fails loudly.

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once; this + the frozen Status line is the single freeze mark)*

- **verdict:** passed
- **gate_cmd:** `bash scripts/scope_guard.sh && (cd crates/blut-metrics &&
  cargo test --test scrape_and_trace)` — run from the crate directory as with
  every other standalone-workspace sidecar
- **result:** scope guard PASS and the engine contains ZERO
  axum/hyper/reqwest references (no scrape or OTLP socket in `blut/src`). The
  gate ingests a 2-host mesh fixture, serves the REAL router on a REAL socket,
  scrapes it over TCP, and asserts the broker/stage/mesh/cache/ε gauges and the
  stage-duration histogram are present with NON-DEFAULT values (a zeroed series
  would pass a presence check while telling an operator nothing); the
  host-hopping stage's spans share ONE `trace_id` with the remote span parented
  onto the dispatching span, and that chain survives into the OTLP payload.
  Sidecar 11 tests / 4 binaries, clippy 0, fmt clean; engine 18/18 suites (909
  tests), clippy 0. CI + release gates added.
- **git_sha:** engine `60d149c` (schema `9f840b6`, emission `3de67b9`, sidecar
  `60d149c`)

## Related Decisions

ADR 0083 (interface stack / sidecar boundary), ADR 0093 (web dashboard consuming
the same gauges), ADR 0067 (status.jsonl observability substrate this reads),
ADR 0034 (no-HTTP charter), ADR 0046/0047 (broker metrics source), ADR 0061
(mesh dispatch / ε budget).

stage-latency regression that can't be tuned away via the sampling knob.

# ADR 0098: Build cost/chargeback dashboards and fail-closed budget guards over the cloud-queue cost ledger

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it, so the original stays as historical record. When the
> deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and set Status to
> `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`. A frozen ADR is permanent. To reverse a frozen
> decision later, write a *new* ADR that supersedes it.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` → `Complete — frozen 2026-08-03`

## Context

Cloud spend is the line item an operator running remote compute watches most
closely, and it is a gap across the orchestrator field: Dagster, Prefect,
Metaflow, and Ray have no native chargeback — teams bolt on Kubecost or a cloud
provider's billing console after the fact. ADR 0082 landed the cloud compute
queue plus a **cost ledger** that records, per submitted job, the provider,
resource class, wall-time, and billed cost. That ledger exists and is written,
but nothing reads it: there is no per-run / per-tenant / per-provider spend
rollup, no budget cap that can actually stop a run before it overspends, and no
forecast of where an in-flight campaign's burn is heading. This ADR extends ADR
0082 (it does not supersede it) by turning that raw ledger into governance:
dashboards plus a fail-closed budget guard.

## Decision

Add cost accounting on top of the ADR 0082 cost ledger in two layers. **(1)
Engine layer — the budget guard:** a pure lineage/ledger read in `blut/src`
(charter-fine, no server) that, at job-submission time, sums prior spend for the
run/tenant against a declared budget cap and **refuses admission when the cap
would be exceeded** — a fail-closed STOP routed through the existing broker
admission path (ADR 0046/0047), never bypassing it; a missing or unreadable cap
is treated as cap=0 ⇒ refuse, not as "unlimited." **(2) Sidecar layer — the
dashboards:** `crates/blut-web` (ADR 0083) renders spend rolled up per run,
per tenant, and per provider, plus a linear burn-rate forecast (spend-to-date ÷
progress) with a projected time-to-cap. Every cost type consumed by both layers
lives in `blut-types` so the guard, the CLI (`blut cost report`), and the web
view read one schema. No PHI or clinical-tenant cost data crosses into a remote
provider (ADR 0061 hard-block remains fail-closed); cost rows for clinical
tenants stay local-only.

## Rationale

- **Native chargeback is a real differentiator.** Making per-tenant/provider
  spend a first-class, queryable rollup is something the incumbents punt to
  external tooling; BLUT already owns the ledger, so it can own the answer.
- **A budget cap is only real if it can STOP.** A dashboard that reports overspend
  after the money is gone is theater. Putting the cap check on the admission path
  means the cap is enforced before the provider is billed — the same fail-closed
  posture as every other governance gate in the system.
- **Reuse the enforcement path we already trust.** The cap check refuses via the
  broker admission gate rather than inventing a second kill path, so there is one
  place a run gets stopped and one audit trail.
- **Forecast turns accounting into planning.** Spend-to-date over run progress
  gives a time-to-cap projection an operator can act on mid-campaign instead of
  post-mortem.
- **Clinical isolation is non-negotiable.** Cost rows for PHI-bearing tenants
  never leave the local host, consistent with ADR 0061.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Report-only dashboards, no enforcement (the Kubecost shape).** Rejected: it
  leaves the one thing operators actually want — a hard spending ceiling —
  unbuilt, and overspend is only discovered after billing. Visibility without a
  STOP is not governance.
- **Enforce the cap inside the cloud-queue submitter as a bespoke check, outside
  the broker.** Rejected: a second admission/kill path that can drift from the
  broker's, duplicating the fail-closed logic ADR 0046/0047 centralizes. The cap
  must ride the existing admission gate.
- **Defer to the cloud provider's own billing alerts.** Rejected: provider
  alerts are per-account, lagging (hours), and blind to BLUT's per-run/per-tenant
  attribution — they cannot stop a specific run, only notify after the fact.

## Consequences

- Upside: BLUT ships native chargeback + a hard, pre-billing budget ceiling —
  ahead of the incumbents on cost governance.
- Upside: the ADR 0082 ledger stops being write-only; `blut cost report`, the web
  dashboard, and `blut-notify` budget-threshold SLA rules all consume it.
- Downside: budget caps become load-bearing config — a mis-set or absent cap
  fails closed and blocks submission (by design), which will surface as "why did
  my run get refused?" support load until operators internalize cap=0⇒refuse.
- Downside: forecasting is linear and therefore wrong for bursty/non-uniform
  workloads; it is advisory, and the hard STOP is the cap, not the forecast.
- Constrains: cost record schema in `blut-types` is now shared by engine guard +
  web + CLI; changes need a Progress-Log entry.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — write once; amend only by a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** engine-side `budget_guard` (lineage/ledger read hooked into the
  broker admission path) + `blut cost report` CLI; `blut-web` cost views
  (per run/tenant/provider + burn forecast); cost record types in `blut-types`.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `scripts/scope_guard.sh && cargo test -p blut --test budget_guard && cargo test -p blut-web --test cost_rollup`
  - `pass when:` `exit==0` — the budget_guard test asserts a job whose projected
    spend crosses the cap is REFUSED via the broker admission path (not a bespoke
    exit), that a missing/unreadable cap refuses (cap=0, not unlimited), and that
    a clinical-tenant cost row is never emitted to a remote provider; the
    cost_rollup test asserts per-run/tenant/provider sums and the forecast match
    a fixture ledger to the cent.
- **Rollback:** disable the budget_guard admission hook (jobs admit on broker
  policy alone, as before this ADR) and drop the `blut-web` cost views; the ADR
  0082 ledger continues to be written, just unread. Additive-only, clean revert.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-08-03 — BUILT + FROZEN (engine `e042529`)._ Both layers landed over one
  schema in `blut_types::cost`.
  * **Money is integer micro-dollars, never a float.** The predecessor ledger
    (ADR 0067 T3.1e) recorded `f64` abstract units and its own comment warned a
    currency ledger must be fixed-point; this ADR's gate requires sums matching
    "to the cent", which floating point cannot promise under repeated addition.
  * **One implementation of the rollup arithmetic**, in the keystone, called by
    the guard, the ledger reader, and the dashboard — duplicating it is how a
    system refuses a job over a figure its own dashboard disagrees with.
  * **Fail-closed:** a missing, unreadable, malformed, zero, or tenant-less cap
    all resolve to `BudgetCap::REFUSE_ALL` ($0.00, which refuses) — never
    "unlimited". `budget_guard` returns the broker's own `AdmitDecision`, so a
    budget refusal travels the same path as a memory refusal rather than a
    bespoke exit that would skip admission's auditing and containment.
    Restricted-tenant rows are filtered once, in shared code, before anything is
    summed for export — while staying fully visible to LOCAL accounting, since
    local-only is not the same as invisible. `forecast()` returns `None` for
    progress of 0/negative/>1/NaN rather than fabricating a projection, because
    a projected total of `0` reads as "free".
  * Found and fixed by its own test: `to_dollars_string` split on the CENT
    divisor, rendering `$0.99` as `$99.00`.
  * Noted for ADR 0092: `dot_blut()` now exists in three modules (sensord, cli,
    cost); consolidating it is precisely the ownership question 0092 owns, so it
    was left alone rather than refactored mid-ADR.

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once; this + the frozen Status line is the single freeze mark)*

- **verdict:** passed
- **gate_cmd:** `bash scripts/scope_guard.sh && cargo test --test budget_guard`
  and `cargo test --test cost_rollup` in `crates/blut-web` (the sidecar is a
  standalone workspace, so its half runs from the crate directory)
- **result:** scope guard PASS. budget_guard: a job crossing the cap is REFUSED
  through the broker `AdmitDecision` with a legible "$10.01 > $10.00" reason; a
  missing AND a malformed cap both refuse; another tenant's spend cannot consume
  this tenant's budget; the clinical row is withheld from export yet still
  counted locally. cost_rollup: per-run / per-tenant / per-provider sums and the
  burn forecast match the fixture to the cent ($15.00 at 25% progress projects
  $60.00, flagged over a $20.00 cap; zero progress yields no projection).
  Engine 19/19 suites (947 tests), blut-types 30, blut-web 5 suites; clippy 0
  everywhere, fmt clean, wasm32 keystone green.
- **git_sha:** —  ·  **artifact sha256:** —

## Related Decisions

ADR 0082 (cloud queue + cost ledger — this extends it), ADR 0096 (GPU/resource
scheduling that feeds resource-class cost), ADR 0108 (tenancy/quota governance),
ADR 0046/0047 (broker admission path the cap rides), ADR 0061 (clinical/PHI
hard-block), ADR 0083 (blut-web sidecar host).

## Validation  *(ongoing — distinct from the completion gate above)*

Wrong if: a run overspends past its declared cap without being refused (the STOP
leaked); a missing cap ever defaults to unlimited instead of refusing; clinical
cost data appears in a remote-provider ledger row; the cap check grows a second
kill path outside broker admission; or the reported rollups diverge from the raw
ADR 0082 ledger totals.

# ADR 0099: Expose a full artifact-provenance graph, per-model cards, and a run-diff tool over the lineage_db substrate

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it, so the original stays as historical record. When the
> deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and set Status to
> `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`. A frozen ADR is permanent. To reverse a frozen
> decision later, write a *new* ADR that supersedes it.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` (increment 1 — provenance graph + lineage tenant column) → `Complete — frozen 2026-07-11` (graph + card + diff; gate passes)

## Context

Asset-level lineage is a headline feature of the modern orchestrator: Dagster's
asset graph and Flyte's lineage view let a user click any output and walk
backward to every input, code version, and parameter that produced it — the
audit story regulated and research users both demand. BLUT has the raw material
but not the product. `src/lineage_db.rs` (the substrate landed under the ADR 0090
vision-Phase-11 track) records rows: which stage produced which content-addressed
artifact, with which args, under which run. What is missing is the **graph** over
those rows (artifact→artifact provenance you can traverse), a **model card** that
collates everything about one trained model (its training data, args, metrics,
and PCCP/acceptance-gate outcomes) into one signed view, and a **run-diff** tool
that answers "what changed between run A and run B?" — the first question anyone
asks when two runs of the same recipe disagree. This ADR extends the lineage_db
substrate; it does not re-decide the schema.

## Decision

Build three read-side capabilities over `src/lineage_db.rs`, keeping all
graph/card/diff computation as pure lineage reads in the engine (charter-fine —
no server) with rendering delegated to sidecars. **(1) Provenance graph:** a
`blut lineage graph <artifact>` query that traverses the producer/consumer edges
transitively to emit the full artifact→artifact DAG (as typed
`blut-types` rows and a DOT/JSON export), rooted at any content-addressed
artifact and walking backward to source inputs or forward to descendants. **(2)
Model cards:** `blut lineage card <model-artifact>` collates one model's
training-data artifacts, resolved args, recorded metrics, and its
acceptance/PCCP gate outcomes into a single deterministic, content-addressed card
(re-running on the same lineage rows yields a byte-identical card). **(3)
Run-diff:** `blut lineage diff <runA> <runB>` reports the symmetric difference of
two runs — differing args, differing input artifact hashes, differing metrics,
and gate-outcome deltas. Cache keys are unchanged: the graph reads the existing
content-addressed identities, it does not mint new ones. Clinical/PHI-tenant
lineage rows are never exported to a remote sink (ADR 0061 fail-closed); the web
rendering (ADR 0083 `blut-web`) reads the same typed rows the CLI emits.

## Rationale

- **The substrate is already there; only the read side is missing.** lineage_db
  records the edges — turning rows into a traversable graph is a query layer, not
  a new write path, so provenance parity with Dagster/Flyte is cheap and honest.
- **Model cards are the audit deliverable.** Collating data+args+metrics+gate
  outcomes into one signed, content-addressed view is exactly what a PCCP
  verification record (per the project's FDA-shaped change control) needs — the
  card becomes a reusable regulatory artifact, not just a dashboard tile.
- **Run-diff is the debugging workhorse.** "Why do these two runs differ?" is the
  most common question; answering it by diffing lineage rows (args + input hashes
  + metrics + gates) is deterministic and beats eyeballing two log files.
- **Determinism is a correctness property.** Because cards and diffs are pure
  functions of content-addressed lineage rows, they are reproducible and
  themselves content-addressable — a card can be cited by hash in an ADR or a
  verification record.
- **No charter drift.** All traversal is a read in the engine; only rendering
  leaves the engine, into the existing sidecars.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Rebuild lineage on a graph database (Neo4j) or an external catalog
  (OpenLineage/Marquez).** Rejected: it forks the source of truth away from the
  content-addressed lineage_db, adds a server dependency the charter forbids in
  the engine, and creates a sync problem between the cache's artifact identities
  and the catalog's. The graph must be a view over lineage_db, not a copy.
- **Model cards as hand-written Markdown per run.** Rejected: non-deterministic,
  un-diffable, drifts from reality the moment args change, and cannot be
  content-addressed or gate-checked. Cards must be derived, not authored.
- **Line-by-line log diff instead of structured run-diff.** Rejected: logs are
  noisy (timestamps, ordering) and don't isolate the semantically meaningful
  deltas (args/input-hash/metric/gate); a structured diff over lineage rows does.

## Consequences

- Upside: BLUT reaches artifact-lineage parity with Dagster/Flyte and adds
  deterministic, content-addressed model cards + run-diff that the incumbents
  don't offer as first-class, hash-citable artifacts.
- Upside: model cards double as PCCP verification-record inputs; run-diff becomes
  the standard triage tool when two runs of a recipe disagree.
- Upside: the web dashboard (ADR 0083) gets a lineage view for free by reading the
  same typed rows the CLI emits.
- Downside: transitive graph traversal cost grows with lineage depth; deep DAGs
  will need bounded/paged queries (the CLI exposes a depth limit) to stay
  interactive.
- Constrains: the graph/card/diff row types in `blut-types` become a shared read
  schema (engine CLI + web); changes need a Progress-Log entry. lineage_db's
  producer/consumer edge recording is now load-bearing — a stage that fails to
  record an edge produces a card/graph with a silent hole.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — write once; amend only by a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** `blut lineage graph|card|diff` CLI subcommands (pure
  lineage_db reads) emitting typed `blut-types` rows + DOT/JSON export; a
  deterministic content-addressed model-card format; `blut-web` lineage/card/diff
  views over the same rows.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `scripts/scope_guard.sh && cargo test -p blut --test lineage_graph_card_diff`
  - `pass when:` `exit==0` — against a fixture lineage_db: `graph` returns the
    full transitive producer set for a leaf artifact (no missing/extra edges);
    `card` is byte-identical across two runs on the same rows (content-addressed
    determinism) and includes data+args+metrics+gate-outcome sections; `diff`
    reports exactly the seeded arg/input-hash/metric/gate deltas between two runs
    and nothing else; and a clinical-tenant row is never present in an exported
    graph/card.
- **Rollback:** remove the `blut lineage` subcommands + `blut-web` views;
  lineage_db keeps recording rows as before (read-side only, additive), so revert
  is clean with no data-path change.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-07-11 — INCREMENT 1 LANDED (engine main `8bbae1e`): the provenance GRAPH
  (capability 1 of 3) + the ADR-0096 lineage tenant column that powers the
  fail-closed clinical export._ `lineage_db` v2→v3 adds `runs.tenant TEXT NOT
  NULL DEFAULT 'default'` (additive; a `PRAGMA table_info`-guarded `ALTER TABLE`
  migrates an extant v2 db); `RunRow.tenant` threaded through
  record_run/get_run/row_to_run, with the upsert using

# ADR 0100: Build a searchable, typed, lineage-linked dataset catalog over BLUT artifacts and deliberately stop short of a DVC-style dedup hub

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it. When the deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and
> set Status to `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`. To reverse a frozen decision,
> write a *new* ADR that supersedes it.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` → `Complete — frozen 2026-07-11`

## Context

BLUT knows a great deal about every artifact it produces — the ABIR type
(ADR 0069/0074), the content hash (0078), the producing stage and its inputs
(`src/lineage_db.rs`) — but a human cannot *ask* about it. "Which datasets are
EEG at 256 Hz?", "what produced `dataset://tuh@v3` and what did it feed?", "show
me every ABIR manifest tagged `sleep`" are all unanswerable without grepping raw
lineage. Dagster ships an asset catalog; DVC ships a dataset registry with a
content-addressed dedup hub and remote push/pull. The catalog UI is genuine
white-space for BLUT — nobody has built the *browse/search* surface — but the
dedup-hub half is **not** white-space we want: the content-addressed cache (0078)
already deduplicates, and a push/pull hub is a network data plane the mesh
(0079) and cloud queue (0082) already own. The gap is discovery, not storage.

## Decision

Build a **read-only dataset catalog** as an engine-side view over the lineage DB
and the ABIR type registry — a `blut catalog` surface (`search`, `show`, `tag`)
plus a queryable index — with **no new storage and no hub**. Each catalog entry
binds: the dataset's `dataset://name@v` handle (resolver shared with ADR 0090),
its **schema** (channel count, sample rate, dtype, window shape — read from the
ABIR manifest, not re-derived), its **artifact kind** (the ABIR/0069 type), its
**lineage links** (the producing stage + downstream consumers, straight from
`lineage_db`), free-form **tags**, and **provenance** (source corpus, hash,
ingest time). `blut catalog search "modality:eeg fs:256 tag:sleep"` filters the
index; `blut catalog show <name>` renders the entry + its lineage neighborhood;
`blut catalog tag <name> <tag>` appends a tag row. The catalog is a *projection*
— every field is derived from existing sources (ABIR types, lineage rows, the
0090 registry), so it can be rebuilt from scratch and holds no authoritative
state except tags. It **deliberately does not** implement content dedup (0078
does), a remote push/pull hub (0079/0082 do), or blob storage of any kind.
Clinical/PHI datasets carry the 0061 flag in their catalog entry and are
filtered out of any cloud-surfaced view; browsing is a local read (no HTTP —
a future `blut-web` sidecar, 0083, can serve it).

## Rationale

- **The data to catalog already exists, uncatalogued.** ABIR types + lineage +
  hashes are all recorded; the catalog is an *index and query* layer, so the
  build cost is a searchable projection, not new bookkeeping.
- **Schema comes from ABIR, not re-derivation.** 0069/0074 made the manifest
  carry typed modality/rate/shape; the catalog reads those fields, so it can
  never disagree with the artifact about its own schema.
- **Lineage-linked entries turn "what is this?" into "what made it and what
  used it?"** — the graph the operator actually needs, drawn from the edges
  `lineage_db` already stores.
- **Stopping short of a hub is a feature, not a shortfall.** Dedup (0078) and
  the network data plane (0079/0082) are already solved elsewhere; re-solving
  them here would duplicate a cache and a mesh. The honest scope is discovery.
- **A rebuildable projection has no drift class of bug** — except tags, there is
  no authoritative catalog state to corrupt; `blut catalog rebuild` regenerates
  it from lineage + ABIR.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Adopt DVC as the dataset layer.** Rejected: DVC's core value is its
  content-addressed dedup + remote hub, both of which BLUT already has (0078 for
  dedup, 0079/0082 for transport) — we'd import a second, overlapping data plane
  and a `.dvc` metadata format that duplicates ABIR. We want DVC's *catalog*
  ergonomics, not its storage engine.
- **Build the catalog as a writable source of truth (its own DB).** Rejected: a
  second authoritative store for schema/lineage that ABIR and `lineage_db`
  already own — guaranteed to drift. A rebuildable projection cannot drift by
  construction (tags excepted, which are additive).
- **Ship only the ADR 0090 `dataset://` resolver, no browse surface.** Rejected:
  the resolver answers "give me *this* dataset by name"; it cannot answer "find
  the datasets matching X" — discovery is the whole point of a catalog and the
  actual white-space here.

## Consequences

- A new catalog index (materialized view over `lineage_db` + ABIR types) and the
  `blut catalog search|show|tag|rebuild` subcommands.
- Tags are the one piece of authoritative catalog state — they need an append
  path and must survive a `rebuild` (rebuild reprojects derived fields, preserves
  tags).
- The catalog is **read-mostly and non-authoritative** — it must never be the
  place a schema or lineage fact is *edited*; those belong to ABIR and
  `lineage_db`. A field that disagrees with its source is a bug in the
  projection.
- Explicitly foregoing a hub means cross-machine dataset sharing stays the job
  of the mesh/cloud queue — the catalog shows what's *here*, plus registry
  handles for what could be fetched.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — amend only via a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** a catalog index (view over `lineage_db` + ABIR type registry),
  a tags table, and `blut catalog search|show|tag|rebuild` subcommands with a
  typed query grammar (`modality:` `fs:` `kind:` `tag:` `hash:`).
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `cargo test -p blut catalog:: && blut catalog rebuild && blut catalog search "modality:eeg fs:256" && blut catalog show tuh@v3 | grep -q 'produced_by'`
  - `pass when:` `search returns the seeded EEG-256 entries and no others; show renders the entry's schema + producing stage + downstream consumers from lineage; a tag added via 'catalog tag' survives 'catalog rebuild'; a clinical-flagged (0061) entry is absent from any cloud-surfaced view`
  - `gate_cmd:` `blut catalog show <schema-mismatch-fixture>; test $? -ne 0`
  - `pass when:` `a catalog entry whose projected schema disagrees with its ABIR manifest fails the consistency check rather than serving a stale field`
- **Rollback:** drop the catalog index + tags table + subcommands; discovery
  reverts to raw lineage grep; `lineage_db`, ABIR, and the 0090 registry are
  untouched.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-07-11 — LANDED + FROZEN (engine main `d3d6d73`). `src/catalog.rs`: a
  read-only PROJECTION over `datasets_db` + `lineage_db` (no new storage/hub/blob).
  `Schema` (modality/fs/channels/dtype) read from the dataset's ABIR manifest =
  its `metadata` JSON, never re-derived; `CatalogEntry` projected from a
  `DatasetRecord` + lineage neighborhood (`LineageDb::producing_stage` +
  `consumers_of`, both added); a clinical flag (restricted-tenant tag or
  `clinical:true`). `CatalogQuery::parse` (`modality:/fs:/kind:/tag:/hash:`,
  fail-loud on unknown key / bad term / non-numeric fs); `search()` with a
  `cloud_surfaced` flag that fail-closed excludes clinical entries (ADR 0061).
  Tags are the ONLY persisted state (`catalog_tags`, WAL) — they survive a
  rebuild; `verify_consistency()` fails on schema drift from the source manifest.
  CLI `blut catalog {rebuild,search,show,tag}` (`--cloud`/`--json`). **Gate met:**
  `cargo test -p blut catalog::` = 6 passed — fail-loud grammar; search returns
  only the `modality:eeg fs:256` entries; a clinical entry is local-visible but
  ABSENT from a cloud view; a tag persists (idempotent) + filters; a schema drift
  (fs 256→512) fails the consistency check; the lineage neighborhood projects.
  857 lib green; clippy+fmt+scope_guard clean. MiMo PASS WITH NITS → WAL on the
  tags store; verified build_index is used, hashes are lowercase at write, and
  schema-only consistency is the gate's intent. **GATE-FORM NOTE:** the ADR's
  `blut catalog rebuild/search/show …` shell invocations are adapted to the
  in-crate `catalog::` tests (the engine is lib-only — no engine binary; the CLI
  is wired for cookbook binaries); `blut-web` catalog browsing rides the ADR-0083
  crate split. Status → Complete — frozen 2026-07-11._

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once)*

- **verdict:** `passed`
- **gate_cmd:** `cargo test -p blut catalog::`
- **result:** exit 0 (6 passed). Search returns the seeded EEG-256 entries and no
  others; show projects the schema + producing stage + downstream consumers from
  lineage; a tag survives a rebuild (tags are the only persisted state); a
  clinical-flagged entry is absent from a cloud-surfaced view; and a schema-drift
  fixture fails the consistency check rather than serving a stale field.
  scope_guard PASS; 857 lib green; clippy + fmt clean.
- **git_sha:** engine `d3d6d73`  ·  **artifact sha256:** n/a (source-only)

## Related Decisions

ADR 0069 (ABIR typed IR — the schema/kind the catalog indexes), 0074 (ABIR
production migration — manifests carry the typed fields), 0078 (content cache —
the dedup the catalog does NOT re-implement), 0079/0082 (mesh / cloud queue —
the transport the catalog does NOT re-implement), 0090 (registry — shares the
`dataset://` resolver).

## Validation  *(ongoing — distinct from the completion gate)*

Wrong if: a catalog field is edited as a source of truth (schema/lineage must
live in ABIR/`lineage_db`); a `rebuild` drops user tags; a projected schema
diverges from its ABIR manifest without failing; a clinical-flagged dataset
surfaces in a cloud view; or scope creeps into blob storage / a push-pull hub
(that belongs to 0078/0079/0082).

# ADR 0101: Add a partition abstraction with partition-aware execution, backfill windows, and a status matrix

<!-- The title IS this ADR's one-line summary in the generated index/digest. -->

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it. When the deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and
> set Status to `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-07-10` → `In progress` → `Complete — frozen 2026-07-12`
(engine `6744182`)

## Context

BLUT executes a DAG **once** over its inputs. There is no first-class notion of
"run this same graph over each slice of a partitioned domain, track which slices
are done, and fill the gaps." Every partitioned workload today is faked: a shell
loop over corpora, a hand-maintained list of which datasets have been ingested,
a re-run of the whole graph when one corpus arrives late.

This is genuine white-space versus the competition. Dagster's central data-model
is the **partitioned asset** — a definition parameterized by a partition key
(daily dates, categories), with a UI matrix of which partitions are
materialized/stale/failed, and a **backfill** that launches the graph across a
selected key range. Airflow has scheduled backfills over `execution_date`
windows. BLUT has neither the key nor the matrix — so it cannot answer "which of
the 40 corpora have a current codec-ready manifest?" without a side script, and
cannot re-run only the stale slice.

The workloads that want this are concrete and already in the repo:
- one LMA manifest **per corpus** (~40 corpora), each a partition;
- codec eval **per dataset × preset**, a 2-D partition space;
- time-windowed ingest as new recordings land.

Constraints: partitions must ride on the existing content-addressed cache (0078)
so a materialized partition is *free* to skip; a backfill launches many stages
and therefore must flow through the never-OOM broker (0046/0047) — a backfill can
never storm the box; and the clinical/PHI hard-block (0061) applies per partition
(a `Restricted` partition is refused, never silently skipped-as-done).

## Decision

Add a **partition abstraction** as a thin, typed layer over the existing DAG —
the graph is unchanged; a partition parameterizes *which inputs* it runs over:

1. **`PartitionKey` + `PartitionSpec`.** A stage/asset may declare a
   `PartitionSpec`: `Time { granularity, tz }`, `Categorical { values }`, or a
   `Multi` product of the two (dataset × preset). A concrete run carries a
   `PartitionKey` (e.g. `2026-07-05` or `tuh_eeg×fast`) that flows into the
   node's cache key — so each partition is a distinct content-addressed
   artifact, and a materialized one is a cache hit.
2. **Partition-aware execution.** `blut backfill <asset> --partitions <range>`
   expands the range into one PlanSpec instance per key (reusing 0078's dynamic
   fan-out, `map_output`), submits them, and lets the cache skip already-done
   keys. Each expanded stage is an ordinary broker-admitted launch — the backfill
   is bounded by admission, never a parallel flood.
3. **Partition status matrix.** A `PartitionStatus` store (a table in the
   existing lineage SQLite, no new service) records per key:
   `{materialized | stale | failed | restricted | missing}`, derived from cache
   presence + last-run lineage rows. `blut partitions status <asset>` renders the
   matrix as text (and the TUI/web sidecars read the same table — charter-safe,
   no in-engine server). "Stale" = an upstream partition's artifact hash changed.

`--partitions` accepts a range (`2026-07-01:2026-07-08`), an explicit set, or
`--missing`/`--stale` selectors so a backfill targets exactly the gaps.

## Rationale

- **Partition key in the cache key is the whole trick.** It makes "materialized"
  and "skip if done" fall out of the existing content-addressed cache for free —
  no new done-tracking state to keep consistent, and it honours the 0078 charter
  (the key is *extended* with the partition, existing un-partitioned keys are
  unchanged since their `PartitionKey` is `None`).
- **Backfill = fan-out we already have.** ADR 0078's `map_output` dynamic DAGs
  already express "one instance per element"; a backfill is that pattern with the
  element being a partition key, so this rides proven machinery.
- **The matrix answers the operator's real question** — "what's done, what's
  stale, what failed" — from the lineage DB the sidecars already read, needing no
  charter-violating dashboard service.
- **Per-partition PHI hard-block** keeps a `Restricted` corpus from ever being
  marked done-by-skip: it shows `restricted` in the matrix and is refused at
  admission, fail-closed (0061).

## Alternatives Considered

- **Keep the shell-loop status quo (external per-corpus scripts).** Rejected:
  the done-list is hand-maintained, drifts from reality, has no staleness notion,
  and re-runs the whole graph when one corpus lands late — the exact toil this
  abstraction removes. It also can't express dataset×preset 2-D spaces cleanly.
- **A separate partition-tracking service/daemon (Dagster-daemon style).**
  Rejected on charter: ADR 0034 forbids an in-engine service/supervisor. The
  status lives in the existing lineage SQLite and is read by CLI + sidecars — no
  new process.
- **Encode partitions as distinct hand-written DAGs (one graph per corpus).**
  Rejected: N copies of the same graph is unmaintainable and defeats the cache's
  cross-partition reuse; a change to the shared stage would need N edits.

## Consequences

- `PartitionSpec`/`PartitionKey` become additive `blut-types` serde types; the
  node cache-key function gains a `partition: Option<PartitionKey>` input that is
  `None` for existing un-partitioned nodes (their keys unchanged).
- A new `partition_status` table in the lineage SQLite (additive migration); the
  TUI/web sidecars gain a matrix view reading it.
- `blut backfill` and `blut partitions status` are new CLI subcommands;
  `backfill` is a thin driver over 0078 fan-out + broker admission.
- Commits us to defining "stale" precisely (upstream artifact-hash change); a
  wrong staleness rule either re-runs too much or serves outdated partitions.
- A large backfill (40 corpora × N presets) is throttled by the broker, so it may
  take wall-clock time — correct by design (never OOM), but the matrix must show
  `missing` vs `in-flight` so an operator doesn't mistake throttling for failure.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — amend only by a dated Progress Log entry)*

- **Deliverable:** `PartitionSpec`/`PartitionKey` types + partitioned cache key +
  `blut backfill` + `blut partitions status` + the lineage-DB status matrix.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `cargo test -p blut partitions -- --nocapture` (a 3-key
    categorical asset: backfill all 3 → matrix all `materialized`; invalidate 1
    upstream → that key alone reads `stale`; `--missing` re-runs only it; a
    `Restricted` key is refused and shows `restricted`, never `materialized`) +
    `pytest -k partition_backfill`
  - `pass when:` exit 0 **and** an un-partitioned asset's cache keys are
    byte-identical to the pre-ADR baseline (partition = `None`).
- **Rollback:** the partition field defaults to `None` and is the last cache-key
  input; drop it and every existing key reverts. `blut backfill`/`partitions` are
  additive subcommands — removing them touches no existing path.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-07-10 — opened._
- _2026-07-11 — INCREMENT 1 LANDED (engine main `bc63bc6`): the richer per-cell
  status MATRIX._ `src/config/partition.rs`: `CellStatus`
  {Materialized | Stale | Failed | Restricted | Missing} + `CellStatus::derive`
  (clinical DOMINATES fail-closed — a restricted cell is Restricted regardless of
  run state; then None⇒Missing, non-`done`⇒Failed, done+upstream-drift⇒Stale,
  done+fresh⇒Materialized). `status_matrix()` maps a set's cells → status, with
  the `restricted`/`stale` predicates INJECTED (the ADR-0100/lineage hash
  comparison) so the derivation is a pure, testable function; the `stale_of`
  check is short-circuited to materialized cells only (its lineage cost is not
  paid on Missing/Failed/Restricted cells). This is the read-side the
  `--missing`/`--stale` backfill selectors target. Gate part: `cargo test -p blut
  partition` = 15 passed (incl `cell_status_matrix_derives_all_states` — all five
  states + clinical-dominates). 857 lib green; clippy+fmt clean. MiMo PASS WITH
  NITS → the stale short-circuit. **REMAINING (own increments):** the partitioned
  cache key (partition as the LAST, default-`None` cache-key input ⇒ byte-identical
  to the pre-ADR baseline when unpartitioned), `blut backfill <asset>
  --partitions <range>` execution wired to this matrix, the `blut partitions
  status` CLI render, the lineage-hash stale-detection feeding `stale_of`, and the
  cross-repo `pytest -k partition_backfill`. ADR stays In progress._
- _2026-07-12 — M2.0 CONTROL/GATE REPAIR (engine main `058c232`)._ The original
  `cargo test -p blut partitions -- --nocapture` command was a substring filter
  that executed **zero tests** and exited 0, so it was not a fail-closed gate.
  The runnable progress gate is now `cargo test -p blut --test
  partition_backfill -- --nocapture` (1 passed). It proves the already-landed
  persisted missing-cell work list plus all five read-side matrix states. Source
  audit also corrects the prior remaining-work wording: `blut partition
  backfill` already runs cells through `run_one_recipe`, per-cell admission, and
  a shared cross-cell RAM semaphore. Still open: partition identity in cache
  keys, stale/missing selectors wired to the matrix, lineage-derived staleness,
  matrix-aware CLI rendering, and per-cell Restricted refusal. Therefore this
  named target is a progress gate only; the full acceptance gate remains unmet
  and the ADR stays In progress._
- _2026-07-12 — M2.3 PARTITION COMPLETION LANDED (engine main `6744182`; feature
  `81e617a`, reviewed hardening `6744182`)._ `PartitionSpec`, `PartitionKey`,
  `PartitionValue`, and time granularity are WASM-safe `blut-types` contracts.
  Every static node, map template, and runtime-spawned subplan carries the
  partition into the cache key; `partition=None` retains the exact pre-ADR
  golden key. The lineage v5 projection and tenant-scoped canonical JSONL
  derive Materialized only from a matching done run, current source/compiled

  Cache-hit jobs emit current-job metadata and cache proof, so a warm retry is

  explicit/range selection, default/`--missing`/`--stale`/`--force` selectors,
  tenant isolation, exact one-cell stale recomputation, and pre-launch
  Restricted refusal. This corrects the original gate wording: an invalidated

  (1 passed), and `pytest -q tests/test_blut_partition_backfill.py -k
  partition_backfill` (1 passed). Final repository evidence: 776 default tests;

  bench targets passed; strict all-feature clippy, fmt, `blut-types`
  `wasm32-wasip1`, scope guard, and diff checks passed. Independent Standards

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once)*
