# ADR 0168: One data layout, one archive wire — and never a physical path inside a digested payload

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. As
> implementation proceeds, **append** dated entries to the Progress Log — never
> rewrite or delete earlier text; correct an earlier statement with a *new* dated
> entry beneath it, so the original stays as historical record. When the
> deliverable passes its gate, fill **Completion** and set Status to
> `Complete — frozen YYYY-MM-DD`. A frozen ADR is permanent. To reverse a frozen
> decision later, write a *new* ADR that supersedes it (updating this one's
> Status pointer is the only edit allowed after freeze).

## Status

`Accepted 2026-08-10.` First child of ADR 0167 (the consolidation constitution),
carrying its invariants **1 (one data root)** and part of **2 (one provenance
identity)**. **D1 was confirmed by the owner on 2026-08-10** — freeze the sealed
set, seal forward — which was the only item blocking acceptance. D2 landed the
same day. See the Progress Log.

## Context

ADR 0167 fixed the invariants. This is the first migration under them, and it is
the one everything else waits on: the derived caches, the sealed cohorts, the
training manifests and the corpus archives all address the same bytes through
four different conventions.

**Everything in this section was measured on 2026-08-09, not inferred.**

### The layout

| path | size | holds |
|---|---|---|
| `/mnt/4tb/data/Archive/lma` | 867 GiB | the 14 canonical `.lma` corpora — the only source |
| `/mnt/4tb/data/Training` | 73 GiB | derived caches (`fb_cache` 526,226 `.npy`, `l3_cache`, `l3_cache_snn`, `manifests/`) |
| `/mnt/4tb/data/training` | **20 KiB** | an empty husk one capital letter away |

`/mnt/4tb` is 3.7 TB, 1.5 TB free. The largest corpus, `tueg_v2.0.2`, is 716 GiB
on its own, so a convert-in-place needs headroom it does not currently have.

The lowercase husk deserves a sentence, because 0167's table recorded it at 48 GB
and it is now 20 KiB: **its harm was never the bytes.** An empty directory one
letter from a live root is *more* dangerous than a full one, because every
`is_dir()`-style check passes on it and reports success.

### The wire

All 14 archives begin `4c4d4132` — `LMA2`. `lma_forensic.rs` already states the
problem and the mapping: LMA1/LMA2 *"predates \[ADR 0139 contract 5] and is the
last large store-side holdout"* — a bespoke header, bespoke JSON manifest and
bespoke EOCD footer describing something BCS2 already models as
`ProfileId::FORENSIC_TREE_V1`. **Package 8 migrated the code; the data never
moved.** What is missing is a driver: `lml --help` has no convert/migrate verb.

### The finding that governs this ADR

`prepared_joint_cohort.py` contains two row builders, twenty-one lines apart.

`_semantic_cohort_row()` (`:433`) is deliberately path-free. Its docstring, in
full: *"Remove physical locator while retaining complete logical source
identity."*

`_joint_manifest()` (`:454`) emits `"path"` in every row, and `:740`/`:747`
digest exactly those bytes into `manifest_sha256`.

So the codebase already knows the right answer, states it in a docstring, and
then does the opposite in the payload that gets sealed. Measured consequence:

- **18,603 digest-covered path strings**, every one under `/mnt/4tb/data/Training`,
  across **13 of the 20** manifest files in **10 sealed cohorts** (the other 7
  manifests have no rows).
- All **20** `manifest_sha256` fields verified byte-bound to their manifest files.
- `immutable_artifact.py:28` raises `FileExistsError` rather than replace a
  sealed artifact — by design.

**The blast radius is not 20 files. It is 68, across 6 tiers, and it terminates
in the PCCP production checkpoints.** Reverse-reachability over the digest
citation graph inside `/mnt/4tb/lamquant-artifacts`:

| tier | n | what |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 13 | `{train,val}.manifest.json` — carry the paths |
| 1 | 19 | `cohort-receipt.json`, `qualification-role-receipt.json`, `*.snapshot.receipt.json` |
| 2 | 5 | `training-replay-authority.json` and **3 sealed `.snapshot.bcs2`** (1.6 GB, 262 MB, 84 MB) |
| 3 | 24 | **`student_encoder_joint_production.ckpt`, `decoder_tier3_joint_production.ckpt`**, their `.provenance.json`, candidate + recovery checkpoints |
| 4 | 3 | `codec_artifact_set.json` ×2, `package.stdout.txt` |
| 5 | 4 | PCCP gate evidence logs |

Both hops that make this alarming were spot-checked as **named provenance
fields**, not coincidental hex:

- `train.snapshot.bcs2` embeds `"cohort_receipt_sha256":"5dc818dd…"` in a BCS2
  role record;
- `student_encoder_joint_production.ckpt` embeds
  `train_artifact_sha256 = 77183165…`, the digest of that snapshot.

That is a genuine chain from a filesystem path to the artifact PCCP's
`production_sha256` contract binds.

### The relief, and it is decisive

**The sealed `.bcs2` payloads contain no path strings at all** — verified by
byte scan across all three. `dataset_root` in the receipts is a *hash*, not a
path. Every `logical_id` / `group_id` / `split_id` is path-free by construction.
So the physical locator never entered the semantic identity; it entered only the
one payload — `_joint_manifest`'s rows — that had no business carrying it.

### Live bugs found on the way (all confirmed present today)

| site | wrong |
|---|---|
| `env.sh:5`, `tools/bootstrap.sh:69` | `L3_CACHE_DIR=/mnt/4tb/data/Training` — the **parent** of the real cache. Masked only because `apply_env` overwrites it |
| `tools/scripts/bench_train_pipeline.py:68` | `L3_CACHE_DIR=/mnt/4tb/data/l3_cache` — **a path that has never existed.** The bench reports warm-cache timings against a cold path and cannot fail. It is producing wrong numbers today |
| `lma_dataset.py:113` | defaults to `Training/labels`, absent; the npz fast path misses every stem (defect #229) |
| `clean_data_cruft.sh:53-58` | `rm -rf` allow-list frozen on the old root; after the move it exits 0 having cleaned nothing |

`bench_train_pipeline.py` is the one to sit with. It is a **benchmark** whose
entire purpose is measuring cache-warm throughput, pointed at a directory that
has never existed on any machine, silently, for its whole life.

## Decision

### D1 — Do not re-seal history. Seal forward.  *(OWNER — the only open item)*

The 10 sealed cohorts are **records of training runs that already happened**.
They state where the data was at the time, and that statement remains true after
the data moves; what changes is that the record describes a past filesystem, not
the present one. Rewriting them to say something else would not make them more
true, and the cost is rewriting production checkpoints and PCCP gate evidence to
restore digests over history that did not change.

Therefore: the sealed set is **frozen as-is**. No manifest is rewritten, no
receipt edited, no `.bcs2` re-emitted, no signature re-taken. Replaying one of
those specific cohorts byte-for-byte requires the layout that existed when it was
sealed, and that is the correct meaning of an immutable record.

> **This reverses a policy recorded before the measurement.** The earlier
> decision — *"re-seal affected artifacts"* — was taken when the believed scope
> was "20 manifest files and 20 `manifest_sha256` fields, no signature breaks."
> The measured scope is 68 files terminating in `production_sha256`-bound
> checkpoints. That is a materially different question, so it is put again rather
> than assumed to carry over. **D1 needs owner confirmation before Phase 2 runs.**

### D2 — A physical path may never enter a digested payload

`_joint_manifest()` drops `"path"`, matching `_semantic_cohort_row()` twenty-one
lines above it. Row identity is `logical_id` + `source_sha256`; a reader resolves
the locator at read time from the current root. This is the root-cause fix, and
without it Phase 2 merely relocates the defect.

New cohorts sealed after D2 are migration-proof. Old ones stay frozen under D1.
The schema string changes, so this is a versioned change, not a silent one.

### D3 — Three directories, and the name states the contract

```
/mnt/4tb/data/
  corpora/     canonical archives — the ONLY source. Never regenerated.
  derived/     regenerable from corpora. Deletable at will, by definition.
  artifacts/   sealed evidence. Immutable, append-only.
```

Same filesystem, so the move is a metadata operation; the work is in the
references. A reader who has never seen this tree must be able to tell from the
directory name alone whether losing its contents is a catastrophe or an
inconvenience. `Training/` vs `training/` conveyed nothing.

### D4 — LMA2 → `FORENSIC_TREE_V1`, smallest corpus first

Reuse `lma_forensic.rs`'s stated mapping rather than inventing one: `content_id`
stays the hash of the *file*; the frame declares what it holds and which
capability recovers it (`Store` verbatim · `Zstd`/`CAP_ZSTD` ·
`Lml`/`CAP_LML_LOSSLESS_V1` · `+ CAP_LMA_SYNTHETIC_REEMIT`). Add the missing
`lml` subcommand to drive it.

Order `mental_arithmetic` (106 MB, 76 entries) → `tueg_v2.0.2` (716 GiB, 70,841),
so a converter bug surfaces on 76 entries. Verification is a **full 4-slice
roundtrip on every entry** via the existing `lml roundtrip` — signal samples, raw
EDF header, non-EEG channels, trailing partial-record bytes. Do not write a
second comparator.

Originals are kept until **every** corpus converts *and* passes an independent
second pass, then sequestered to `legacy/` — never deleted. A converter bug found
on corpus 12 must not already have cost corpora 1–11.

### D5 — The gate asserts NON-existence

`check_single_data_root.py` must refuse when either old root **exists**, not
merely check that the new one does. `Training/lma` and `Training/memmap` are
already empty husks, so every existence-shaped check passes on nothing — the same
defect class as the `cache_paths` trap and the tautological test that failed to
catch it (Progress Log, ADR 0167).

The in-process half of this gate **already landed**: `cache_paths.RETIRED_SUBPATHS`
(cookbook `3f76b2f`…`2963d41`) makes `data_root()` refuse a root still carrying a
migrated-away location. Phase 2 populates that tuple in the **same commit** that
flips the three `*_SUBPATH` constants, so no window exists where both layouts
resolve.

### D6 — Fix the four live bugs before the move, not with it

They are wrong today, independent of any migration, and one is actively emitting
false benchmark numbers. Fixing them inside the migration commit would make a
bug fix indistinguishable from a relocation in the diff.

## Rationale

- **The move is cheap; the references are the work.** Same filesystem, so bytes
  do not travel. Every hour of this migration is spent on things that *name* the
  data, which is exactly why D2 matters more than D3.
- **An immutable record you rewrite is not a record.** D1 is not pragmatism about
  effort; re-sealing to make a past run's paths match a present filesystem would
  encode a false statement into signed evidence.
- **The codebase already contains the right answer.** `_semantic_cohort_row`'s
  docstring is the specification D2 implements. This is not a new principle being
  imposed — it is an existing one that one function skipped.
- **Smallest-first is not caution, it is arithmetic.** A bug caught on 76 entries
  costs minutes; on 70,841 it costs a re-run of 716 GiB against a nearly-full
  disk.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Re-seal everything (the pre-measurement policy).** Rejected under D1 —
  68 files, terminating in `production_sha256`-bound checkpoints and PCCP gate
  evidence, to restore digests over history that did not change.
- **Symlink the old roots to the new ones.** Rejected: it makes both paths work
  forever, so nothing ever gets fixed and the gate can never go green. It also
  defeats D5, since the old root then genuinely exists.
- **Rewrite paths inside sealed manifests in place.** Impossible as well as
  wrong: `immutable_artifact.py:28` refuses replacement.
- **Convert the archives first, then move.** Rejected: converting needs the
  largest corpus's own size in headroom, which the reclaim in Phase 1 provides.
- **Keep LMA2 and wrap it.** Rejected — it is the last store-side holdout against
  ADR 0139 contract 5, and a wrapper adds a ninth identity rather than removing
  the eighth.

## Consequences

- Replaying the 10 frozen cohorts byte-for-byte needs the pre-migration layout.
  Accepted under D1, and it is what "immutable" means.
- D2 changes the cohort manifest schema, so cohorts minted before and after are
  distinguishable by schema string. Intended.
- Deleting `derived/` costs the eval/probe suite hours of regeneration —
  `fb_cache`/`l3_cache` feed `eval_finite_rate`, `eval_risk_limited_bytes` and the
  Ω-vision probes, **not** the production trainers.
- Holding all 14 originals until the second verification pass keeps ~867 GiB
  occupied longer than strictly necessary. Deliberate.
- **Rollback:** Phases 0–1 are reversible (nothing sealed changes). Phase 2 is a
  rename, reversible by rename. Phase 3 is additive — the LMA2 originals still
  exist and still decode — until the sequester step, which is the point of no
  easy return and comes last.

## Implementation Plan  *(the contract — amend only by a dated Progress Log entry)*

| phase | deliverable | gate |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | blast radius enumerated | **DONE** — 68 files / 6 tiers, above |
| 1a | `cache_paths` trap closed | **DONE** — cookbook `3f76b2f`…`2963d41`, 14 tests, mutation-checked |
| 1b | the four live bugs fixed | each cited path exists, or the setting is gone |
| 1c | reclaim headroom (~511 GB: 424 G cargo targets, 73 G derived, 14 G `.bak`) | `df` shows ≥ 716 GiB free before Phase 3 |
| 2 | `corpora/` `derived/` `artifacts/`; `*_SUBPATH` + `RETIRED_SUBPATHS` flipped in one commit | `check_single_data_root.py` refuses both old roots (D5) |
| 3 | D2 — `_joint_manifest` drops `"path"` | a newly minted cohort contains no `/mnt/` string |
| 4 | `lml` convert verb; 14 corpora smallest-first | 4-slice roundtrip total on every entry, twice |
| 5 | LMA2 originals sequestered to `legacy/` | `corpus_manifest.py verify` green on all 14 |

Phase 3 may run before Phase 2 — it is source-only and independent. Phase 4
requires Phase 1c.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last; never rewrite an earlier entry)*

- _2026-08-09 — opened._ Phase 0 and 1a complete before the ADR was written,
  which is the right order here: the ADR's central decision (D1) is only
  answerable with the blast radius in hand, and the pre-measurement policy it
  reverses was formed without it. Every number in Context is measured; the two
  provenance hops that make the blast radius alarming were opened and read rather
  than inferred from a digest match.

- _2026-08-10 — **D1 confirmed by the owner: freeze, do not re-seal.** Status
  moves to Accepted; Phase 1b and Phase 3 (D2) land._

  The 10 sealed cohorts, 3 `.snapshot.bcs2`, 24 checkpoints and the PCCP gate
  evidence stay byte-identical. Replaying those specific cohorts byte-for-byte
  requires the pre-migration layout, and that is the accepted cost — it is also
  simply what an immutable record means.

  **Phase 1b** (meta `10099dd4`, `1ba962a2`; cookbook `11f08dfb`): `bootstrap.sh`
  now writes only `LAMQUANT_DATA_ROOT`; `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s claim that submodules
  read `$LAMQUANT_DATA` is corrected; `bench_train_pipeline.py` is sequestered to
  `archive/retired_tools/` with a README indexing the directory; the label cache
  no longer defaults to a path that has never existed. `clean_data_cruft.sh` is
  deliberately NOT fixed — its allow-list is correct today and only becomes wrong
  after Phase 2, so it belongs there.

  **Phase 3 / D2** (cookbook `26f65ee`): snapshot manifest **v3**. Rows carry a
  root-relative `locator`; the reader supplies the root; `dataset_roots` is
  untouched because it was already a ContentId rather than a directory — verified
  against a real sealed manifest rather than assumed. The physical root lives in
  the cohort receipt's existing `cache_directory`, which is a record of where a
  run read from, not an identity.

  Two things worth recording because the obvious version of each is wrong:

  1. `root` is *enforced*, not ignored, when passed with a v1/v2 manifest —
     every absolute row path must already resolve under it. The first cut refused
     it outright, which was defensible but blocked any consumer serving all three
     schemas; enforcing turns the parameter into an audit and unblocks that.
  2. The three `build_prepared_joint_cohort` tests **do not cover this change** —
     they fail at `import abir` before reaching the writer, and did so before it.
     Four direct tests were added against the pure functions instead. This is
     noted rather than glossed because "the cohort tests pass" would have been a
     true sentence carrying a false implication, which is the defect class ADR
     0167 exists to refuse.

  Phase 2 (the move) is now unblocked and is the next unit of work.

- _2026-08-10 — **Phase 2 tooling built and proven; the move itself is not yet
  run.** Two corrections to D3, both forced by measurement._

  **`artifacts/` is not created, and D3 is wrong to imply it should be.** The
  sealed tree at `/mnt/4tb/lamquant-artifacts` names itself by absolute path in
  the receipt fields a verifier *reads* — `cohort_payload`, `dataset_document`,
  `label_definition`, `manifest` — and D1 froze those receipts. Moving the tree
  changes no digest, but it leaves every frozen receipt **unresolvable**: it
  would cost the verifiability of exactly what D1 preserved, in exchange for a
  tidier name. It already satisfies what `artifacts/` was for — outside the repo,
  immutable, append-only. **The three-directory scheme is `corpora/` + `derived/`
  under the data root, plus the sealed tree where it stands.**

  **`Archive/` holds more than `lma`.** `_decoder` (22 MB), `ASCII` (Bonn, 11 MB),
  `edf` (empty) and two symlink farms. The mover refuses to run on any
  unclassified entry rather than migrating part of a directory — that is how a
  fourth top-level location gets created by accident.

  **Symlinks, measured:** **740** under the data root. **727 are already
  dangling** (`Training/_farm_ingest/{chbmit,siena}` — broken today, pointing at
  an Archive layout that no longer holds what they want; Phase 1c reclaims them).
  The **13 live** ones are the `lma_manifest`/`lma_small` farms, and they break on
  the move. They are repointed **relative**, which is D2's lesson applied to the
  filesystem: a relative reference survives the next move, an absolute one has to
  be hunted down and rewritten every time.

  **The lowercase husk is not empty.** Earlier it was recorded as a 20 KB empty
  husk; it holds four memmap sidecars (`{fullband,l3}_{train,val}.meta.json`)
  describing memmaps that are gone — one of them still cites
  `Training/manifests/split_manifest_codec_ready.json`. The mover leaves them and
  says so; they need classifying before Phase 2 completes.

  Landed: `tools/scripts/check_single_data_root.py` (D5) with ten tests, and
  `tools/scripts/migrate_data_layout.py` (dry-run default, `--apply`,
  `--revert`) with nine. Both wired into `ci_local`'s foundation job.

  **The gate is deliberately not "assert the new root exists"** — `Training/lma`
  and `Training/memmap` are already empty husks, so every existence-shaped check
  passes on nothing. It asserts no *retired* location survives, in source or on
  disk, and reports NOT-APPLICABLE rather than green where the data root is
  absent, so it can never pass by having had nothing to look at. Its source half
  catches the `env.sh` class permanently: the two bugs that actually shipped are
  two of its ten tests.

  **Three real bugs in the mover were found by running it, not by reading it** —
  none visible in dry-run output: revert left both farm symlinks dangling; the
  husk restore ran after its parent directory had been renamed back, dying on
  `FileNotFoundError`; and apply left an empty `Archive/`, which is the exact
  husk shape D5 refuses, self-inflicted. This is the argument for the sandbox
  test being part of the deliverable rather than a convenience: a dry run shows
  what the plan *says*, never whether it is right.

  Revert is **not** a byte-identical inverse and should not be: it returns farm
  links relative where the originals were absolute. Restoring the absolute form
  would be restoring the defect. Pinned by a test so the difference reads as
  intent.

  **Not yet done: the move.** It renames 867 GiB of source-derived EEG and is the
  owner's call to run. The gate is green on the current tree, so nothing is
  blocked by tooling.

## Completion / Resolution  *(fill once; this + the frozen Status line is the single freeze mark)*

- **verdict:** _pending_
- **gate_cmd:** _pending_
- **result:** _pending_
- **git_sha:** _pending_  ·  **artifact sha256:** _pending_

## Related Decisions

ADR 0167 (consolidation constitution — this is its first child), ADR 0139 (ABIR
platform, frozen — D4 completes its contract 5 for the store side), ADR 0144
(BCS2-backed training window store), ADR 0090 and 0100 (dataset registry and
catalog), ADR 0166 (the provisional non-clinical codec whose evidence tree D1
freezes), ADR 0169 (one identity — consumes D2's path-free rows).

## Validation  *(ongoing — distinct from the completion gate above)*

- **Watch for a path re-entering a digested payload.** D2 fixes one producer. The
  general rule needs a check: any payload that gets hashed should be greppable for
  `/mnt/` and `C:\` and come up empty. Until that check exists, D2 is a fix and
  not an invariant.
- **Watch `stat_fingerprint_dir`** (`lamquant.rs:866-894`) — it hashes an absolute
  directory path into what reads as a content hash, changes on `touch`, and is the
  eighth provenance system per 0167's correction. Its fate is decided before
  Phase 2; if it survives unchanged, D2 is only half done.
- **Watch for the gate being satisfied by an empty husk.** D5 exists because
  `Training/lma` already passes an existence check while holding nothing.
- **Trigger for a superseding ADR:** any proposal to re-seal the frozen cohorts,
  or to reintroduce a physical locator into a hashed payload for convenience.

# ADR 0176 — Make one generated ADR overview the structural parent and implementation work-board

<!-- ADR-LIFECYCLE:BEGIN -->
> **Lifecycle:** `accepted`. Canonical source: frontmatter.
<!-- ADR-LIFECYCLE:END -->

## Status

`Proposed 2026-08-11` → `Accepted 2026-08-11` by owner decision.

## Context

LamQuant already generates an ADR index and digest, but both are secondary
navigation views. Numbered ADRs are exempt from the documentation parent gate,
and no generated parent shows the implementation queue separately from proposed,
complete, or historical decisions. As a result, `accepted` can remain ambiguous:
it means the decision is in force, not that its deliverable passed a gate.

Current measured baseline at acceptance is 162 ADRs: 54 accepted, 15 in progress,
28 complete, and 65 proposed or historical. The active queue therefore contains
69 ADRs. A preliminary scan finds 48 active ADRs without a concrete `gate_cmd`.
Those numbers must be regenerated from repository state rather than copied into
the overview.

## Decision

Generate `docs/ADR_OVERVIEW.md` from the canonical ADR model and make it the
literal documentation-tree parent of every numbered ADR. The overview places
`accepted` and `in-progress` ADRs in the active implementation queue, lists every
other lifecycle bucket, exposes runnable-gate coverage, and links to governance,
topic, and digest views. Parent coverage is fail-closed immediately. Existing
missing-gate debt is captured by an exact ratchet: new debt and stale exemptions
both fail.

## Rationale

- One generated parent gives contributors one entry point without creating a
  second hand-maintained roadmap.
- Literal `parent:` edges let the existing documentation-tree gate prove that no
  ADR is orphaned.
- `tools/adr_model.py` already owns lifecycle and relationship semantics; view
  generation must consume that module instead of reparsing frontmatter.
- A debt ratchet permits migration of legacy ADRs without making CI permanently
  red while preventing any new ungated accepted work.
- Lifecycle remains authoritative: an ADR leaves the active queue only through a
  valid transition to complete, falsified, or superseded state.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Keep only the generated index and digest.** Rejected: they list decisions but
  do not participate in the structural parent tree or enforce closure coverage.
- **Use a hand-maintained implementation roadmap.** Rejected: lifecycle counts,
  links, and gate coverage would drift from ADR source files.
- **Fail immediately on all legacy missing gates.** Rejected: it would make every
  unrelated change red until the full historical audit completed.
- **Treat proposed ADRs as active work.** Rejected: proposal review and accepted
  implementation are different queues.

## Consequences

- Every numbered ADR gains a frontmatter-only parent edge. Frozen body hashes
  remain unchanged because ADR freeze hashes exclude frontmatter.
- `docs/decisions/README.md` becomes governance guidance below the overview.
- Existing index and digest paths remain generated compatibility views.
- Accepted ADRs without runnable gates become explicit burn-down debt.
- Hosted and local document gates must execute the same strict ADR checks.

## Implementation Plan

- **Deliverable:** generated ADR overview, canonical model support for parent and
  gate coverage, literal parent migration, closure-debt ratchet, tests, and CI
  wiring.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `python3 tools/adr_lint.py --strict && python3 tools/doc_tree_lint.py && python3 tools/doc_compose.py && python3 tools/doc_views.py && python3 -m pytest -q tests/contracts/architecture/test_adr_governance.py && python3 tools/ci_local.py --job doc-tree`
  - `pass when:` every numbered ADR has the exact overview parent, every ADR
    appears once in deterministic generated views, active rows equal accepted
    plus in-progress records, new or stale closure debt fails, frozen hashes are
    stable, and local/hosted gates invoke the same strict checks.
- **Rollback:** revert overview, parent metadata, ratchet, and gate commits
  together; existing index and digest remain compatible throughout.

## Progress Log

- _2026-08-11 — opened and accepted._ Owner selected literal parent semantics,
  active = accepted + in-progress, and a staged hard gate.
- _2026-08-11 — implementation remeasurement._ Adding this ADR moved the corpus
  to 163 records and the active queue to 70. Concrete-command validation found
  51 missing runnable gates, not the preliminary 48; the first scan had counted
  conceptual or truncated `gate_cmd` prose as executable. The exact 51-ID set is
  now the ratchet baseline.

## Completion / Resolution

- **verdict:** _pending_
- **gate_cmd:** _see Implementation Plan_
- **result:** _unmeasured_
- **git_sha:** _pending_ · **artifact sha256:** _pending_

## Related Decisions

ADR 0139 (unified platform constitution), ADR 0167 (consolidation constitution),
and ADR 0168 (first consolidation child). ADRs 0169–0175 remain reserved for the
other ADR 0167 child programs.

## Validation

Supersede this decision if a generated parent becomes too expensive to validate,
if frontmatter-only parent edits invalidate frozen ADR integrity, or if lifecycle
and gate coverage cannot be represented without duplicating source-of-truth data.

# ADR 0177 — Build a trusted, capability-compiled firmware platform for every OH! board

<!-- ADR-LIFECYCLE:BEGIN -->
> **Lifecycle:** `proposed`. Canonical source: frontmatter.
<!-- ADR-LIFECYCLE:END -->

## Status

`Proposed 2026-08-12.` This master constitution remains proposed until owner
acceptance. After acceptance it remains open until every target-family child and
the aggregate system-qualification child pass their fail-closed gates. Creating
this ADR does not qualify a board, promote firmware, or authorize clinical use.

## Context

LamQuant already has the pieces of a programmable firmware platform, but not yet
one qualified platform contract:

- ADR 0139 makes ABIR-compatible Node graphs the semantic architecture and the
  MCU AOT realm a first-class execution target.
- ADR 0142 gives `blut-graph-core` deterministic graph verification, lowering,
  resource planning, BGP3 serialization, and bounded MCU execution.
- ADR 0151 requires byte-changing implementation identity to change and makes
  Host/`McuAot` equivalence the migration oracle.
- Current firmware authenticates BGP3 plans, binds physical steps to a static
  executable registry, and executes with caller-owned arenas.
- ADR 0167 requires one kernel set and reserves ADR 0175 for the broad, stable
  cross-language SDK surface after consolidation.
- ADR 0019 repaired Firmware Hub dispatch around a `probe-rs`-only tool policy,
  but its per-target build and flash assumptions cannot cover Zephyr, vendor
  loaders, secure boot, signed bundles, recovery, or qualification.

Those pieces establish compute semantics. They do not yet establish who owns
hardware authority, how application intent becomes a bounded runtime schedule,
which keys may authorize which behavior, how boards and modules declare
resources, how updates recover, or how equivalent behavior is proven across
three MCU families and both RP2350 instruction-set architectures.

The product requirement is one programming model across:

- an RP2350 product board and Raspberry Pi Pico 2, qualified on Hazard3 and
  Cortex-M33;
- an STM32N6 product board and STM32N6570-DK;
- an ESP32-P4 product board and ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board.

Product-board revisions and secure-element part numbers are not yet fixed here.
They are mandatory `BoardManifest` inputs before target qualification; this ADR
must not guess them.

## Decision

Build one trusted, capability-compiled OH! firmware platform. Applications
express semantic acquisition and processing intent; a signed profile and a
capability/resource compiler lower that intent into a content-addressed
`RuntimePlan`. A vendor-pinned trusted acquisition core validates the plan and
exclusively owns hardware authority. Current hardware uses an
`McuOwnedSupervisor`; future FPGA hardware uses the same explicit supervisor
contract with split authority and FPGA veto. Every supported board exposes the
same semantic graph, safety state machine, artifact model, OH Device Protocol,
and host tooling. Target adapters may differ internally, but protocol-visible
and safety-visible behavior may not.

## Governing Architecture and Interfaces

```text
untrusted application intent
  -> semantic graph + signed FirmwareProfile
  -> capability/resource compiler
  -> signed, content-addressed RuntimePlan
  -> trusted plan validation + acquisition core
  -> McuOwnedSupervisor now | FpgaSupervisor later
  -> AFE, clocks, triggers, slots, power, transport
```

Compiler output is not trusted merely because it compiled. Trusted boot and
runtime code verifies signatures, profile authority, board compatibility,
content identities, resource proofs, rollback counters, and exact BGP3 plan
identity before any hardware-affecting transition.

### Trust boundary and authority

Trusted core exclusively owns:

- acquisition state and transition authorization;
- clocks, timestamps, sample/frame counters, DMA, interrupts, and buffers;
- trigger input and trigger output arbitration;
- module enumeration, slot state, power budgets, rails, bias, and references;
- AFE configuration and electrical-state enforcement;
- faults, explicit data gaps, status indication, watchdog, safe shutdown, and
  recovery entry;
- plan admission and resource ownership after boot.

Applications submit bounded requests. They never receive HAL, Zephyr, RTOS,
register, DMA, interrupt-controller, raw clock, watchdog, or raw power-control
access. A public API that exposes one of those mechanisms violates this ADR even
if documentation labels it unsafe.

Current boards use `McuOwnedSupervisor`: trusted MCU code owns deterministic
timing and electrical enforcement. Future FPGA-equipped boards use
`FpgaSupervisor` with explicit split authority:

- FPGA owns deterministic timing, counters, triggers, slot power, fault
  isolation, power budgets, frame integrity, watchdog enforcement, and legal
  electrical states.
- MCU owns authenticated policy, profile validation, ABIR production,
  processing, storage, transport, diagnostics, and coordinated update.
- FPGA may reject or halt an MCU request. MCU has no bypass around an FPGA
  safety decision.

Physical FPGA implementation is not part of the current three-target program.
Supervisor protocol, simulator, fault model, and MCU/FPGA behavioral-equivalence
suite ship now. A later FPGA hardware qualification requires a separate ADR and
cannot inherit simulator evidence as silicon evidence.

### Acquisition state machine

All targets implement one normative state machine:

```text
Booting -> Safe -> Enumerating -> SelfTest -> Configured -> Armed
  -> Acquiring -> Stopping -> Safe

any permitted state -> FaultLatched -> Recovering -> Safe | Shutdown
any permitted state -> Shutdown
```

Each command, timeout, reset, watchdog event, power-loss point, module event,
and update event has an explicit legal transition or an explicit denial. Safety
degradation emits typed faults and explicit gaps; it never silently changes
rate, channel set, counter behavior, trigger behavior, power state, or evidence
quality. `FaultLatched` persists until policy-authorized recovery clears the
specific cause. Reset alone is not evidence that the cause cleared.

### Firmware profiles, keys, and modules

`FirmwareProfile` binds authority tier, accepted keys, capabilities, limits,
board/module allowlists, update channel, evidence eligibility, and development
unlock state.

- **Research:** requires an explicit, visible development unlock. Developer keys
  may replace trusted-core or application components. Resulting artifacts are
  marked research and cannot be accepted as general-product or clinical
  qualification evidence.
- **General:** trusted core remains vendor-pinned. Owner or vendor keys may sign
  applications and modules only within profile-declared bounds.
- **Clinical:** manufacturer-controlled approved keys, locked board/module/profile
  allowlists, controlled update channel, and qualification-bound artifact
  identities. Research unlock and developer keys are rejected.

Third-party device modules are statically linked, signed,
capability-declared, resource-bounded, and conformance-tested. No profile permits
dynamic native MCU code loading. Data-driven tables and weights remain data only;
their parser, schema, bounds, hash, and authority are trusted-core concerns.

### Runtime and platform adapters

Reuse ABIR, `blut-graph-core`, `Target::McuAot`, authenticated BGP3 plans,
existing kernels, and the firmware static executable registry. Firmware work
extends those contracts rather than creating a second graph language or an
alternate implementation-identity system.

Capability/resource compilation emits fixed tasks, priorities, stacks, queues,
arenas, memory placement, DMA channels, interrupt ownership, WCET budgets, and
backpressure policy. Applications cannot spawn tasks, select priorities, claim
interrupts, resize queues, or allocate real-time resources after admission.
No post-boot allocation is permitted on the real-time acquisition path.

Zephyr is an internal platform adapter, never a public SDK interface:

- RP2350 Cortex-M33, STM32N6, and ESP32-P4 start from a pinned Zephyr 4.4.0
  baseline.
- RP2350 Hazard3 retains the native Rust static runtime until equivalent Zephyr
  support passes the same qualification. Hardware being RISC-V-capable is not
  proof that a documented Zephyr Hazard3 build target exists.
- Trusted Rust core links as a static library. Architecture does not depend on
  Zephyr treating Rust as a first-class application language.
- A target child ADR may advance Zephyr only with complete semantic, safety,
  timing, protocol, update/recovery, and HIL evidence on every affected target.

At proposal time, official Zephyr documentation identifies 4.4.0 as a stable
release and documents maintained board support for
[STM32N6570-DK](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/boards/st/stm32n6570_dk/doc/index.html),
[ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/boards/espressif/esp32p4_function_ev_board/doc/index.html),
and Pico 2 through the documented
[`rpi_pico2/rp2350a/m33`](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/boards/raspberrypi/rpi_pico2/doc/index.html)
build target. Pico 2 documentation describes both Cortex-M33 and Hazard3
hardware, but that does not qualify a Zephyr Hazard3 adapter.

MCUboot and [MCUmgr](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/services/device_mgmt/mcumgr.html)
may supply internal boot, image-management, and update mechanics. Public device
management remains OH Device Protocol; clients never need to know which
bootloader, RTOS service, probe, or vendor utility a BSP uses.

### Public SDK and application model

The Rust package remains `lamquant-firmware-sdk`; examples may use the product
alias:

```rust
use lamquant_firmware_sdk as oh;

let session = oh::session()
    .acquire(oh::ads1299().channels(32))
    .process(oh::lossless())
    .output(oh::usb())
    .build();
```

`oh::acquire(...)` is a permission-bearing request to the trusted acquisition
system. `oh::input(...)` consumes existing device, stream, or archive data and
does not imply acquisition authority. Trigger output is a separate signed
actuator capability; acquisition permission never implies actuation permission.

Common workflows also support declarative `firmware.toml`. First complete SDK
release includes Rust, manifest schemas, and the `openhuman.firmware` Python
host package. Stable C ABI and C++ wrapper remain ADR 0175 work. ADR 0177 may
define their required semantics, protocol, and artifact inputs, but may not
freeze those cross-language source APIs early.

Licensing boundaries are explicit:

- SDK interfaces, schemas, host clients, examples, and bindings:
  `Apache-2.0 OR MIT`;
- shipping trusted-core implementation: `AGPL-3.0-or-later`;
- weights: separately packaged under their existing RAIL-M governance.

Every `FirmwareBundle` records applicable licenses. Linking, distribution, and
source-offer obligations are release gates, not README-only claims.

### Content-addressed artifacts

Child ADRs define canonical encodings and schemas for these versioned types:

- `FirmwareProfile` — authority tier, keys, policy, limits, allowlists, evidence
  eligibility, and update channel;
- `BoardManifest` — exact product/dev-kit revision, MCU/ISA, memory, peripherals,
  clocks, AFE/slot topology, secure-element identity, debug/unlock policy, BSP,
  and tool adapters;
- `ModuleManifest` — module identity, electrical limits, capabilities, resource
  demands, driver/kernel identity, calibration contract, and signatures;
- `RuntimePlan` — authorized BGP3 identity plus fixed tasks, resources, placement,
  timing, ownership, and failure/backpressure policy;
- `FirmwareBundle` — bootloader, trusted core, application, BGP3 plan, modules,
  weights, optional FPGA bitstream, board compatibility, hashes, SBOM,
  provenance, signatures, and rollback counters;
- `EvidenceBundle` — exact hardware, fixture, calibration, toolchain, source,
  artifact, command, observation, and signature bindings for a gate result.

Identity is domain-separated and canonical. Identical inputs produce an
identical `RuntimePlan` identity. Any byte-relevant input changes identity.
Artifact identifiers and rollback counters are never reused, including after a
failed migration or revoked release.

### One device protocol and one tool surface

OH Device Protocol owns authenticated discovery, capability negotiation,
acquisition control, data, clocks, triggers, diagnostics, updates, recovery,
explicit gaps, backpressure, reconnect, and faults. Transport adapters may carry
the protocol over USB, Ethernet, serial, or another qualified link; they do not
define competing device semantics.

`firmware` remains the sole user-facing command and Firmware Hub backend:

```text
firmware init
firmware doctor
firmware boards
firmware compile
firmware build
firmware test
firmware flash
firmware monitor
firmware diagnose
firmware recover
```

Board support packages select and invoke Cargo, west/sysbuild, `probe-rs`,
OpenOCD, STM32CubeProgrammer, and vendor tools behind typed adapters. Users and
SDKs do not construct vendor-specific command lines. At the first qualified
target cutover, this rule supersedes only ADR 0019's decision that `probe-rs` is
the canonical flash tool. ADR 0019's launcher-table, explicit-path, and
sequester-not-delete lessons remain applicable until separately superseded.

### Target contract

Qualification requires both product hardware and named development hardware:

| Family | Product target | Development target | Required execution |
|---|---|---|---|
| RP2350 | exact revision supplied by `BoardManifest` | Raspberry Pi Pico 2 | native Hazard3 and Zephyr-backed Cortex-M33 |
| STM32N6 | exact revision supplied by `BoardManifest` | STM32N6570-DK | Zephyr-backed Cortex-M55 |
| ESP32-P4 | exact revision supplied by `BoardManifest` | ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board | Zephyr-backed RISC-V |

Every row runs the same semantic, protocol, safety, timing, fault, update,
recovery, and HIL conformance suite. A development-kit pass does not qualify the
product board; a product-board pass does not remove development-kit support.
RP2350 passes only when Hazard3 and Cortex-M33 have equivalent protocol-visible
behavior under the same plan and fault corpus.

## Rationale

- Hardware authority must have one owner. Shared access between an application
  and trusted core cannot prove clock, DMA, trigger, or power invariants.
- Capability compilation preserves the semantic graph while making memory,
  scheduling, interrupts, and WCET reviewable before execution.
- Signed profiles separate research freedom from general and clinical evidence
  without maintaining three firmware architectures.
- One protocol and artifact family lets host software remain stable while BSP,
  RTOS, bootloader, probe, and vendor mechanics vary.
- Zephyr reuse lowers board-support cost where upstream coverage exists. Native
  Hazard3 runtime avoids pretending unsupported parity is already available.
- Simulator-first supervisor work makes later FPGA authority explicit without
  blocking current MCU-owned boards or treating simulation as silicon proof.
- Product boards and development kits catch different risks. Both are required
  for reproducibility, support, and recovery testing.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Give applications a restricted HAL.** Rejected: any direct register, DMA,
  interrupt, clock, or power access creates a second hardware authority and
  makes safety behavior application-dependent.
- **Expose Zephyr as the SDK.** Rejected: it leaks scheduling and driver details,
  cannot cover native Hazard3 equivalently, and makes host/application contracts
  depend on one RTOS.
- **Use one native bare-metal runtime for every board.** Rejected: duplicates
  mature board, driver, boot, and update integration while still requiring a
  common semantic and conformance layer.
- **Use Zephyr on Hazard3 immediately because Pico 2 contains Hazard3 cores.**
  Rejected: silicon capability and a qualified, documented build target are
  different claims.
- **Permit dynamically loaded native MCU modules.** Rejected: runtime code
  loading defeats static resource proof, task ownership, WCET analysis, and the
  signed executable registry.
- **Make `probe-rs` the universal flash mechanism.** Rejected: target boot and
  recovery requirements include vendor and sysbuild flows that one probe tool
  cannot honestly abstract by itself.
- **Wait for physical FPGA hardware.** Rejected: current targets are MCU-owned;
  delaying the supervisor contract would hard-code MCU-only authority and make
  future safety partitioning a breaking redesign.
- **Publish the complete C/C++ SDK now.** Rejected: ADR 0175 deliberately freezes
  broad cross-language compatibility after interior consolidation.
- **Qualify only development kits.** Rejected: dev kits do not prove product
  power, AFE, module, secure-element, clock, or recovery behavior.

## Consequences

- Firmware becomes a platform program, not one binary or one flash command.
- Trusted core and supervisor interfaces become safety- and security-critical;
  changes require child-ADR gates and new evidence.
- Applications become less powerful mechanically but more portable semantically.
- Zephyr, MCUboot, MCUmgr, probe tools, and vendor utilities become replaceable
  BSP implementation details.
- Static plans require explicit ceilings for memory, tasks, queues, DMA,
  interrupts, codec expansion, timing, and power. Unsupported requests fail at
  compile or admission time.
- Research unlocks create a permanent evidence boundary. Research output cannot
  be relabeled as general or clinical evidence after capture.
- Existing bare-metal firmware remains available during migration. Cutover is
  target-by-target only after parity and recovery gates pass.
- Physical FPGA qualification remains future work, but its authority contract
  can no longer be postponed or bypassed.
- ADR 0175 remains owner of stable C ABI and C++ wrapper compatibility. ADR 0177
  owns firmware semantics, trust, artifacts, protocol, and initial Rust/manifest/
  Python delivery needed to qualify the platform.

## Implementation Plan

### Child ADRs

| ADR | Scope | Required deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| 0178 | Trust and artifacts | profiles, tiered keys, secure boot, anti-rollback, canonical bundles, update, recovery |
| 0179 | Acquisition authority | normative state machine, `McuOwnedSupervisor`, future `FpgaSupervisor`, immutable status/fault/gap semantics |
| 0180 | Platform runtime | `BoardManifest`, BSP interface, Zephyr/native adapters, static task/resource-plan lowering |
| 0181 | SDK and compiler | Rust/manifest interfaces, BGP3 activation, resource proof, qualified third-party modules |
| 0182 | Protocol and tools | OH Device Protocol, Python host SDK, `firmware` CLI/TUI, diagnostics and recovery |
| 0183 | RP2350 qualification | product board plus Pico 2; Hazard3 and Cortex-M33 equivalence |
| 0184 | STM32N6 qualification | product board plus STM32N6570-DK |
| 0185 | ESP32-P4 qualification | product board plus ESP32-P4-Function-EV-Board |
| 0186 | System qualification | Raspberry Pi 5 HIL, cross-target equivalence, fault injection, update recovery, endurance, sealed evidence |

Each child must define runnable, fail-closed gates before acceptance. Missing
hardware, identity, measurement, tool, corpus, or evidence is FAIL or explicitly
blocked work; it is never a skipped pass.

### Execution order

1. Freeze trust, artifact, state-machine, protocol, and board-capability schemas.
2. Build host simulator, mock supervisor, compiler, and first complete synthetic
   acquisition graph.
3. Activate authenticated BGP3 execution in the trusted firmware runtime.
4. Bring RP2350 through a complete dual-ISA vertical slice.
5. Port the same contracts to STM32N6.
6. Port the same contracts to ESP32-P4.
7. Run shared Raspberry Pi 5 HIL and qualification campaign.
8. Freeze ADR 0177 only after all target and aggregate gates pass.

### ADR creation gate

- **Deliverable:** this proposed constitution, canonical lifecycle metadata, and
  generated ADR/documentation views.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `python3 tools/adr_lint.py --strict && python3 tools/doc_tree_lint.py && python3 tools/doc_compose.py && python3 tools/doc_views.py`
  - `pass when:` all commands exit 0 and generated views contain ADR 0177 exactly
    once under `proposed` with no unknown relationship or topic.

### Master completion gate

- **Deliverable:** qualified artifacts and sealed evidence from ADRs 0178–0186.
- **Acceptance gate (fail-CLOSED; unmeasured ⇒ FAIL):**
  - `gate_cmd:` `cargo run --locked --manifest-path firmware/Cargo.toml -p lamquant-firmware-conformance -- verify-all --evidence firmware/evidence/qualification.toml`
  - `pass when:` command exits 0 from the exact source and evidence identities
    recorded in `EvidenceBundle`. Until that package, command, evidence manifest,
    and every required hardware record exist and pass, ADR 0177 is not complete.
- **Rollback:** retain or restore the previous signed trusted core and profile for
  each target. A failed target migration does not move other target defaults.
  Never reuse artifact identities or rollback counters.

The master verifier must prove all of the following:

1. valid signatures, profile authority, anti-rollback, revocation behavior, and
   research-unlock evidence isolation;
2. deterministic builds and identical `RuntimePlan` identity from identical
   inputs;
3. capability denial, resource conflict, memory overflow, WCET overflow,
   malformed plan, incompatible board/module, and unauthorized module all fail
   closed before hardware authority is granted;
4. state-machine model checking covers every command, transition, reset,
   timeout, fault, replay, and power-loss point;
5. no post-boot allocation on the real-time path; bounded stacks, queues,
   interrupts, DMA ownership, buffers, and worst-case codec expansion;
6. OH Device Protocol golden, malformed, authentication, replay, downgrade,
   reconnect, backpressure, and resource-exhaustion vectors pass;
7. Host and MCU graph semantics agree, and applicable lossless outputs remain
   byte-identical under ADR 0151 identity rules;
8. every product board and development kit passes boot, BIST, acquisition,
   counters, trigger loopback, explicit-gap injection, transport, watchdog, safe
   shutdown, update rollback, and recovery;
9. RP2350 Hazard3 and Cortex-M33 expose equivalent protocol-visible behavior;
10. Raspberry Pi 5 HIL performs power cycling, flashing, capture, fault
    injection, diagnostic collection, and sustained recording;
11. maximum-load soak passes for every supported product target; and
12. evidence binds exact hardware revision, secure-element identity, toolchain,
    source SHA, artifact hashes, calibration identity, and test-fixture identity.

## Progress Log

- _2026-08-12 — opened._ Recorded master trust boundary, artifact and protocol
  constitution, three-family target matrix, dual-ISA RP2350 requirement, child
  ADR sequence, simulator-now/FPGA-later boundary, and aggregate fail-closed
  qualification command. No target qualification is claimed.

## Completion / Resolution

- **verdict:** _pending_
- **gate_cmd:** _see Master completion gate_
- **result:** _unmeasured; required conformance package and qualification evidence
  are future child-ADR deliverables_
- **git_sha:** _pending_ · **artifact sha256:** _pending_

## Related Decisions

ADR 0019 (Firmware Hub launcher/probe policy; probe-rs-only decision superseded
at first qualified platform cutover), ADR 0139 (ABIR platform), ADR 0142
(capability graph compiler and execution realms), ADR 0151 (Node/kernel identity
and byte equality), ADR 0167 (consolidation constitution), and ADR 0175 (reserved
broad cross-language SDK compatibility after consolidation).

## Validation

Supersede this ADR if any supported board requires a second public semantic
graph, device protocol, safety state machine, artifact identity system, or SDK
acquisition meaning; if application code must receive direct hardware authority;
or if `McuOwnedSupervisor` and future `FpgaSupervisor` cannot implement one
observable contract. Re-open a completed target qualification when its board
revision, secure element, boot chain, toolchain baseline, trusted-core identity,
protocol behavior, or safety/timing envelope changes outside its proven bounds.

adrs.preserved_body:
# ADR 0178: Remove the cross-repo pin cascade rather than keep paying it

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. Append dated
> implementation evidence and amendments to the Progress Log — never rewrite or
> delete earlier text.

## Status

`Accepted 2026-08-16`

Refines ADR 0150 (cross-repo revision coherence) and delivers the pin item ADR
0155 proposed on 2026-08-02 and never built. Supersedes neither: 0150's rules
remain correct, and this ADR removes most of the work they imply.

## Context

Twelve submodules pin each other by `rev =`. That duplicates a fact the meta's
gitlinks already record, and the duplication is the whole cost:

- **63 `rev =` strings across 28 manifests** must agree with **12 gitlinks**.
- `check_cross_repo_pins.py` resolves "integrated" from `git ls-tree HEAD` — the
  last *meta* commit — so one repin pass can only repair the layer that commit
  recorded. Convergence needs a commit-and-push round **per layer of the
  dependency graph**.
- Cargo resolves `git =` dependencies from the **remote**, so each layer must be
  pushed before the next can relock. The cascade is therefore not a local
  operation, which is the reason it gets deferred.

Measured 2026-08-16, on a session whose only goal was getting completed branches
onto main: absorbing two gitlinks produced 41 mismatches and 4 unresolvable
pins; repairing them produced 12 duplicate-linked packages against a declared
ceiling of 2; and the whole cascade had to be backed out. Several hours, net
zero.

Two facts make this worth an ADR rather than more tooling.

**The cascade is avoidable, and the avoidance was already in the tree.** The
root `Cargo.toml` has carried `[patch."https://github.com/Quitetall/blut.git"]`
for one crate — `blut-graph-core` — for some time. Nobody generalised it.

**Some fleet states have no valid intermediate.** codec-lossless main pins
`blake3 = "=1.8.2"`; ABIR pins `=1.5.5` in four crates. Two exact pins cannot
coexist, so no ordering of repins converges — and holding one owner back while
the others advance is precisely what manufactures duplicate links. This class is
not a tooling problem and no amount of automation fixes it.

## Decision

**1. The meta builds from its gitlinks, not from sibling pins.** Every
intra-fleet crate is `[patch]`ed to its submodule worktree. The meta resolves
zero fleet crates over git. A stale `rev =` in a sibling manifest is drift to be
repaired on a schedule, never a blocker for integration.

**2. Pins are not deleted.** Each owner still builds standalone with `--locked`
against the revisions it declares — `clean_clone_check.py` verifies exactly that
from the remotes — and the pin checker still reports drift. What changes is what
drift *costs*.

**3. Convergence is one command.** `tools/scripts/integrate.py` drives the
fixpoint: repin → relock → commit → push, per layer, until the checker reports
zero. It refuses rather than half-applies, and it generates the provenance
trailers the commit hook requires instead of bypassing the hook.

**4. It refuses three things by name**, each drawn from a failure that happened:

- **Fleet conflict** — two owners requiring incompatible exact versions of one
  dependency. Reported and stopped, because the repair is a coordinated bump and
  that is a decision, not a sweep.
- **Duplicate links** — the count may not rise. One crate version reachable from
  two sources is two distinct types to rustc.
- **Push order** — an owner is pushed before anything repins onto it. A cascade
  that is content-correct but unpushed is not partly done, it is broken.

**5. Preconditions are checked up front**, together, before any round starts: no
detached submodule HEADs, no pre-existing uncommitted work in an owner.

**6. Shared exact-pinned dependencies need one declaration.** A version that
more than one owner pins exactly must be declared in one place the fleet reads,
so incoherence is impossible rather than merely detectable. *Not yet built —
see Progress Log.*

## Rationale

- **Two sources of truth for one fact is the defect.** The gitlink already says
  which revision the tree integrates. A `rev =` restating it can only ever agree
  or be wrong, and keeping 63 of them in agreement with 12 gitlinks is work that
  buys nothing the gitlink did not already provide.

- **Batching does not fix a fleet with no valid intermediate state.** An
  integration train reduces how often the cascade runs, not what it costs, and
  the blake3 split would have hit the same wall with more changes bundled into
  it. Decoupling the meta build removes the blocker; the train is scheduling on
  top of that.

- **A refusal is cheaper than a rollback.** The 2026-08-16 cascade was
  discovered bad *after* it was committed and pushed, and backing it out cost
  more than the repair would have. Every guard above turns a rollback into a
  refusal.

- **Automating commits means automating provenance.** Bypassing the hook was
  never an option: an unattributed automated commit is exactly the kind this
  tree must be able to audit later.

## Consequences

1. A dirty `abir/` worktree now fails the **meta** build, not only ABIR's, since
   ABIR's `build.rs` fail-closes on a dirty checkout. This surfaces at the point
   of the mistake, which is the intended trade, but it is new behaviour.

2. Adding a fleet repository to the meta means adding it to `[patch]` **and** to
   `[workspace] exclude`. Miss the patch and its crates are fetched at a pinned
   revision while siblings come from worktrees — the double-link failure. Miss
   the exclude and cargo claims its crates for the meta workspace and fails on
   `workspace.package.edition was not defined`.

3. The pin checker will now routinely report nonzero drift on a healthy tree.
   That is intended. Its number is a queue depth, not an alarm.

4. `integrate.py` requires every submodule on a named branch. The fleet
   habitually sits detached after a gitlink sync, so this will refuse until
   someone attaches them — deliberately, because a commit on a detached
   submodule HEAD is unreachable.

## Gate

Every claim above is mechanically checkable, so this ADR carries a runnable gate
rather than an entry in the closure-debt allowlist.

- `gate_cmd:` `python3 tools/scripts/integrate.py && python3 tools/scripts/check_locks.py && python3 -m pytest -q tests/contracts/architecture/test_pin_decoupling.py`

What each leg proves: `integrate.py` with no `--apply` is the dry run, so it
exercises the preflight and the summary without writing; `check_locks.py` holds
the duplicate-link ceiling, which is the invariant a bad cascade breaks first;
and the contract test pins the decoupling itself — that the meta resolves zero
fleet crates over git, and that every patched repository is also excluded from
the workspace.

## Reversal triggers

Revisit if: the meta ever needs to build a fleet crate at a revision *other*
than its gitlink; `[patch]` and gitlinks disagree without the lock gate noticing;
`integrate.py` converges a cascade that a clean-clone build then rejects; or the
duplicate-link ceiling is raised rather than driven down.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last)*

`2026-08-16` — Accepted, with items 1–5 landed and item 6 outstanding.

Item 1: the root workspace patched all four ABIR crates to their worktrees and
excluded `abir` from the workspace. **Measured: git-resolved fleet crates 4 → 0,
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` 0 errors, and the pin checker still
reporting 13 mismatches** — that last number is the proof of decoupling, since
before this a stale sibling pin blocked the build outright.

Items 3–5: `tools/scripts/integrate.py`. Guards verified rather than asserted —
the fleet-conflict detector was tested against the real cargo text from the
blake3 split and correctly distinguishes it from ordinary drift; the duplicate
counter agrees with the lock gate; the dry run leaves the working tree
byte-identical; refusal exits 1.

The preflight in item 5 was **earned, not designed**. The tool's first real run
repinned eight owners, committed one, and only then discovered on push that the
submodule was on a detached HEAD — leaving the fleet half-rewritten and
requiring manual cleanup. A precondition discovered mid-cascade is a
precondition checked too late.

Item 6 is not built. The blake3 split remains live: ABIR pins `=1.5.5` in four
crates, codec-lossless main pins `=1.8.2`, and the meta therefore holds
codec-lossless at the last revision that integrates. BLAKE3 the algorithm is
version-stable so digests should not move, but ABIR is the forensic core where
blake3 computes content addresses, and that claim should be verified against the
golden vectors rather than asserted inside a dependency bump.

`2026-08-16` — Items 1 and 3 finished, item 6 superseded by what the fleet turned
out to be. **The cascade converged: 0 mismatched, 0 unresolvable, 0 unused
authorities, foundation gate PASS.**

**The patch table was missing its most important entry: this repository.**
codec-lossless's `lamquant-lml` pins `github.com/Quitetall/LamQuant`, so the meta
resolved five of its OWN crates twice — once as workspace members, once fetched
from its own remote at a revision it had long since passed. `lamquant_ops::
Transport` from `crates/lamquant-ops` was a different type from the one arriving
through codec-lossless. Adding the patch took duplicate-linked packages **7 → 2**,
the declared ceiling.

This ADR's gate was RED when the ADR was accepted. `test_pin_decoupling.py` named
all five crates. A gate that runs beats a decision that describes.

**Decision 3 was wrong in a way only a real run could show.** `integrate.py`
repinned every owner in one pass and judged the result. On a fleet more than one
layer deep that cannot work: it rewrote all 21 manifests and refused because ABIR
resolved from two sources in firmware, visualization and both cookbooks — those
owners had been repinned onto the new ABIR while still consuming codec-lossless
at its PUBLISHED revision, whose manifests named the old one.

The order is now derived, not hoped for: the owner graph is read from the
manifests and topologically sorted, and each layer is repinned, relocked,
committed, pushed **and recorded in the meta** before the next begins. Recording
is not bookkeeping — the checker resolves "integrated" from `git ls-tree HEAD`,
so a layer that is pushed but uncommitted is a layer the next one cannot see.

Three further defects surfaced only by running it, each fixed:

- `dirty_submodules()` read the SUPERPROJECT's status, which fires both for an
  owner with edits and for one whose gitlink merely differs. The tool tried to
  commit in an owner with nothing to commit and reported git's "up to date" as a
  failure. It now asks each owner about its own worktree.
- Commit and push were one loop over dirty owners, so an owner with an unpushed
  commit but nothing left to commit was never pushed — the exact way a consumer
  ends up pinning a revision no remote has.
- The duplicate guard judged a workspace once its OWNER settled.
  `training/cookbooks/core` declares no git pin at all yet reaches ABIR through
  PATH dependencies on repositories that settle two layers later. It is now
  judged only when everything it RESOLVES FROM has settled, read from both the
  lockfile's git sources and cross-repository path dependencies.

**Item 6 is not what this fleet needed; the real finding is a cycle.**
codec-lossless, firmware and visualization consume crates FROM the meta while the
meta integrates them. No ordering of repins closes that, and it is not a shared-
version problem at all. Measured: advancing the engine gitlink alone took
duplicate-linked packages 2 → 5, because the pinned meta revision's crates still
named the older engine.

It is handled by declaring the meta once in the authority registry, at a revision
chosen deliberately — the first where the meta's own crate pins agree with its
gitlinks. Three stale entries collapse into it (`7aa9217c` and `44c86a95` were
never registered at all, which is why the checker called them UNRESOLVABLE rather
than drift: it had nothing to resolve them against). That removed the last 5
unresolvable pins.

The tax is real and worth stating: every advance of a repository the meta's
crates pin forces a matching move here AND a bump in all three consumers.
`integrate.py` cannot do the last part, because an authority pin is a decision.
The fix that removes the tax is removing the dependency — codec-lossless
consuming `lamquant-ops`/`-tui`/`-config` behind an optional UI feature — not
better tooling.

**A gate checked something no fixer could reach.** `check_abir_foundation.py`
audits PEP 508 direct references (`name @ git+https://…@<rev>`) as managed edges,
but the repin sweep only ever enumerated `Cargo.toml`. Two Python pins sat stale
with no tool able to move them. The sweep now enumerates `pyproject.toml` too and
rewrites PEP 508 revisions through the same `submodule_map()`, so a Python
reference and a Cargo pin cannot disagree about what this tree integrates.

Also closed on the way: ABIR's `integration/adr0169`, and codec-neural's and
openecs's `integration/adr0168-cascade`, were merged into their mains. The whole
fleet had been pinning branch tips that their own mains did not contain.

legacy_gates.command: python3 tools/scripts/integrate.py && python3 tools/scripts/check_locks.py && python3 -m pytest -q tests/contracts/architecture/test_pin_decoupling.py
