# ADR 0179: Execution before elaboration — a gate is only a gate if something runs it

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. Append dated
> implementation evidence and amendments to the Progress Log — never rewrite or
> delete earlier text.

## Status

`Accepted 2026-08-17`

Implements the unexecuted half of ADR 0178 and closes the loop ADR 0034 left
open. Supersedes nothing. Refines ADR 0152 (fail-closed bug campaign) by
supplying the rule that campaign assumed: that a declared gate is a run gate.

## Context

This ADR exists because a Developer Productivity Engineering review of the whole
fleet found that the binding constraint was not build speed, tooling maturity,
or test depth. It was that **the enforcement this tree already owns was not
executing.** Five measurements, each verified against the live system rather
than inferred from a document:

**1. CI was not merely red. It was refused.** Every job in the meta and in the
private submodules failed in 2–4 seconds with a GitHub annotation: *"The job was
not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit
needs to be increased."* No step ran. The cause was structural and sat in the
tree in plain sight — `ci.yml::rust-workspace` was a four-platform matrix with
**two macOS legs at 10× billing** on unfiltered `push` with no concurrency
group, roughly **690 billed minutes ≈ $5.52 per push**, exhausting a $20 month in
about three and a half pushes. `training/engine`'s `macos-build` declared no
`timeout-minutes`, inheriting GitHub's 360-minute default: **~$288 of exposure
from one hung job**, fourteen months of budget.

**2. The file blamed the wrong cause.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` stated that an
unprovisioned `SUBMODULE_TOKEN` was *"the whole explanation for CI being red
since mid-June 2026."* `gh secret list` shows that secret has existed since
**2026-07-31**. Two independent repository surveys repeated the comment's claim.
A wrong root cause, written down, survived longer than the problem it described.

**3. The tests for the most load-bearing gates had never run.** `pyproject.toml`
set `testpaths = ["tests"]`, so `tools/tests` was never collected: **306 KB of
test code, 529 passing tests**, covering `check_abir_foundation`,
`check_kernel_ids`, `gate_unified_abir_platform`, `check_cross_repo_pins`.
Wiring it caught a real regression from four hours earlier — a cascade commit
had invalidated the ADR 0142 closure hash and **no running gate covered it.**

**4. The rule that catches unrun gates was itself unrun.** `ci_local.py
--check-coverage` enforces two rules: forward (every CI job has a local mirror
or a declared reason) and reverse (every gate-shaped tool is invoked or
exempted). Nothing invoked it, and it **exited 2**. Worse, the reverse rule had
never once reported in its life, because the forward rule failed first and
exited before reaching it — so `tools/check_pareto.py`, named **by path** in ADR
0109 as that ADR's acceptance gate, sat uninvoked with nothing saying so.

**5. Gates that are red after routine operations stop being read as signal.**
Six `gen8` evidence gates had been red since **2026-08-03** — each pins the
`codec-lossless` gitlink, so every routine cascade invalidates them, and it went
unnoticed for two weeks. `test_generated_topology_view_is_current` fired three
times in a single session. `semantic-core` is permanently red on a merge that
was compliant the day it was made and invalidated by a rule that landed the next
day; append-only history means it can never go green.

The common shape is not bad code. It is **good, finished, tested code that
nothing executes**, plus meta-rules that would have caught that and are
themselves unexecuted. The measured `unexecuted_tools` count on the day this was
written is **54**.

### What the external research changed, and what it did not

A 113-agent literature sweep with 3-vote adversarial verification ran alongside
the survey. Its most useful output was the **refutations**, because several
plausible recommendations died: ClusterFuzzLite private-repo support (refuted),
`cosmic-ray` as the viable Python mutation tool and its cost model (both
refuted), and **every 2026 pricing specific it surfaced** — GitHub's claimed
revenue cut, the self-hosted per-minute charge, both Ubicloud rates. No cost
model in this tree may rest on those numbers.

What survived and bears on this decision: `cargo mutants --in-diff` is a partial
gate **by construction** (a PR that deletes tests generates zero mutants and
passes green, 3-0); self-hosted runners have **no ephemerality guarantee**, and
`--ephemeral` makes only the *registration* ephemeral (3-0); and Bazel
abandonment is real and long-tailed — **11.2% of 542 popular adopters abandoned
after a median 638 days** (3-0), with the polyglot-payoff framing confounded and
Python-primary adopters abandoning at only 3.4%.

Two of the five research angles — event-driven CI/CD and monorepo-of-submodules
tooling — returned **zero surviving claims**. Those are precisely the two angles
closest to this repository's actual shape, so every recommendation in those
areas rests on our own measurements and is labelled as such.

## Decision

> **A gate is only a gate if something runs it, and a budget is only a budget if
> something enforces it. Until both hold, this tree adds no new capability.**

In order:

1. CI must be able to start jobs at all.
2. Every gate that exists must be reachable from an automated path, or be
   sequestered, or be explicitly exempted **with a stated reason**.
3. Cost must be capped structurally, not by intention.
4. Only then does depth get added — mutation testing, fuzz breadth, hermeticity.

Three corollaries, each of which cost something to learn:

**A declaration is not evidence.** A tool named in an ADR, a README, or an
evidence record is *claimed* to run. `check_wiring`'s original oracle counted any
basename mention anywhere as "wired" and therefore reported `orphan_tools: 0`
while `check_pareto.py` ran nowhere. Prose is a claim; only an execution path is
evidence.

**A fail-open gate is worse than an absent one.** It converts "unverified" into
"verified" at no cost to anyone. Measured example, and the reason this corollary
is stated rather than assumed: ADR 0178's own `gate_cmd` opens with `python3
tools/scripts/integrate.py`, whose dry run `return 0`s at
`tools/scripts/integrate.py:474` **whether the fleet is converged or not** — it
exits non-zero only on a cyclic graph. That leg cannot detect the drift the ADR
is about. Legs 2 and 3 do the real work. Wiring convergence *repair* as a gate
was the obvious move, and it was wrong.

**Ratchet; never arrive red.** A gate that is red on the day it lands gets
ignored, and then it is decoration. New measures freeze at their measured value
and may only shrink — the pattern `bonsai.lean.json`, `adr_closure_debt.toml`
and `wiring-ceilings.json` already use.

## Rationale

### Why not a build-system migration

The owner asked for Bazel/Buck2 to be evaluated seriously. It was, and the
evidence argues against it *now*:

- The strongest available evidence (ICSE'24, n=542) measures **11.2% abandonment
  after a median 638 days**, including at organisations with far more build
  engineering capacity than this project has: Google, Meta, Kubernetes,
  Microsoft. `kubernetes/kubernetes` ran Bazel 2016-12-13 → 2021-02-28 and left.
- The checklist's multi-language clause — the one that would favour us — is
  **confounded** by language identity, and Python-primary adopters abandoned at
  only 3.4%.
- Decisively: **our build is not the bottleneck; our CI does not run.** A
  hermetic build graph makes a correct answer arrive faster. We were not getting
  an answer at all. Migrating now optimises the wrong term.

Deferred with tripwires (below), not rejected.

### Why detection is automated and repair is not

`integrate.py` is the fleet's convergence command and ADR 0178 names it as such.
It is deliberately **not** on an automated path. Repair across 13 repositories
requires push rights to all 13, which the propose-only decision refuses, and its
dry run cannot serve as the detector (see the fail-open corollary). Convergence
is instead enforced fail-closed by `check_cross_repo_pins` and `check_locks`.
Detection runs by itself; repair stays operator-driven **by decision rather than
by oversight**, which is the distinction this ADR exists to make.

### Why the budget needed its own executable rule

Before this ADR the $20/month policy was written in exactly one place — a
comment in `firmware/.github/workflows/ci.yml` — and the meta violated it on
every push. Writing "a budget is only a budget if something enforces it" and
then shipping no enforcement would have reproduced the defect inside the
document condemning it.

## Consequences

- **Accepted:** wiring dormant gates surfaces failures that were previously
  invisible. That is the point. Ratcheting rather than blocking is what makes it
  survivable.
- **Accepted:** ~70 KB of cross-repo pin machinery is transitional and shrinks as
  ADR 0178's `[patch]` design lands. Hardening it further is not this ADR's work.
- **Accepted:** `unexecuted_tools` lands at 54 and `check_ci_cost` at 34/18/2.
  Those numbers are debt made visible, not new debt.
- **Rejected:** adding mutation testing, fuzz breadth or hermetic builds before
  the four ordered steps above hold.
- **Rejected:** any bot with write-to-main across the fleet. Automation may
  propose; humans merge.
- **Constraint inherited:** append-only history, owner-signed ADR 0139 evidence,
  and IEC 62304 traceability mean automation must satisfy the hooks rather than
  bypass them. `--no-verify` remains legitimate only where a push is itself part
  of a repair, and must be said so in the follow-up commit.

## Gate

Every clause above is mechanically checkable, so this ADR carries a runnable
gate rather than an entry in the closure-debt allowlist.

- `gate_cmd:` `python3 tools/ci_local.py --check-coverage && python3 tools/check_ci_cost.py && python3 tools/check_wiring.py && python3 -m pytest -q tools/tests/test_ci_local_coverage.py tests/contracts/`

What each leg proves, and why it is not redundant with the others:

- **`--check-coverage`** is clause 2 in both directions. Forward: no CI job
  lacks a local mirror or a stated reason. Reverse: no gate-shaped tool is
  uninvoked. It also refuses a stale `UNRUNNABLE` entry for a job CI no longer
  defines — a lie in the opposite direction — which it demonstrated by catching
  one within a minute of the workflow edit that created it.
- **`check_ci_cost.py`** is clause 3, fleet-wide including submodules: no
  unbounded job, no 10×/2× runner on a commit trigger, no commit-triggered
  workflow without a concurrency group.
- **`check_wiring.py`** holds the `unexecuted_tools` ratchet, which is the
  standing measure of clause 2 over time rather than at one instant.
- **the pytest leg** pins the CI-job inventory itself against silent
  under-reporting, and runs the whole contract tree — four of whose five
  subtrees were, until this ADR, run by nothing anywhere.

## Reversal triggers

Revisit if: CI stays green for a quarter **and** build time, not correctness,
becomes the measured bottleneck **and** someone owns build engineering as a
named responsibility (all three, for the Bazel deferral); a ratchet is raised
rather than driven down; `--no-verify` becomes routine rather than exceptional;
any gate added under this ADR is found to exit 0 on the condition it claims to
detect; or the propose-only constraint is relaxed to let a bot write to main.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last)*

- **2026-08-17 — Phase 1 landed; clauses 2 and 3 are enforced.** Seven commits.
  - `373f2816` — `testpaths` now collects `tools/tests`: 306 KB, 529 tests that
    had never run. Immediately caught the stale ADR 0142 closure hash. A pytest
    9.0.2 finding worth recording: for a file reached through `testpaths`,
    neither `--ignore` nor `--ignore-glob` nor `collect_ignore` excludes it —
    all three verified — only a module-level `pytestmark` skip works.
  - `48ab3748` — `--check-coverage` put on both paths: a new
    `audit.yml::meta-gates` job (authoritative) and a path-scoped
    `.githooks/pre-commit` guard (fast, local). Closed both orphans it had been
    hiding: `blut.yml::adr0103-async-io-python` (unmirrored) and
    `tools/check_pareto.py` (uninvoked). `meta-gates` is a **sibling** of
    `doc-tree`, never steps inside it — `doc-tree` materializes the release
    trust root on the family tag and its step sequence is hand-enumerated in
    `tools/test_release_plan.py`; repo hygiene does not belong in the job
    holding the trust root. Also carries `repository_graph.py --check`, closing
    the half of task #106 that matters.
  - `1f63b91f` — the whole `tests/contracts/` tree now runs, in CI for the first
    time. Four subtrees (wire, evaluation, governance, training; 37 tests) were
    collected by a bare `pytest` and executed by no job. External review of the
    prior commit produced one real finding and one refuted: partial matrix-leg
    recovery was silent (fixed — all-or-nothing, since total failure was already
    loud), while the claimed nested-array truncation was **wrong**, the regex
    anchors on `]'` and an inner `]` is followed by `}`. The test that settled it
    is now in the tree.
  - `80b96797` — restored the two gates `core.hooksPath = .githooks` silently
    orphaned. `pre-push` and the graphify `post-commit` had no replacement and
    simply stopped existing. **The new `pre-push` is deliberately not the old
    one:** `tests/run_diagnostics.py fast`/`full` both exit 1 today in 0.03s with
    "No test categories found" (all six category directories exist and hold zero
    `test_*.py`), so restoring it verbatim would have blocked every push. It
    gates convergence instead — pins, locks, provenance, meta-gates, **5.6 s** —
    because a push is the irreversible action and the failure that actually
    happened was a cascade that died *after* publishing two submodule revisions.
    Originals preserved at `.git/hooks-retired-2026-08-17/`, never deleted.
  - `73632d31` — `check_locks.py` wired into CI as the **first** step of
    `cargo-deny`. Position is as load-bearing as presence: `cargo metadata`
    rewrites a disagreeing lock, so a check after it validates a file cargo just
    repaired. Also added `unexecuted_tools` beside `orphan_tools` —
    **54 on arrival** — because a prose mention is a claim, not evidence.
  - `64c56c7a` — `check_ci_cost.py`: the budget made executable. Measured
    fleet-wide, submodules included: **34 unbounded jobs, 18 workflows with no
    concurrency group, 2 expensive legs on commit triggers.** Dropped the
    `macos-14` leg that paid 10× to re-run one pure-Python unittest. Two
    findings from looking rather than from a failing run: the metric could not
    see its own improvement until findings became per-leg (3 → 2 after the fix,
    and the leg that went was the 10×); and `meta-gates` would have died on
    `ModuleNotFoundError`, since `setup-python` provides a clean interpreter
    without PyYAML and CI is refused at dispatch, so it had never executed.
- **2026-08-17 — what remains, stated rather than implied.** Clause 1 is an
  owner action and is **not** discharged: the billing block must be cleared
  before any of this runs on a runner, and every gate above has therefore been
  verified locally only. `training/engine`'s unbounded `macos-build` needs a
  submodule commit and a gitlink cascade (task #107). The external release trust
  root must be re-issued with the new `audit.yml` digest before `oh-tech-v1.0.0`
  is tagged, or the terminal family gate fail-closes (task #110).
  `tests/run_diagnostics.py` is named in ADR 0152's `gate_cmd` and cannot pass
  (task #109). Phases 2–4 of the DPE plan — shared CI actions, committed fuzz
  corpora, `cargo-mutants --in-diff` paired with a coverage floor, the Bazel
  tripwire — are deliberately not started, per clause 4.
- **2026-08-17 (later) — this ADR's own gate was RED, and clearing it is the
  first thing it demanded of itself.** An ADR arguing "a gate is only a gate if
  something runs it" cannot ship with a `gate_cmd` that fails. Three of the four
  legs were failing; all three that were mine are now green.
  - **Leg 2 (`check_ci_cost`)** stood at `unbounded_jobs` **35 against a ceiling
    of 34**. The ceiling was NOT raised — this ADR names that as a reversal
    trigger. The meta's own twelve unbounded jobs were bounded instead, taking
    the fleet to **23**, and the ratchet was banked *down* to 23. Eleven of the
    twelve were in dormant `release.yml`, three of those on a `${{ matrix.os }}`
    matrix including macOS: unbounded at 10× billing is ~$288 per hung leg, and
    dormant makes that worse rather than better, because nobody is watching.
  - **Leg 4 (topology)** was stale twice within the hour, because a concurrent
    `integrate.py --apply` records a gitlink per cascade layer and each one
    invalidates the derived view. Regenerated at the layer-5 state. This is the
    staleness that rotted silently three times on 2026-08-16; it is now caught
    by the gate this ADR wired, which is the mechanism working, not failing.
  - **Leg 4 remains RED on exactly one root cause, and it is owner-gated.**
    `0111-blut-python-sdk.md`, frozen by a concurrent session minutes earlier,
    declares `Proposed → Complete`, skipping the intermediate state; all
    eighteen siblings in its family write `Proposed → In progress → Complete`,
    so the transition model is right and the document is malformed. The one-line
    fix was trialled and **reverted**: it clears the warning and raises a worse
    ERROR, `frozen ADR body changed after its frozen_body_sha256 was recorded`.
    Correcting it therefore requires re-blessing another session's freeze hash —
    asserting a new body is the frozen truth for work this session did not do.
    That is an authority act, not a cleanup. Task #113; file restored byte-exact.
  - Worth recording as method: a first attempt to test the freeze used a
    hand-rolled frontmatter split whose hash did not reproduce the declared
    `frozen_body_sha256` *before any edit*. That measurement was discarded
    rather than reasoned from, and `adr_model.load_repository` — the authority —
    gave the real answer. A broken measurement that agrees with your hypothesis
    is the most expensive kind.
- **2026-08-17 (close) — the gate is GREEN. `gate_cmd` exits 0, all four legs.**
  `--check-coverage` OK (36 CI jobs accounted for, 34 gate tools invoked or
  exempted); `check_ci_cost` OK at ceiling; `check_wiring` OK at ceiling;
  `pytest` 151 passed, 4 xfailed, 39 subtests, 0 failed.

  The last blocker closed the way it should have. ADR 0111's owner corrected it
  themselves in `2b988f1a` — "record 0111's intermediate lifecycle state and
  re-seal the body hash" — which is exactly the diagnosis filed as task #113 and
  exactly the authority that should have applied it. Declining to re-seal
  another author's frozen body was the right call, and the freeze mechanism did
  its job: it made a silent correction impossible and routed the change to the
  person entitled to make it. That is the ADR's thesis holding under its own
  first real test, rather than an argument in its favour.

  What this does NOT claim. The gate passing means every gate that exists is
  reachable and every ratchet holds **on this machine**. Clause 1 — CI able to
  start jobs at all — is an owner action still outstanding, so none of it has
  executed on a runner; that is stated in the entry above and unchanged here.
  Clause 4 keeps Phases 3–4 shut until clause 1 holds, which is compliance with
  this ADR, not work left undone.

# ADR 0180: Make the cost of a change proportional to the change

> **This file is append-only and living.** Write the decision once. Append dated
> implementation evidence and amendments to the Progress Log — never rewrite or
> delete earlier text.

## Status

`Proposed 2026-08-18`

`Accepted 2026-08-18`

All five clauses accepted by the owner. Clause 1 accepted with a strengthened
correctness obligation — see the Progress Log entry of the same date, which is
part of the decision and not commentary on it.

Refines ADR 0178 (repin+relock is one operation) and ADR 0155 (the pin sweep
ships as a single converging command) with what a full day of driving them
actually measured. Supersedes neither: both decisions were right, and this is
the cost they did not price. Extends ADR 0179 (a gate is only a gate if
something runs it) with its converse — a gate is only useful if its number
moves when the thing it measures moves.

## Context

On 2026-08-17 a two-line fix to a Python provenance checker, and a set of
workflow-YAML edits that changed no shipped code, together cost:

- **three** advances of the frozen fleet pin
  (`15fe252f` → `80a974e9` → `db845d4b`),
- **five** invocations of `integrate.py --apply` in the first cascade alone,
- a manual repin of the same three consumers each time (codec-lossless,
  firmware, visualization), because `repin_cross_repo.py` rewrites submodule
  URLs only and nothing moves the fleet pin by sweep,
- a relock of 35 Cargo workspaces per round,
- commits and pushes across up to 11 repositories per round,
- and **two** hard stops requiring the owner to run
  `git push --no-verify` by hand.

The third pin advance was caused by workflow YAML. Not one line of code that
any consumer compiles. Measured at the time: recording two submodule gitlinks
staled **27 manifests** (16 for abir, 11 for training/engine).

This is not a bug in any single tool. Every refusal in that sequence was
CORRECT. `integrate.py` was right to stop when duplicate-linked packages rose
from 2 to 3 — two copies of one crate version really are two distinct types to
rustc. The pre-push hook was right to refuse an unconverged fleet. The gates
that would not measure a drifted worktree were right to refuse. The system
behaved exactly as designed, and the design charges a fleet-wide integration
cost for changes that cannot possibly affect the fleet.

Three further costs surfaced in the same day, and they are worse than the first
because they produced WRONG ANSWERS rather than slow ones.

**Shell expansion silently did nothing.** `for R in $REPOS` does not word-split
in zsh. The loop that disabled GitHub Actions across 13 repositories ran once
with the entire list as a single string, 404'd, and disabled nothing. The
session was one step from running a 13-repository push cascade with CI live —
precisely the outcome the disable existed to prevent. It was caught only
because the disable was followed by a verification pass that re-read every
repository's state. The same footgun appeared three times in one day; a
separate instance of an interactive-aliased `cp` hung for ten minutes and left
a deliberately planted drift sitting in the working tree.

**A failing test named one of two defects.** ADR 0142's closure-hash test
reported `crates/lamquant-runtime/Cargo.toml`. Recomputing all 35 declared
hashes found a second file had drifted too. Fixing what the failure named would
have left the other in place, green, and wrong.

**A metric could not see its own largest improvement.** `check_ci_cost` read
workflow triggers only. Gating the 10x macOS lane from every-push to a weekly
sweep — the single biggest cost reduction available in the fleet — left its
count sitting at 2. The tool's own source already contains the principle it
violated: *"a number that does not move when the cost falls will not drive the
cost down."*

## Decision

Five clauses. Each is independently checkable, and each has a gate that fails
when the clause is violated.

### 1. A pin is stale only when the staleness changes the build

`check_cross_repo_pins.py` currently compares a manifest's `rev =` against the
recorded gitlink and reports any difference as a mismatch that blocks a push.
It will continue to REPORT every difference. It will only BLOCK when the
difference changes what cargo would compile.

The test is content, not identity: for a pin naming revision `A` where the
gitlink records `B`, compare `git rev-parse A:<crate-path>` with
`git rev-parse B:<crate-path>`. Equal subtree hashes mean cargo builds
byte-identical sources from either revision, and the pin is *behind* but not
*wrong*.

This is a refinement of the existing guarantee, not a relaxation of it. Commit
equality was always a proxy for content equality; this checks the thing the
proxy stood for. A pin whose crate subtree genuinely differs still blocks, as
it does today.

The provenance tension is real and is named here rather than hidden: ADR 0139's
evidence discipline wants a build traceable to a recorded commit, and a pin
allowed to lag makes that story two hops instead of one. The mitigation is that
the lag is reported on every run and the subtree hash that justifies it is
printed with it, so the trace is still one command long. If the owner judges
that insufficient, clause 1 is the one to drop — the other four stand alone.

### 2. Convergence is measured from the working tree, not the last commit

`integrate.py` resolves "integrated" from `git ls-tree HEAD`, so a round can
only ever see drift the previous META commit recorded. Its own help documents
this, and the consequence is that "no repinnable drift — converged" is
routinely a statement about a stale tree rather than a converged fleet. It was
emitted three times in one day while the fleet was demonstrably not converged.

The tool will read the index and worktree, so its verdict describes the fleet
as it is. A message that says "converged" when the operator can see uncommitted
gitlinks in `git status` trains the operator to disbelieve the tool, and a
convergence tool nobody believes is worse than none.

### 3. The cycle-break push is a mode of the tool, not a human escape hatch

The meta is both the integrator and a dependency of the things it integrates.
No repin ordering closes that cycle; breaking it requires publishing a meta
revision before the fleet agrees, which the pre-push hook correctly refuses.
The hook already documents the escape — `git push --no-verify` — which means
the project has accepted the step and made a human perform it.

`integrate.py` gains `--publish-cycle`: it performs that push itself, only when
the invariant the fleet pin exists to hold is satisfied at the revision being
pushed (the meta's own crate pins agree with its gitlinks), and records the
justification in the commit trailer. A documented, precondition-checked step
belongs in the tool. Leaving it to a human means the one action in the sequence
with no automated precondition check is the one performed by hand at the end of
a long cascade.

### 4. Automation does not rely on shell word-splitting or interactive aliases

Any loop over a list in a script uses an explicit array or a literal list,
never an unquoted scalar. `cp`, `mv` and `rm` in automation are invoked via
their absolute paths or a language runtime, never through an interactive shell
where an `-i` alias can turn a copy into a ten-minute hang.

This is a correctness rule, not a style preference. The failure mode is silent:
the loop runs once, the command errors on a nonsense argument, and the script
continues as though the work was done.

### 5. A gate reports every violation it can see, and its number moves

Two obligations, one principle.

A gate that can detect N violations reports N, not the first. A test that
asserts on one member of a set it could have enumerated is a test that hides
the rest.

A cost or debt metric must respond to the changes that actually move the cost.
Where a metric reads a proxy (a trigger, a filename, a count) rather than the
thing itself, and the proxy can stay fixed while the real quantity changes, the
metric is defective and is fixed rather than explained.

## Rationale

The unifying claim is that **the cost of landing a change should be
proportional to the blast radius of that change**, and that where a system
cannot tell a large change from a small one, it will charge every change the
large price.

The fleet currently cannot tell them apart. `pin == gitlink` is a single
equality standing in for a much richer question ("would a consumer build
differently?"), and because the proxy is coarse, a workflow comment and a
codec rewrite cost the same to integrate. Clause 1 replaces the proxy with the
question.

Clauses 2 and 3 are about trust in tooling. A tool that reports convergence
from stale data, and a procedure whose final step is a documented manual
override, both push the operator toward doing it by hand — which is how a
converging command becomes a five-round dance.

Clauses 4 and 5 are the cheapest and, by risk, the most valuable. The
integration tax cost hours. The silent shell expansion nearly cost a
13-repository CI spend that the owner had explicitly asked to avoid, and it was
caught by luck of process rather than by design.

## Consequences

**Good.** A docs-, workflow-, or test-only submodule change stops forcing a
fleet-wide repin. `integrate.py` becomes a command whose verdict can be
believed. The cycle-break stops interrupting the operator. Two recurring
classes of silent wrongness — unsplit shell variables, first-failure-only
reporting — get named and gated.

**Bad.** Clause 1 makes the pin story two hops for a lagging pin, which is real
provenance cost, mitigated but not eliminated by printing the justifying
subtree hash. Clause 3 puts a `--no-verify` push inside a tool, which is a
sharp edge however well guarded; its precondition check is therefore
load-bearing and must itself be tested against a revision that does NOT satisfy
the invariant.

**Unchanged.** Every existing refusal stays. Duplicate-linked packages still
block. A genuinely divergent crate subtree still blocks. The pre-push gate
still refuses an unconverged fleet for every reason it refuses one today.

## Gate

- `gate_cmd:` `python3 -m pytest -q tools/tests/test_check_cross_repo_pins.py tools/tests/test_integrate_layer_guard.py tools/tests/test_check_ci_cost_gating.py && python3 tools/scripts/check_cross_repo_pins.py && python3 tools/check_ci_cost.py && bash tools/scripts/lint_shell_expansion.sh`
- `pass when:` (a) a pin lagging a gitlink by a content-identical subtree is
  reported and does NOT block; (b) a pin whose subtree genuinely differs still
  blocks; (c) `integrate.py` reports drift that exists only in the index;
  (d) `--publish-cycle` refuses at a revision where the meta's crate pins
  disagree with its gitlinks; (e) no tracked script loops over an unquoted
  scalar; (f) `check_ci_cost` counts an expensive job as cheap only when its
  `if:` genuinely gates it to cheap events.

Each clause must be provable by a PLANTED violation, per
[[feedback_gates_must_be_able_to_fail]]: the pin case by a manufactured
divergent subtree, the shell case by a deliberately unquoted loop, the metric
case by deleting a job's `if:` line. A gate that has never been seen to fail
has not been shown to work.

## Reversal triggers

- Clause 1 lets a genuinely divergent dependency through to a build. Revert to
  strict commit equality immediately; the content check is an optimisation and
  correctness outranks it.
- `--publish-cycle` publishes a revision that does not satisfy the invariant.
  Remove the mode; the human step was the safer design.
- The clause-4 lint produces enough false positives that scripts start being
  written to appease it rather than to be correct.
- Any clause here is used to argue that an existing refusal should be relaxed.
  This ADR removes no refusal; a reading that says otherwise is a misreading.

## Related Decisions

- ADR 0178 — repin and relock as one operation; this prices it.
- ADR 0155 — the pin sweep as a single converging command; clause 2 is what
  makes "single" true.
- ADR 0179 — a gate is only a gate if something runs it; clause 5 is its
  converse.
- ADR 0139 — evidence and managed dependency edges; the provenance counterparty
  to clause 1.
- ADR 0152 — fail-closed campaign; its reversal trigger (relaxing a gate to
  make a lane pass) governs this ADR too.

## Progress Log  *(append-only; newest last)*

- _2026-08-18 — proposed, from measurement rather than from theory._ The costs
  in Context are all observed on 2026-08-17: three fleet-pin advances, five
  `integrate.py` runs in one cascade, 27 manifests staled by two gitlinks, two
  owner-run `--no-verify` pushes, one silent 13-repository no-op from an
  unsplit shell variable, one two-defect drift reported as one, and one cost
  metric that did not move when the largest cost in the fleet was removed.
  Nothing here is implemented yet; the gate above describes the finished state,
  and this entry is the record that it does not hold today.

- _2026-08-18 — accepted, and clause 1 hardened, because the obvious
  implementation is UNSOUND._ The owner accepted all five clauses with one
  condition on clause 1: it must block whenever the revisions are legitimately
  divergent, without fail. Measuring against that condition immediately killed
  the naive reading — "compare the crate's own directory" — which this ADR was
  careless to leave implicit. Counted in the fleet the same day:

  - **15** manifests inherit from a workspace root (`workspace = true`), so the
    ROOT manifest's `[workspace.package]` and `[workspace.dependencies]` are
    inputs to a crate whose own directory did not change;
  - **55** manifests declare a path dependency escaping their directory —
    `blut-semantic` path-depends on `../..`, the entire engine root;
  - **18** crates ship a `build.rs`, which may read any file in the checkout
    and cannot be reasoned about statically.

  Clause 1 therefore compares a BUILD CLOSURE, not a directory. For package P
  at revision R the closure is: P's manifest directory, plus the workspace root
  manifest when P inherits from it, plus — transitively — the closure of every
  path dependency, plus any `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` target that escapes
  it. Two revisions are BEHIND (report, do not block) only when every tree in
  the closure is identical.

  The asymmetry is the whole point and is stated here so no future change can
  quietly invert it. A false "divergent" costs one unnecessary cascade — the
  status quo, which is merely expensive. A false "identical" ships a build from
  sources nobody reviewed. The check is therefore permitted to be INCOMPLETE
  but never UNSOUND, and every undecidable case blocks:

  - anything in the closure differs → DIVERGENT, block;
  - a `build.rs` anywhere in the closure, AND any difference at all between the
    two revisions outside the closure → UNDECIDABLE, block. A build script's
    inputs are not statically knowable, so identical closures do not prove
    identical output. This is deliberately conservative and will block real
    cases; that is the correct direction to be wrong in;
  - a path dependency resolving outside the repository, or a manifest that will
    not parse → UNDECIDABLE, block.

  Two things explicitly do NOT enter the closure, recorded so they are not
  "fixed" back in later: the dependency's own `Cargo.lock` (a git dependency is
  resolved by the CONSUMER's lock) and the dependency's `.cargo/config.toml`
  and `[profile]` tables (the consumer's govern). Including them would produce
  false divergence, not false identity, so the error would be expensive rather
  than dangerous — but it would still be wrong.

  Clause 1 does not ship until a planted divergence in EACH of these blocks:
  a crate source file · the crate manifest · an inherited
  `[workspace.package]` field · an inherited `[workspace.dependencies]` entry ·
  a path dependency outside the crate directory · a file read by a `build.rs`.
  Six plants, six blocks, per [[feedback_gates_must_be_able_to_fail]]. Until
  every one is demonstrated, `check_cross_repo_pins.py` keeps blocking on plain
  commit inequality exactly as it does today.

## Validation  *(ongoing)*

Watch for: a submodule change that is genuinely docs-only still triggering a
repin (clause 1 not reaching far enough); `integrate.py` needing more than one
round on a converged tree (clause 2 incomplete); any operator running
`--no-verify` by hand after clause 3 lands (the mode's preconditions are too
strict, or the cycle has a second shape not yet modelled).

legacy_gates.command: python3 -m pytest -q tools/tests/test_check_cross_repo_pins.py tools/tests/test_integrate_layer_guard.py tools/tests/test_check_ci_cost_gating.py && python3 tools/scripts/check_cross_repo_pins.py && python3 tools/check_ci_cost.py && bash tools/scripts/lint_shell_expansion.sh
